articles.title: Kiteworks Fixes Critical Flaw Found During Nine-Hour Precautionary Shutdown
articles.text:
Kiteworks on Monday said it worked with federal intelligence authorities over the weekend as it identified and addressed a critical security vulnerability during the scheduled precautionary shutdown.
"During the shutdown, this activity led to the discovery of a previously unknown critical vulnerability confined to a capability that is enabled for less than 1% of the customer base," the company said in a statement. "Kiteworks developed and deployed a fix during the window, [and] applied an additional protective layer across all environments."
There is no evidence that the vulnerability has ever been exploited in a malicious context. Other Kiteworks products are not affected by the flaw.
The development comes days after Kiteworks, previously Accellion, urged customers to take their systems offline for a period of nine hours, in addition to shutting down environments it hosts on behalf of customers, after receiving intelligence about a potential imminent cyber attack.
The company stressed that the action was more preventative than a reaction to a confirmed breach of its systems. On September 27, 2026, the shutdown recommendation was lifted.
Kiteworks has not disclosed any specifics about the nature of the flaw, and how it could be exploited. It does not have a Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifier as of writing. The Hacker News has contacted the company if it plans to release a public advisory about the flaw and assign it a CVE ID for easier tracking.
"Telling customers to take production systems offline is not a decision any vendor makes lightly, and we knew exactly what we were asking of them," Kiteworks CISO Frank Balonis said.
"We made it anyway, because when the choice is between certainty and convenience, customer data is not something we are willing to gamble with. That decision is what made the rest possible. We would make the same call again tomorrow to protect our customers' data."
Now that the threat window has passed and no anomalies were observed, customers are recommended to bring their Kiteworks system back online.

articles.title: Microsoft actualiza Windows 11 con un menú de inicio personalizable, más funciones de IA y de seguridad
articles.text:
Microsoft ha comenzado a distribuir Windows 11 26H2, una actualización que incorpora cambios en la personalización del menú de inicio, la barra de tareas y las herramientas de búsqueda, además de nuevas funciones de inteligencia artificial y seguridad. La nueva versión también busca facilitar el acceso a las opciones del sistema y reducir las interrupciones durante la instalación de actualizaciones.
A diferencia de otras versiones del sistema operativo, Windows 11 26H2 no requiere una reinstalación completa en los equipos compatibles con las ediciones 24H2 y 25H2.
PUBLICIDAD
Microsoft utiliza un paquete de habilitación que activa funciones previamente incorporadas mediante actualizaciones mensuales, por lo que el proceso de instalación debería ser más rápido.
Windows 11 26H2 incorpora un menú de inicio más personalizable
Una de las principales novedades de Windows 11 26H2 está en el menú de inicio, que ahora ofrece más opciones para adaptar su apariencia y organización a las preferencias de cada usuario.
La actualización permite elegir distintos tamaños y ocultar secciones como las aplicaciones ancladas, los elementos recientes y la lista completa de programas. También es posible esconder el nombre y la fotografía de la cuenta del usuario, lo que ofrece una interfaz más sencilla y con menos elementos visibles.
PUBLICIDAD
La barra de tareas también recibe nuevas opciones de personalización. Ahora puede colocarse en la parte superior, inferior, izquierda o derecha de la pantalla. Además, incorpora un tamaño compacto que permite aprovechar mejor el espacio disponible, especialmente en equipos con pantallas pequeñas.
Por su parte, Windows Search, el buscador integrado del sistema operativo, presenta mejoras en la organización de los resultados y el indexado de las carpetas utilizadas habitualmente. También ofrece controles adicionales para gestionar las sugerencias procedentes de la web y Microsoft Store.
La inteligencia artificial gana presencia en Windows 11
Microsoft también ha ampliado la integración de la inteligencia artificial en Windows 11. Una de las novedades se encuentra en Configuración, donde se incorpora un agente capaz de localizar y modificar determinados ajustes mediante instrucciones escritas en lenguaje natural.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta herramienta busca facilitar el acceso a las opciones del sistema sin que el usuario tenga que recorrer distintos menús. En lugar de buscar manualmente una configuración, podrá describir lo que necesita para que el agente le ayude a encontrarla o modificarla.
El Administrador de tareas también recibe nuevas funciones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial. Entre ellas, ofrece información adicional sobre las cargas de trabajo de IA y la actividad de la unidad de procesamiento neuronal (NPU), un componente especializado en ejecutar este tipo de operaciones.
No obstante, algunas de estas herramientas dependen del hardware del ordenador y del mercado en el que se encuentre el usuario, por lo que no estarán disponibles en todos los equipos.
PUBLICIDAD
Más seguridad y control sobre las actualizaciones
La actualización también introduce mejoras destinadas a reforzar la protección del sistema. Una de las más importantes es Administrator Protection, una función que limita los privilegios elevados a los momentos en que realmente se necesitan.
Esta herramienta permite autorizar determinadas acciones administrativas mediante Windows Hello, el sistema de autenticación biométrica de Microsoft. El objetivo es reducir la exposición permanente de los permisos que podrían aprovecharse para realizar cambios no autorizados.
Windows Update también incorpora ajustes para facilitar la gestión de las actualizaciones y reducir los reinicios innecesarios. La nueva versión permite identificar con mayor claridad las descargas disponibles y busca evitar que las instalaciones interrumpan las actividades del usuario.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, hay mejoras en el Explorador de archivos, Narrador y Acceso por voz, así como una mayor compatibilidad con lectores de huellas, audio compartido mediante Bluetooth y el uso simultáneo de la cámara desde varias aplicaciones.
Cómo instalar Windows 11 26H2
Microsoft ha iniciado el despliegue gradual de Windows 11 26H2 para los equipos compatibles con las versiones 24H2 y 25H2. Para comprobar si está disponible, hay que ingresar en Configuración, seleccionar Windows Update y activar la opción “Obtener las últimas actualizaciones en cuanto estén disponibles”.
La actualización no aparecerá necesariamente al mismo tiempo en todos los ordenadores. Microsoft puede aplicar bloqueos temporales cuando detecta problemas de compatibilidad con determinados dispositivos o programas.
PUBLICIDAD
En los equipos que ya utilizan Windows 11 25H2, el cambio será similar a la instalación de una actualización mensual, ya que ambas versiones comparten la misma base de código. Sin embargo, 26H2 también marca el inicio de un nuevo ciclo de soporte: 24 meses para las ediciones Home y Pro, y 36 meses para Enterprise y Education.
De esta manera, Microsoft concentra sus novedades en la personalización, la inteligencia artificial y la seguridad, sin introducir una renovación completa de la plataforma.
PUBLICIDAD

Suas fotos podem “desaparecer”: Samsung encerra integração com Microsoft
Fotografias salvas na nuvem não ficarão mais disponíveis na galeria, mas podem ser baixadas no app da Microsoft.
Os usuários de celular Samsung devem notar, a partir de hoje (30/09), o fim da integração do Galaxy com o OneDrive, serviço de nuvem da Microsoft. Isso significa que todas as fotografias armazenadas no serviço digital vão “desaparecer” da galeria nativa da Samsung, segundo um comunicado da própria Microsoft.
Para não perder suas fotos e vídeos no celular Galaxy, é necessário baixar as fotos manualmente na galeria até o fim do dia, segundo a Samsung australiana. Todo o conteúdo já sincronizado com o Microsoft OneDrive seguirá disponível na nuvem da Microsoft, mas será necessário baixar o app oficial para acessá-lo.
Os adeptos do OneDrive ainda poderão fazer o backup das fotos, mas será necessário instalar o app dedicado a isso, que está disponível na Google Play Store. É necessário ativar a função de backup de câmera, de modo que as fotografias feitas com o smartphone sejam enviadas automaticamente para a nuvem.
O passo a passo é o seguinte:
Se você foi pego de surpresa, provavelmente suas fotos já não estão mais disponíveis na galeria. A boa notícia é que elas não foram deletadas, mas sim retiradas do app da Samsung. Para acessá-las, basta usar o app Microsoft OneDrive no celular.

articles.title: I tested Logitech’s new mechanical keyboard, and its a stern rival to Razer boards — and one clever feature sets it apart
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Logitech G316 X is a competent mechanical keyboard with a premium feel and solid-feeling, satisfying switches. There’s a decent selection of input customizations, too, although none that actually impact performance. The integrated screen is also rather useless. However, these negatives aren’t too damaging, considering the G316 X is better value than many other premium equivalents.
Reasons to buy
- +Solid, satisfying tactile switches
- +Great build quality
- +Good customization software
Reasons to avoid
- -Wired only
- -Lacks some useful keys
- -Screen a little pointless
Why you can trust TechRadar
Logitech G316 X 98: One-minute review
The G316 X is Logitech’s new gaming keyboard, featuring mechanical switches and an integrated display for good measure.
In typical Logitech fashion the G316 X sports a minimalist appearance, available in monotone colorways (black or white), and free of unnecessary details or angles. The vibrant RGB backlighting is a nice touch, though, as is the thin LED strip at the top.
These smart looks are complimented by exceptional build quality. The chassis is solid yet light, while the PBT keycaps feel great thanks to their subtle texturing and sturdy fit, putting the G316 X's construction up there with the best gaming keyboards.
Also worth highlighting are the adjustable feet. Rather than plastic flaps that fold out, the G316 X enlists soft rubber blocks that you remove and turn over when you want to adjust the tilt angle from four to eight degrees. The integrated screen, however, is a letdown. It may look good, but it's small and displays no real information.
Thankfully, G HUB — the software used for customizing the G316 X — is more useful. There are numerous assignments available, including the ability to map up to five inputs to a single key. There are also three different mapping layers for you to play around with.
Thanks to its stock tactile switches, I enjoyed gaming with the G316 X. Their solid, thocky response imparts plenty of feedback, yet they're still snappy enough to feel quick. They’re damped enough to remove harshness from impact, but they’re not the quietest switches around.
In addition to gaming, I also found the G316 X great for typing. My one small complaint is that the feet don’t tilt the board quite enough for my liking. Nevertheless, I still found it sufficiently comfortable to use without a wrist-rest — not something I can say about every gaming keyboard.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The G316 X isn’t the most affordable mechanical keyboard around, but it's cheaper than some of its key rivals. It’s a shame its screen is merely a gimmick and it lacks wireless connectivity, but the G316 X is still a strong choice for those after a solid-feeling experience.
Logitech G316 X 98 review: Price & availability
- $119.99 / £109.99 / AU$199.95
- Available now in black or white
- Cheaper than some rivals
The G316 X costs $119.99 / £109.99 / AU$199.95 and is available now. It comes preinstalled with tactile switches, although these are hot-swappable. There are two colorways to choose from: black or white.
It's quite expensive for a wired mechanical keyboard, although cheaper than those from other premium brands. For instance, it comes in lower than the HyperX Origins 2 1800, and a lot less than the Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75% — the latter is one of the best-made and best-performing examples in the sector, though.
In today’s marketplace, however, there are more budget-friendly gaming keyboards available. The MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra, for example, offers multiple wireless connectivity options, but also analog switches that feel great and offer plenty of tweakability.
Logitech G316 X 98 review: Specs
| Layout | 98% | 
| Switch | Mechanical (Tactile) | 
| Programmable keys | Yes | 
| Dimensions | 15.1 x 5.5 x 1.6 inches (384 x 140 x 40mm) | 
| RGB or backlighting | Yes (customizable) | 
Logitech G316 X 98 review: Design and features
- Minimalist looks with bright RGB
- Premium-feeling materials and build
- Practical adjustable feet
The G316 X has a retro-modern look, sporting an ultra-square form and minimalist design. There aren’t any odd angles or contours that sometimes blight gaming peripherals; the only flourishes here are a translucent green Escape key and volume wheel, and an LED strip between the number and F rows.
These are actually quite attractive, as is the bright customizable RGB backlighting against the white option of the keyboard, in particular.
Although the G316 X is made of plastic, it’s one of the best around. It’s solid yet light — the ideal combination. The PBT keycaps help lend the board a premium feel, featuring a subtle texture that makes them satisfying to touch.
Like many gaming keyboards, the G316 X comes with adjustable feet, but they’re not of your typical fold-out type. Instead, they’re rubber blocks that you have to remove and flip over to switch the tilt angle from four to eight degrees.
This may appear a less elegant solution at first, but it’s actually rather clever. The static design provides greater stability, so there’s no danger of the blocks closing in when moving the board around. Also, their large surface area and rubber material delivers a better grip.
Ironically, it’s the integrated LED screen that turns out to be the least sophisticated aspect of the G316 X. It may look sharp, but it’s seriously lacking in functionality, merely displaying a few basic animations when adjusting the volume or or playing back media — none of which are helpful.
The 98% layout is compact yet practical, even including a dedicated number pad, although there are a few navigation keys absent that I would’ve liked to see remain. There aren’t many default Fn shortcuts labelled on the keys, either.
Thankfully, you can make your own shortcuts using Logitech’s G HUB peripheral software. There are plenty of assignments available here, and three different layers in which to arrange them. There’s even the ability to assign up to five inputs to a single key.
You can also customize the Game Mode button next to the aforementioned screen in order for it to disable more keys beyond the Windows key. However, you won’t find many performance-based settings to play with, beyond the ability to adjust the polling rate, which has a maximum value of 8KHz.
Logitech G316 X 98 review: Performance
- Excellent feedback from tactile switches
- Great for gaming and typing
- Tilt angle is limited
The standout aspect of the G316 X is its stock tactile switches. I found they provided plenty of feedback, actuating with a solid and noticeable thock, yet they still able to rebound quickly, making them feel snappy. There’s just enough dampening to prevent presses feeling harsh, but relative to many other gaming keyboards, it’s minimal. This means the G316 X can be quite loud when you’re hammering away.
I found the board comfortable when gaming with the WASD keys. This is thanks to the adjustable feet, which make up for the lack of wrist support and reasonably thick base. However, I wish they tilted the layout a little further for optimum comfort: I often hit the back edge of the spacebar, although its curved design made this less of an issue than it might have been been otherwise. It also seems like it’s damped to a greater degree than the other keys, which makes it all the more gratifying to press.
The spacing between the keycaps is ideal: they’re not so close that you’ll hit the wrong key, nor so far apart that reaching them is a stretch. I also found them surprisingly easy to type on, despite their relative tallness. Not only does the aforementioned tilt angle mitigate their height, but their prominent indentations guide your fingers to the correct key, helping to prevent typos.
Should I buy the Logitech G316 X 98?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | Not cheap, but compared to other upmarket rivals, the price is reasonable. | 4 / 5 | 
| Design and features | Solid yet light, and the double-sided feet are clever. It’s a shame about the lack of navigation keys and shortcut labelling, though. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | The tactile switches are satisfyingly solid and provide plenty of feedback, although I wish there was slightly more of a tilt angle for maximum comfort. | 4 / 5 | 
| Overall | The G316 X is a fantastically thocky mechanical keyboard that's comfortable enough to just about get away with no wrist support. | 4 / 5 | 
Buy the Logitech G316 X 98 if…
You want solid switches
The stock tactile switches provide plenty of feedback and pleasing resistance, yet are still snappy enough to compete.
You want solid feet
The rubber blocks underneath are stable and grippy, and can be flipped over to adjust the tilt angle.
Don't buy it if…
You want an interactive screen
The one here serves little purpose, while others feature settings menus and display useful game-related information.
You want the best value possible
Although the G316 X is well priced compared to other premium models, there are numerous gaming keyboards — mechanical and otherwise — that offer greater features for a lower price.
Logitech G316 X 98 review: Also consider
HyperX Origins 2 1800 
The HyperX Origins 2 1800 is another wired gaming keyboard with mechanical switches and hot-swappable hardware, but it's slightly less expensive than the G316 X. It still has a premium build and great performance, though. However, its customization software is less involved, and I didn’t find its stock keycaps very amenable to typing.
Read our full HyperX Origins 2 1800 review.
MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra
If you want great value, the FUN60 Ultra is a fine choice. Its analog switches feel superb and offer plenty of scope for customization and tweaking. And to cap it all off, the whole board is surprisingly well made, too.
Read our full MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra review.
How I tested the Logitech G316 X 98
- Tested for a few days
- Used for various tasks besides gaming
- Plenty of gaming keyboard experience
I tested the G316 X for a few days, during which time I used it not only for gaming, but also for typing and web browsing.
I played Counter-Strike 2, which is great test of a peripheral’s accuracy and responsiveness, as well as S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl, which makes wider use of keys beyond those in the WASD area, helping to test the ease of access and comfort in reaching such keys.
I’ve been PC gaming for over a decade, and have used many different keyboards in that time. I also have a wealth of experience reviewing them, from budget models to state-of-the-art offerings from esteemed brands.
- First reviewed: September 2026
- Read more about how we test
Lewis Maddison is a Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He previously worked as a Staff Writer for our business section, TechRadar Pro, where he gained experience with productivity-enhancing hardware, ranging from keyboards to standing desks. His area of expertise lies in computer peripherals and audio hardware, having spent over a decade exploring the murky depths of both PC building and music production. He also revels in picking up on the finest details and niggles that ultimately make a big difference to the user experience.

articles.title: Brosse à dents Dyson à 479€ : on sait enfin ce qui a provoqué le couac industriel
articles.text:
Retirée de la vente en France dix jours seulement après son lancement, une partie des CameraJet souffre d’un défaut de fabrication pouvant laisser passer de l’eau dans l’appareil. Dyson dit avoir identifié le problème, mais doit désormais rassurer les premiers acheteurs.
Dix jours auront suffi pour transformer un lancement surmédiatisé en sérieux couac industriel. Présentée le 1er septembre à 479 euros, la brosse à dents connectée Dyson CameraJet a vu sa commercialisation suspendue en France dès le 11 septembre. Après avoir évoqué des tensions sur les stocks, la marque avait fini par reconnaître l’existence d’un composant défectueux. Elle précise désormais l’origine du problème.
Une fuite provoquée par un défaut de fabrication
Dans une déclaration transmise à Allure, Dyson met en cause un lot de production de tubes utilisés par le jet interdentaire. Un problème survenu lors de leur fabrication aurait créé un risque d’infiltration d’eau susceptible d’altérer le fonctionnement de certains appareils.
La marque affirme avoir isolé les produits concernés, repris la production à plein régime et commencé à expédier des appareils à ses distributeurs. Elle ne donne toutefois aucune date précise pour leur retour en rayon en France.
Sauf qu'on ne comprend pas comment un problème aussi gênant a pu passer entre les mailles du contrôle qualité. Kyle Wiens, patron d’iFixit, avançait auparavant auprès de Wired plusieurs scénarios possibles, notamment des pièces mal ajustées ou une colle ayant mal polymérisé.
Dans ce dernier cas, un produit peut parfaitement fonctionner au moment des tests, puis se dégrader sous l’effet de la chaleur ou de l’humidité pendant le transport. Dyson n’a toutefois pas confirmé l’une ou l’autre de ces hypothèses.
Des premiers acheteurs à rassurer
Plusieurs propriétaires ont signalé de l’eau à proximité de la batterie, des messages de surchauffe ou des appareils devenus inutilisables peu après leur achat. Ces témoignages ne permettent pas de mesurer l’ampleur exacte du problème et Dyson indique qu’aucun rappel général n’est organisé à ce stade, même si certains confrères ont été surpris de voir le géant anglais récupérer leurs exemplaires de test.
Dans ce genre de situation, en cas de fuite ou d’alerte de température, le plus prudent reste évidemment de cesser d’utiliser la CameraJet et de ne pas la remettre en charge avant d’avoir contacté le vendeur ou le SAV Dyson. Mieux vaut également conserver sa preuve d’achat et le numéro de série de l’appareil.
Des consignes de reprise et de remboursement ont circulé chez certains distributeurs, mais leurs modalités peuvent varier. Pour un appareil acheté directement auprès de Dyson, la marque demande de contacter son service consommateurs.
Pour Dyson, l’affaire tombe particulièrement mal. La CameraJet devait marquer son arrivée spectaculaire dans l’hygiène dentaire après six années de développement et 38 brevets déposés. Si aucun blessé ne semble avoir été signalé à ce stade, voir un produit à 479 euros disparaître des rayons dix jours après son lancement ressemble tout de même à un sérieux crash industriel.

articles.title: OpenAI planea recibir USD 30.000 millones de inversores: la empresa costaría 1,4 billones de dólares
articles.text:
OpenAI negocia con inversores una nueva ronda de financiamiento de al menos USD 30.000 millones que llevaría su valuación a unos 1,4 billones de dólares, informó Bloomberg.
Según la agencia, las negociaciones se encuentran en una etapa temprana y podrían cambiar. De concretarse, la ronda funcionaría como un puente de capital privado en lugar de la salida a bolsa que la empresa había contemplado para este año, pero que finalmente no se concretó y por ahora no tiene fecha establecida.
PUBLICIDAD
La cifra representaría un salto respecto de la última ronda conocida de la compañía: en marzo, OpenAI recaudó 122.000 millones de dólares en una operación que la valuó en 852.000 millones, con Amazon, Nvidia y SoftBank como principales inversores y Microsoft también participando.
Cómo sería el salto en los ingresos de OpenAI
El ingreso anualizado de OpenAI superó los 40.000 millones de dólares en agosto, un salto del 70% desde julio, según había reportado Bloomberg semanas atrás. La cifra es una proyección basada en el ritmo de ventas de un período determinado, no una medición directa de ingresos anuales ya facturados.
De cerrarse en los términos actuales, la nueva valuación volvería a ubicar a OpenAI por encima de Anthropic, su principal competidora, que había superado momentáneamente a la compañía de Sam Altman a comienzos de año en el mercado privado.
PUBLICIDAD
La ronda llega después de que Altman descartara una salida a bolsa durante 2026 para priorizar la seguridad de sus modelos. “Creo que es inaceptable estar tomando algo así como un 10% de posibilidades de matar a todos para fines de la década”, dijo el ejecutivo a la revista Fortune, en referencia a las advertencias de otros actores del sector sobre los riesgos de la inteligencia artificial avanzada.
OpenAI frena el desarrollo de su IA
Esta semana, OpenAI anunció que no lanzará GPT-6.1 Astra, la versión más avanzada de su modelo insignia, después de determinar que el sistema mostraba una disposición alta a engañar a los usuarios sobre sus propias acciones. En su lugar, la empresa presentó una versión más económica llamada Sol.
PUBLICIDAD
Altman también respaldó una propuesta del director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, para frenar el desarrollo de los modelos más avanzados de IA e incorporar evaluadores externos que auditen su seguridad.
La directora financiera de OpenAI, Sarah Friar, había advertido puertas adentro que un crecimiento de ingresos más lento podría dejar a la empresa sin capacidad para cumplir sus contratos futuros de cómputo, según informó The Wall Street Journal. Friar también planteó dudas sobre si la compañía estaba en condiciones de cumplir con los requisitos regulatorios del mercado bursátil en los plazos que prefería Altman.
La presión regulatoria se suma a una serie de incidentes con agentes de IA de la empresa, entre ellos episodios vinculados a la plataforma Hugging Face y a un sitio web del gobierno de Australia, que OpenAI todavía investiga.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué viene ahora para la empresa de ChatGPT
El anuncio de la ronda coincidió con la jornada de DevDay, la conferencia anual para desarrolladores de OpenAI, donde la empresa presentó Dots, un asistente que ejecuta tareas de forma autónoma a través de aplicaciones como Slack y Teams con supervisión limitada.
Según Bloomberg, la compañía también recortó algunos límites de uso disponibles para los suscriptores de su plan de 200 dólares mensuales, en medio del esfuerzo por sostener el ritmo de gastos que exige la expansión de su infraestructura.
Las fuentes consultadas por la agencia insistieron en que ningún monto ni la estructura final de la ronda están cerrados, y que el resultado dependerá de cómo avancen las conversaciones con los inversores en las próximas semanas.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: 101 Malicious npm Packages Add Developers' WhatsApp Accounts to Groups Without Consent
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have identified a cluster of 101 npm packages that are used to trap developers into a WhatsApp group subscriber campaign dubbed PhantomSub.
"The malicious packages abuse the 'Baileys' WhatsApp open source project to add the victims to groups without their consent," OX Security researchers Nir Zadok, Moshe Siman Tov Bustan, and Vitalii Chepurko said in a technical write-up published Monday.
These packages have been collectively downloaded 490,000 times, out of which 116,000 occurred in the last 30 days. The names of some of the packages are below -
- ourin-baileys
- @nexustechpro/baileys
- @badzz88/baileys
- @ostyado/baileys
- levvleys
- @vanzxy/baileys
- @yudzxml/baileys
- @chatunity/baileys
- @kelvdra/baileys
- neuralwhatsapp
- lilys-baileys
- @fyxzpediaa/baileys
- noxleyss
- @xrelly-stack/bails
- alipclutch-baileys
- kurobails
- eliteprotech-baileys
- @xayz/baileys
- chromestaff-baileys
- @sanzoffc/baileys
- @sairidev/baileys-new
- cloud-baileys
- @nyzzpediaa/baileys-new
- ishumdz-bail
- nishiki-bail
- diezyclutch-baileys
- oktz-baileys
- my-auto-follow
Details of the activity first emerged in August 2026, when SafeDep said it identified a set of Baileys npm forks that were found to engage in malicious behaviors, such as stealthily making the installer's WhatsApp account follow channels the package author controls and injecting the author's advertising URL into every image and video the bot sends.
Then, earlier this month, the Xygeni Security Research Team disclosed details of another Baileys mod named "@dappaoffc/baileys-mod" that was also found to subscribe the developer's authenticated WhatsApp bot session to attacker-controlled newsletter channels.
OX Security's analysis has uncovered three different variants of the malware, each implementing different ways of handling the subscription routine -
- Variant 1 (19 packages), which fetches channel IDs from GitHub at runtime
- Variant 2 (60 packages), which embeds channel IDs in its source code in cleartext
- Variant 3 (14 packages), which embeds channel IDs in its source code in encoded and obfuscated form
One of the WhatsApp groups is assessed to be based in Indonesia and advertises accounts for mobile games and applications, such as Mobile Legends: Bang Bang and TikTok. These posts also specify a phone number that's linked to an Indonesian business WhatsApp account named "Dan."
Some of the other identified groups and channels are listed below -
- Neural (798 followers), which markets Resource Supplies (RSS) sales using JualanRSS, an online marketplace that sells in-game resources such as food, ore, stone, timber, and gold.
- MONTE – BMG (1,000 followers)
- CORTANA TECH (1,300 followers)
- Fyxzpedia.ID – Utama (4,800 followers)
"The channels we could identify are mostly small bot-seller and 'market' channels, largely Indonesian, where follower counts serve as social proof for selling bot scripts, bot-building services, 'premium' APKs and social-media boosting," OX Security said.
"Many packages in this campaign are not independent. The same channel IDs, the same remote channel lists, and the same GitHub accounts appear across packages with different names and publishers. A shared channel means a shared beneficiary: whoever owns the channel collects followers from every package that targets it, whoever published the package."
Developers are advised to check if they have been added to the WhatsApp groups, block them, configure detection rules for blocking the malicious npm Baileys packages, and refrain from using packages that require the personal WhatsApp account to be connected.

articles.title: Apple CEO John Ternus Reportedly Plans Faster Product Launches and a Leaner Company
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Apple CEO John Ternus Reportedly Plans Faster Product Launches and a Leaner Company
New Apple CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1, is reportedly planning an overhaul aimed at faster launches and a leaner company, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Ternus, previously Apple's hardware engineering chief, has apparently discussed moving away from the usual spring and fall launch windows and wants the company to be more experimental. Product teams are said to be pushing out more devices on shorter timelines, and one person familiar with the situation described the mood inside as hectic. Moreover, the cuts have already started. 
Apple has reportedly dismissed a number of engineering program managers in hardware engineering over the past two weeks, including roughly half a dozen directors. Some affected staff were given a limited window to find other roles inside Apple, and those who don't will apparently be let go later this year. Apple also reportedly considered cutting about 5,000 AppleCare jobs this summer while looking at AI support agents, but dropped that plan. It's unclear how this affects the October launches rumored for the OLED iPad mini, HomePod mini 2, and Apple TV 4K. Employees reportedly expect more job cuts in the coming months, and they caution that changing how Apple builds products could take years.

articles.title: It comes with a mighty price tag, but the Razer Blade 16 (2026) is exceptional in almost every way
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Razer's latest Blade 16 packs some of the most impressive portable hardware money can buy in a slim-line form factor, and it still delivers performance in a way not seen before. Its crisp OLED display and outstanding aesthetics back are particular highlights, and it's honestly only let down by an extraordinary price tag, and the lack of an Ethernet port.
Reasons to buy
- +RTX 5090 delivers exceptional performance
- +Stunningly clean aesthetic design
- +Impressive battery life given the spec
- +Crisp, punchy, OLED display
Reasons to avoid
- -No Ethernet port on a gaming laptop
- -Very high price
Why you can trust TechRadar
Razer Blade 16 (2026) two-minute review
Razer's latest Blade 16, is by far, one of the best gaming laptops I've ever tested. The spec on this thing is off the charts. It's got an Nvidia RTX 5090, with 175W of juice behind it, an Intel Core Ultra 9 386H, and no less than 32GB of LPDDR5X RAM running along at an outstandingly zippy 9,600 MT/s.
Razer's crammed all of that performance into a form factor that puts Dell's thin and light XPS line to the sword, and it still manages to keep thermals in check, and ensures power delivery is on point as well.
Speaking of design, this thing is stunningly clean. Razer's taken the humble laptop form factor and made it its own. It's simple, elegant, and sleek in almost every area.
From the keyboard to the trackpad, to the ports, it just oozes premium. It's got an RGB keyboard, of course, and (surprisingly) that green Razer logo etched and illuminated on the back (perhaps the only thing that's a little underwhelming), but aside from that, there's little here to indicate that it's a gaming laptop.
The screen lives up to the rest of the spec; it's a gorgeous 2560 x 1600 OLED offering, spitting out a staggering 240 Hz too, with inky deep blacks. It's hard to fault, and paired with that GPU, there are few games here that don't hold up in their ultra presets. Cyberpunk 2077 and Total War: Warhammer 3 both pulled framerates well into the hundreds.
The only two negatives are the lack of an Ethernet port and the fact it has a price tag so large that you could almost use it as a down payment on a house.
Razer Blade 16 (2026) review: Price and availability
- Available globally now
- Insane price tag for the spec, paying for design
- Soldered RAM so choose memory up front
You can pick up your very own Blade 16 right now, no matter where you are on the planet. Prices start at $3,499 US, £3,499 and AU$5,999 for the base spec.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
That stock model isn't entirely different from our review unit either (genuinely a nice thing to see), the only downgrades come in the form of the SSD, dropping from a 2TB unit, to a 1TB model, and the GPU choice, with the base version featuring an RTX 5070 Ti, instead of our juiced up 5090.
You can also upgrade to an RTX 5080 if you so desire, and there's an option to bump up to 64GB of RAM as well if your bank account can stretch that far in the AI age.
It's also worth noting, demand is quite high (or supply low), so depending where you are in the world, you might see a lot of these units on pre-order, or out of stock (amazingly given the price tag).
It's worth noting you can swap the SSD out, if you're handy with a torx screwdriver.
Razer Blade 16 (2026) review: Specs
|   | Base  | Review  | 
|---|---|---|
| Price  | $3,499.99 / £3,499.99 / AU$5,999.95  | $4,899.99 / £4,799.99 / AU$8,399.95  | 
| CPU  | Intel Core Ultra 9 386H (4.9 GHz, 16 Cores)  | Intel Core Ultra 9 386H (4.9 GHz, 16 Cores)  | 
| GPU  | Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti  | Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090  | 
| RAM  | 32GB LPDDR5X  | 32GB LPDDR5X  | 
| Storage  | 1TB M.2 NVMe PCIe 4.0 SSD  | 2TB M.2 NVMe PCIe 4.0 SSD  | 
| Display  | 16-inch OLED (2560 x 1600), 16:10, 240Hz  | 16-inch OLED (2560 x 1600), 16:10, 240Hz  | 
| Ports and Connectivity  | 1x Thunderbolt 5, 1x Thunderbolt 4, SD Card Reader, 3x USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, 1x HDMI 2.1, 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack, WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 | 1x Thunderbolt 5, 1x Thunderbolt 4, SD Card Reader, 3x USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, 1x HDMI 2.1, 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack, WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 | 
| Battery  | 90Whr | 90Whr | 
| Dimensions  | 355 x 250.5 x 17.4mm (14.0 x 9.9 x 0.6in)  | 355 x 250.5 x 17.4mm (14.0 x 9.9 x 0.6in)  | 
| Weight  | 4.71lbs (2.14kg)  | 4.71lbs (2.14kg)  | 
Razer Blade 16 (2026) review: Design
- Clean, premium aesthetic and feel
- Impressively thin and light
- Lacks an Ethernet port
I've tested a lot of "premium" laptops over the last 11 years of my career, and the result is almost always a mixed bag. Some manufacturers often skimp on the chassis, and just bump up the internal hardware, or shift the screen to a higher res. In the case of the Blade 16 though I can say, hand on heart, that this thing is stunning.
The aluminum chassis has a beautiful cool soft-touch satin finish. The edges are clean cut, and smooth with tighter radial bends, bevels are there, but impressively subtle, and everywhere you look, that design philosophy is mimicked, from the keys, to the typeface, to the trackpad, even to the ports, and the bezel that surrounds that beautiful OLED display.
Razer truly has mastered the art of building a laptop that blurs the lines between gamer and professional, without compromising on either front, and it's a joy to behold.
The only flaw, in my opinion, is the Razer logo on the back of the unit. By default, it's Razer's iconic hard-lit, green, three-headed snake which stands out a touch compared to the rest of the design.
From a hardware perspective, the kit is exemplary. Razer's paired an outstandingly colorful OLED display with an RTX 5090, that's fully unlocked with a chonky 175W TGP. The screen itself only comes in at 2560x1600 in a 16:10 aspect ratio, but it gives it a pixel density of around 189 PPI, which is about 37% denser than your standard 32-inch 4K affair. And that's backed up with a 240Hz refresh rate and Vesa's DisplayHDR TrueBlack 1000 certification too.
I'm a big fan of that pairing as well. Laptop makers often fall into a trap where they try to just cram as many pixels as possible into a product at this price tag. Marketing loves it because "number bigger" and "bigger numbers sell," but it honestly demolishes overall frame rates when going for the 4K or 3K option, and I'd argue that you can't really tell the difference between 190 PPI and 280 PPI anyway. Pairing the high-end RTX 5090 with 1600p gives you a far better, well-rounded experience across anything you throw at it, and allows you to take advantage of higher refresh rates.
Port selection is overall pretty solid too. You've got Thunderbolt 5 and 4 here (both of which support power delivery), along with a healthy complement of USB-C ports, and even an SD card reader, if you're heavy into the ol' photography. There's an HDMI 2.1 out as well, although sadly no dedicated Ethernet, but you do get Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 thrown in as standard.
Also, one thing to bear in mind: given the form factor, RAM is soldered by design, so what you buy is what you get — there's no possibility of upgrading this in the future.
Razer Blade 16 (2026) review: Performance
- Outstanding gaming performance
- Solid at computational tasks
- SSD could be better
Let's address the elephant in the room first. SSD performance is OK, and just OK at that. The Blade 16 (2026) uses a Lexar NM790 PCIe 4.0 SSD either in a 1TB or 2TB config, depending on what you pick.
It's a relatively affordable drive coming out of China, based on YMTC's 232-layer TLC NAND flash, and a MaxioTech MAP1602A controller. There's no DRAM cache on the thing, and it's single-sided and more than reliable enough, but just don't expect it to burst through benchmark results and computational tasks quite like something from SanDisk's labs or the PCIe 5.0 league. Still, we should be thankful because if Razer had picked that, this thing could've cost twice as much.
3DMark: Fire Strike: 36,218; Steel Nomad: 5,911; Time Spy: 21,661
Geekbench 6.6: Multicore: 16,971; Single-core: 2,895
Cinebench 2024: Single Core: 128; Multi Core: 1,234
Crossmark: 2,098
Total War: Warhammer III: 1080p, Medium: 289.2fps
Total War: Warhammer III: 1800p, Ultra: 116.7
Battery Life (PC Mark Gaming): 1 hour and 41 minutes
In-game though, this thing is outstanding. I ran a plethora of benchmarks against it, including our standard suite which we've used for products like the Alienware 15 and other laptops, alongside just running it at full-tilt, on ultra presets at max resolution to really get a solid idea of how it performs.
At 2560x1600 this thing with its RTX 5090 just shatters expectations. Cyberpunk 2077 on the Ray Tracing: Ultra preset, no DLSS, no Multi Frame Gen (MFG) hit 35 fps. With DLSS set to Quality and MFG on, you're seeing that figure jump up to 115.6 fps on the average.
Total War: Warhammer 3 saw 116 fps across its benchmark too. In our standard 1080p medium tests (which we do for consistency) results were off the charts: 290 fps in Total War, 310 in Cyberpunk, 166 in Final Fantasy XIV. These are genuinely impressive results.
The thing driving the bulk of that performance is the 175W TGP (that goes for the 5070 Ti and 5080 models too). It allows the chip to run at full tilt, with max clock speeds for the 5090 tapped out at 2,812 MHz, and it averaged 2,100 MHz under testing conditions, with an average temp of just 65C.
The CPU by comparison was a little toastier, at 93C when maxed out at its peak 4.9 GHz during the runs, with max GPU wattage coming in at 165W out of that 175W maximum. Nice.
Intel's Core Ultra 9 doesn't disappoint, and it scored a healthy 128 points in Cinebench's single core test, the highest single core result I've seen for a laptop by some margin.
Razer Blade 16 (2026) review: Battery life
- 280W charger juices up quick
- Battery life solid given the spec
- Did not finish the video test
On the battery life front, perhaps unsurprisingly given the phenomenal spec pulling power from this thing, it didn't last quite as long in PC Mark's gaming test as you'd expect, but 81 minutes is still a comfortable time, and quite close to what we saw with the (admittedly far cheaper) Alienware 15 DA15265, trailing it by eight minutes.
Try as I might, however, I couldn't get it to run the full PC Mark Video benchmark for any prolonged period without crashing. With a manual benchmark, utilising YouTube and a looped hour long video, it survived for about 3.5 hours before giving up the ghost (although do bear in mind that is with Wi-Fi enabled, which defers to our usual results).
The good news is that the power brick is exceptionally fast at charging the Razer Blade 16 (2026), perhaps unsurprisingly given it delivers 280W of juice.
Should I buy the Razer Blade 16 (2026)?
| Attributes  | Notes  | Rating  | 
|---|---|---|
| Value  | Razer's Blade 16 does not represent good value for money. You're paying for design, cooling and RAM above all else. But the performance the form factor are rare anywhere else, and that does command a premium. | 3 / 5  | 
| Design  | Aside from a missing Ethernet port, there's little to moan about the Blade 16, with a healthy port selection, and an outstanding aesthetic tied with a beautiful design and incredible screen, it's hard to fault it. | 5 / 5  | 
| Performance  | Gaming performance is exceptional and the CPU more than delivers, particularly when tied to that beautiful OLED display, the SSD could be better, but then the price tag would see a hit as a result. | 5 / 5  | 
| Battery life  | 81 minutes in gaming and about 3.5 hours on video streaming. It's enough, but you'll want to keep the charger handy during longer streaming sessions. | 4 / 5  | 
| Final score  | Only let down by its high price, and the lack of an Ethernet port, there's little to not love about this thing, if you've got the cash to buy it. | 4.5 / 5  | 
Buy it if…
You're looking for a laptop that blurs the lines between professional and gamer
With an incredible hardware spec, and performance that delivers not only in-game but in any professional app you throw its way, the Blade 16 is undoubtedly a brilliant laptop.
You love a crisp smooth OLED that looks great no matter what you throw at it
It's just utterly stunning to look at and use, with enough pixel density to keep even the most eager of 4K enthusiasts happy. With exemplary colors and a 240 Hz refresh rate, there's little to dislike about it.
Don't buy it if…
You're after good value for money
This ain't it chief. At near five grand in the UK and US, and nine grand in Oz, it's ridiculous money for a ridiculous spec. It's good, but you're paying mainly for design here, not the spec.
You just need a gosh darn Ethernet port
Seriously? All this money and not a single Ethernet port? On a gaming laptop? Tut tut Razer…
Razer Blade 16 (2026) review: Also Consider
Alienware 16 Area-51
Big bold and beautiful, the Alienware 16 shares a lot of the same ideology as Razer's Blade 16, 2560 x 1600 screen, 240Hz refresh rate, RTX 5090, it's all there, the only downsides? No HDR support, and the battery life isn't quite as good. Still it's a heck of a lot cheaper.
Read our full Alienware 16 Area-51 review
Razer Blade 18 (2026)
The Blade 16's older brother, with a similar top-line spec sheet, but a far larger screen that justifies the 16:10 3840 x 2400 resolution. If you want a gaming laptop that feels like a gaming laptop, but with a bit more pizazz, and aren't so worried about having the latest CPU, then the Blade 18, might just be the right pick for you.
Read our full Razer Blade 18 review
How I tested the Razer Blade 16 (2026)
- Tested in a variety of different locations
- Benchmarked across our usual suite + ultra presets at full res
- 11 years of experience benchmarking and testing all manner of expensive laptops
I've spent years testing and benchmarking some of the world's most expensive laptops, from MSI's ultrabooks, to Asus, to Alienware's and even Razer's so the Blade 16 isn't new territory for me. I set it up as my daily driver and used it over a period of three weeks, to get to grips with it for my professional work and during relaxation time as well, and it delivered on all fronts.
As for testing, I benchmarked it in line with all of my other TechRadar laptop reviews, which focus on a medium 1920 x 1080 preset, to have a consistent baseline for everything we review.
I also tested it at Ultra on its native 2560 x 1600 resolution, to get a good understanding for how it'd be used, in its true config, then compared those results to my knowledge testing other high-end gaming laptops like this for PC Gamer, and other brands.
- First reviewed: September 2026

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro : des utilisateurs signalent des crépitements dans le haut-parleur
articles.text:
À peine commercialisé, l’iPhone 18 Pro voit déjà les signalements se multiplier. Après Face ID et l’écran, c’est désormais le haut-parleur qui fait parler de lui, avec des propriétaires confrontés à des crépitements et autres bruits parasites.
Depuis quelques jours, les témoignages se multiplient sur les forums de MacRumors et Reddit. Des propriétaires d’iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max disent entendre un bruit inhabituel dans le haut-parleur de leur appareil : crépitement, claquement sourd ou petit « tick » intermittent, les descriptions diffèrent, mais le problème reste le même. Apple n’a pour l’heure pas réagi publiquement à ces remontées.
iPhone 18 Pro : le haut-parleur crépite dans plusieurs situations
Le bruit ne se manifeste pas de la même manière chez tous les utilisateurs. Certains l'entendent régulièrement, tandis que d'autres ne le constatent que dans des situations précises, par exemple en faisant défiler une page web, à la réception d'une notification, lorsque le clavier apparaît à l'écran ou pendant un appel passé sur le réseau cellulaire. Sur certains appareils, deux manipulations permettraient également de reproduire le phénomène : activer puis désactiver le mode Avion, ou modifier rapidement la luminosité de l'écran.
Le son semble principalement provenir du haut-parleur d'écoute, celui utilisé pour les appels. Plusieurs propriétaires expliquent par ailleurs avoir retourné leur iPhone avant de recevoir un appareil de remplacement présentant le même problème. Ces témoignages suggèrent que le phénomène ne serait donc pas limité à quelques unités isolées, même si sa portée réelle du problème reste pour l'instant inconnue.
La mise à jour iOS 27.0.1 ne règle pas le problème
Apple a récemment déployé iOS 27.0.1, une mise à jour destinée à corriger un autre bug touchant les iPhone 18 Pro. Celui-ci pouvait provoquer le redémarrage de l’appareil après un échec d’authentification avec Face ID. Les notes de version ne font en revanche état d’aucun correctif concernant le son, et les premiers retours après l’installation indiquent que les crépitements sont toujours présents.
Ce nouveau problème s’ajoute aux autres signalements apparus depuis la sortie des iPhone 18 Pro. Dans les premiers jours de commercialisation, des utilisateurs avaient notamment rapporté des anomalies liées à l’écran. Pour le haut-parleur, la cause reste encore inconnue. S’il s’agit d’un bug logiciel, Apple pourrait le corriger avec une prochaine mise à jour. En revanche, si le problème est matériel, sa résolution pourrait devenir beaucoup plus contraignante pour les utilisateurs.

articles.title: Samsung libera One UI 9 para mais celulares brasileiros • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung libera One UI 9 para mais celulares brasileiros
Galaxy S26 passa a rodar o Android 17, com direito a Now Brief e Now Nudget aprimorados.
Resumo
- A Samsung liberou a atualização da One UI 9/Android 17 para o Galaxy S26 no Brasil.
- A atualização já pode ser consultada no menu Config → Atualização de software. Ela tem 4,030 GB.
- A One UI 9 é baseada no Android 17 e inclui recursos como o Now Brief e o New Nudge aprimorados.
Demorou, mas aconteceu: a Samsung liberou a atualização da One UI 9/Android 17 para o Galaxy S26 vendido no Brasil. Alguns dos nossos seguidores nas redes sociais até entraram em contato para comemorar a novidade! Este é o nível de entusiasmo dos adeptos da gigante sul-coreana (que já estavam bravos, e com razão, pela demora do update).
A atualização já pode ser consultada no menu Config → Atualização de software. O pacote tem 4,030 GB, portanto é recomendável que o download ocorra quando a pessoa estiver dentro da cobertura de uma rede Wi-Fi).
O que muda com a One UI 9?
A descrição oficial da Samsung diz o seguinte: “A One UI 9 aproxima o Galaxy AI do seu dia a dia com experiências mais úteis e intuitivas. Aproveite novas formas de simplificar tarefas, criar e manter-se conectado com funções de IA que se adaptam à maneira como você usa o seu Galaxy.”
Esta nova versão da One UI é baseada no Android 17, o mais recente liberado pelo Google. Entre as novidades de software estão o Now Brief e o New Nudge mais inteligentes, a partir das informações que o sistema captura no próprio telefone da pessoa. Outra função recente é o aplicativo My FanCam, capaz de analisar vídeos e produzir cortes focando em pessoas específicas. Ele foi originalmente apresentado junto com a safra 2026 de telefone dobráveis.
Atualização também é esperada em outros Galaxy
A operação brasileira da Samsung está uma semana atrasada em relação ao cronograma inicialmente obtido pelo Tecnoblog. A linha completa do S26 deveria ter recebido a One UI 9 na semana passada, mas isso não ocorreu e os motivos não são conhecidos.
Já nesta semana, do dia 29 de setembro, deveria ser a vez da linha S25 e dos dobráveis de 2025 serem contemplados com a atualização. No entanto, os donos de Galaxy Z Fold 7 disseram nas redes sociais que até o presente momento não surgiu nenhuma atualização.
Além dos produtos citados acima, os seguintes aparelhos também devem receber o sistema nas próximas semanas: Galaxy Z Flip 7, linha do Galaxy S24, Galaxy Z Flip 6, Galaxy Z Fold 6 e Galaxy A57.

articles.title: Amazon prend de l'avance sur son Prime Day et brade son Echo Hub (-55%)
articles.text:
L'Amazon Echo Hub permet de relier tous vos appareils connectés au sein du même objet. Celui-ci possède une interface fluide et personnalisable. En marge du Prime Day, le Hub chute sous les 100 euros.
Avant le début officiel du Prime Day, l'Amazon Echo Hub passe de 199,99 euros à 89,99 euros
Pourquoi choisir l'Amazon Echo Hub ?
- Tous vos appareils connectés au même endroit : L'Amazon Echo Hub permet de réunir vos volets, vos caméras et votre sonnette connectée au sein d'un seul appareil.
- Un contrôle grâce à la voix : Si l'interface est intuitive, l'Echo Hub est compatible avec Alexa, ce qui vous permet de déclencher vos différents appareils connectés grâce à votre voix.
- Un prix très attractif : 200 euros, cela peut sembler conséquent pour un objet qui peut rapidement faire office de gadget, mais avec cette réduction de 110 euros, il devient tout de suite plus attractif.
Un panneau de contrôle intuitif
Cet Amazon Echo Hub est facile à prendre en main. Il se présente avec un écran de huit pouces tandis que l'interface qui fonctionne grâce à Fire OS offre plusieurs onglets personnalisables. Logiquement, vous pourrez accéder individuellement à tous vos appareils connectés qu'il s'agisse de volets, caméras ou sonnettes. L'Echo Hub est aussi compatible avec la norme Thread, permettant d'y lier également vos objets de contrôle de la température. Vous pouvez aussi créer un widget pour réunir tous les appareils d'une même pièce.
Pour contrôler vos appareils, vous pourrez vous servir de l'écran tactile ou de votre voix puisque l'Echo Hub est compatible avec Alexa.
Un hub et c'est tout
Cependant, l'Amazon Echo Hub n'est pas rempli que de qualités. Pour trouver son premier défaut, il faut continuer de parler de son écran. Si celui-ci s'avère intuitif et personnalisable, il pêche sur sa fluidité. Il peut manquer de réactivité et les changements de page peuvent parfois présenter quelques ralentissements.
Pour trouver son autre grand défaut, il faut se pencher sur son design. Pour commencer, il est en plastique, une matière qui n'est pas des plus agréables au toucher. Néanmoins, en prenant en compte le fait que le produit passe sous les 100 euros, c'est plus facilement oubliable. Surtout que son coloris blanc lui permettra de s'intégrer facilement dans tous les intérieurs.
Le véritable problème réside dans l'absence de caméra qui aurait pu permettre d'effectuer des échanges avec un livreur devant votre porte. Par conséquent, si vous pourrez effectivement voir si une personne sonne à votre porte, il faudra nécessairement vous diriger vers votre sonnette connectée pour échanger avec la personne qui sonne chez vous.
✅ Les points forts
- Un design discret qui s'intégrera dans tous les intérieurs
- Une interface intuitive
- Compatible avec l'assistant vocal Alexa
❌ Les limites
- Une interface qui peut manquer de fluidité
- Pas d'audio bidirectionnelle
Habituellement, l'Amazon Echo Hub est vendu pour 199,99 euros, mais en ce moment, son prix chute à 89,99 euros
L'Amazon Echo Hub s'adresse principalement à ceux qui ont une maison entièrement connectée. Si tel est votre cas, alors cet appareil s'avère intéressant puisqu'il regroupe effectivement tous vos objets. Cependant, l'absence de caméra ou l'impossibilité de communiquer avec une personne qui sonne à votre porte peut en freiner certains.
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Comment profiter des Jours Flash Prime ?
Afin de profiter des Jours Flash Amazon Prime, vous devez avant tout souscrire à un abonnement Amazon Prime. Pour ça, rien de plus simple, il vous suffit de créer un compte Amazon puis de souscrire à l'une des offres Amazon Prime :
- Amazon Prime à 69€ par an
- Amazon Prime à 6,99€/mois
- Amazon Prime Student 3,49€/mois (pour les étudiants et les 18-22 ans)

articles.title: Gaming moves fast. Can its defenses keep up?
articles.text:
Gaming moves fast. Can its defenses keep up?
Gaming’s DDoS challenges reveal a growing security gap
Last October, a massive DDoS attack suspected to be linked to the Aisuru botnet disrupted some of the biggest names in gaming. Steam, Riot Games, PlayStation Network and Xbox experienced simultaneous outages, affecting games including Counter-Strike, Dota 2, Valorant, and League of Legends.
Researchers investigating the event estimated that the attack may have peaked at 29.69 Tbps, which would make it one of the largest DDoS attacks ever recorded.
Founder and CEO of MazeBolt.
These are top-tier, sophisticated technology companies with significant resources devoted to staying online. Yet even at this level, major disruptions still happen. That raises a more useful question than simply how large the attack was: Why can the DDoS defenses that organizations have invested in heavily, still leave them exposed when it matters most?
Why Availability Outages are a Revenue Problem in Gaming Gaming accounted for 19% of DDoS attacks observed by Gcore in H2 2025, making it the third-most-targeted sector, behind technology and financial services. Overall DDoS activity in Gcore's dataset increased 150% year over year.
For a gaming company, availability is arguably the biggest part of the product. If players cannot authenticate, stay connected, or play at all, users, and therefore revenue, go down. The consequence of extended disruption is a lack of trust, affecting the bottom line.
For example, an outage during a major launch or tournament for a gaming company is catastrophic because it’s occurring exactly when they’ve put time and resources into ensuring maximum player demand. A failed launch window means marketing dollars, player acquisition, and revenue all take a hit.
How configuration drift creates DDoS protection gaps
Configuration drift is the growing mismatch between deployed DDoS controls and the changing environment those controls were configured to protect. Gaming is especially vulnerable to this because the product changes constantly.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Studios are always shipping updates because players expect it. To stay relevant and exciting (and profitable), they need to always be launching a major update or new title, or expanding to a new region or user base.
Constant changes mean constant risk. Every new change is a chance for a system or safety net that was in place during deployment to fail. For example, let’s say a studio launches a new matchmaking service. Traffic to that service may be routed differently, but the mitigation policy protecting the original service doesn't automatically follow it. Now you’ve got a gap. The DDoS protection may be the same, but the environment around it isn't.
In addition to product, feature, or service releases, any change to the IT ecosystem may have an impact on the environment the security controls were configured to protect. Those changes accumulate. This is called configuration drift. And it becomes the default, not the exception.
Why point-in-time DDoS testing cannot keep pace with continuous change
This problem is especially concerning in gaming, but any company operating a fast-moving digital service faces some version of it. Point-in-time red team testing alone can't provide current evidence about DDoS protection across a continuously changing environment. If point-in-time testing happens in January, and then the environment materially changes in February, what exactly does the January result tell the team in August?
Despite this, point-in-time testing still has real value: it tells a studio how well its people and procedures respond on the day the test is run. The issue is that the change is continuous. And the release and testing cycles are running on different clocks.
A game studio might make meaningful production changes every week while its formal testing schedule runs, say, quarterly or semiannually. Every change between those two points potentially creates a gap between the environment that passed the test and the environment players are actually using.
Point-in-time testing was never built to validate configuration coverage across an entire, constantly changing attack surface. For gaming companies, that leaves too much time between an environmental change and knowing whether existing DDoS protections still cover it.
What gaming security teams should change
Because gaming infrastructure is constantly changing, DDoS validation needs to be ongoing rather than relying on scheduled point-in-time testing or waiting for major events like a new launch or a tournament. This gives security teams current evidence that their protections continue to work even as infrastructure and services evolve.
That ongoing process should account for changes to public-facing services and how existing protections respond to them. Did this change alter what is exposed, how traffic reaches it, or how existing DDoS controls respond?
When ongoing validation identifies a DDoS gap, teams should investigate how it emerged rather than treating it as an isolated vulnerability to patch. If a configuration change exposed one service, the same change or pattern may exist elsewhere in the environment. Finding the vulnerability should prompt teams to look for similar exposure across other services.
What this means for any always-on digital business
Players don’t care about protection deployments, whether their preferred game passed its last point-in-time test, or if an outage is caused by the technology itself or an outside attack. The game works, or it doesn't.
Gaming makes the consequences of these vulnerabilities unusually visible. When availability is part of the product, even a small weakness can become a business problem the moment attackers find it.
For any always-on digital business, leaders need to pay attention to how their defenses can keep pace with the environment they are responsible for protecting, especially as it changes. The same lesson applies to any company whose customers expect its digital services to be always available.

articles.title: Dutch Police Arrest 24-Year-Old Amsterdam Man in ShinyHunters Investigation
articles.text:
Dutch authorities have confirmed that they arrested a 24-year-old man from Amsterdam in connection with the ShinyHunters group.
"It is true that this month a 24-year-old man from Amsterdam was arrested in an investigation into the hacker group ShinyHunters," the Politie Landelijke Opsporing en Interventies said in an X post Monday.
Police said the individual is expected to appear before the Rotterdam District Court on September 29, 2026.
Although law enforcement officials did not disclose any additional details, independent security journalist Brian Krebs and DataBreaches.Net identified the arrested man as Pepijn van der Stap (aka Umbreon), who was previously apprehended in 2023 for his role in a series of data thefts and extortions.
Per DataBreaches.Net, van der Stap was arrested on September 15, 2026. In 2023, it emerged that the individual worked at cybersecurity company Hadrian and volunteered at the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD).
"Working at Hadrian and volunteering at DIVD made me more paranoid about keeping up appearances, and I actually felt more pressure and paranoia because I was working such long hours," van der Stap told DataBreaches.Net in June 2023.
"So yes, I was doing more lawful work and much less illegal work but I became more paranoid about getting caught. The paranoia became so extreme that I was expecting a knock on the door at any time."
He is presently employed as the offensive security lead at the Dutch company Neo Security, according to LinkedIn.
In his profile, van der Stap acknowledged his journey "hasn't been a straight line" and that "I've seen security from both sides of the terminal, an experience that taught me hard lessons but ultimately gave me clarity: knowledge is for building and protecting, not breaking."
When ShinyHunters was contacted by The Hacker News about the arrest, the group denied having any connection with van der Stap.
"That individual has no association with us. Frankly, we are laughing," the group said. "Dutch police are chasing attention and public favour after the massive embarrassment in [sic] result of the Odido hack. They want to seem like they are ahead of the FBI in investigating ShinyHunters."
The development comes as ShinyHunters claimed credit for its brazen hack of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation's (FBI) job application site apply.fbijobs.gov, stealing terabytes of sensitive data.
"This was all a marketing campaign to protect our business and actively combat disinformation," a ShinyHunters representative told 404 Media. "If we made this statement normally then this much attention to our words and intentions would’ve never been this widespread."
"We'd have been ignored and disregarded. However, now everyone knows what the issue is and what we are doing. Everyone is reading about it. We proved our points on several occasions. We do not care what the public says and we are not affected by it nor do we cloud our judgement by external opinions and thoughts."
In a statement shared with The Hacker News, the group reiterated again that the attack on the FBI's systems was not extortion and that it's not financially motivated.
"We understand why many misinterpreted this as extortion and are convinced we would publish this data and/or misuse it such as selling to third parties due to our history in past operations which has never involved a government entity of prominence," the spokesperson said.
"We again want to emphasise that this is not extortion, it was never one to begin with, not a threat, not a ransom, and not financially motivated. Nothing will happen. We are way past this situation in our business operations and we confidently believe we have been successful due to seeing a recent influx of success in our operations."
Although the group said it exploited a new zero-day flaw in Oracle PeopleSoft to gain unauthorized access and siphon the data, it's now assessed that ShinyHunters employed a URL-encoding trick to bypass web application firewall (WAF) rules designed to mitigate CVE-2026-35273.
Update
In a statement shared on X, the FBI and Dutch National Police formally announced the arrest of a 24-year-old man from Amsterdam, who is suspected to be "one of the alleged leaders of ShinyHunters." The FBI said it's "actively working with partners to obtain and execute more leads in the ongoing investigation based on this arrest."
The suspect is also alleged to have attempted to incite two murders, an accusation that's separate from the investigation into ShinyHunters, the Netherlands Police said, adding the individual was not arrested in connection with the Odido hack.
"Since last year, this cybercriminal and his co-conspirators have allegedly breached more than 140 organizations and taken at least 70 million dollars in extortion payments," FBI Assistant Director Brett Leatherman said. "They often target third-party vendors in cloud-based platforms, stealing sensitive data and extorting victims with threats to publish it."
(The story was updated after publication to include a response from ShinyHunters and add details of the arrest.)

articles.title: Stellantis : trop de demande et pas assez de batteries, le constructeur met des usines françaises en pause
articles.text:
Stellantis : trop de demande et pas assez de batteries, le constructeur met des usines françaises en pause
En octobre, Stellantis va temporairement suspendre la production de véhicules dans plusieurs de ses usines françaises. La faute, notamment, à un manque de pièces centrales.
Peugeot e-3008 Launch Edition 325 Dual Motor
On peut y voir de l'ironie. Alors que Stellantis vient de breveter un système de batterie éjectable en cas d'incendie de véhicule, le groupe a annoncé ce mardi 29 septembre une mauvaise nouvelle liée, en grande partie, à cette pièce indispensable pour les véhicules électriques. Des difficultés d'approvisionnement vont ainsi obliger Stellantis à temporairement mettre à l'arrêt quatre usines en France.
Voitures électriques : forte demande, mais Stellantis manque de batteries
Si l'an dernier à la même période, plusieurs usines étaient temporairement mises en pause pour éviter de gonfler les stocks de voitures, cette fois “cette décision est liée à une disponibilité insuffisante de certaines batteries destinées aux versions longue autonomie de nos véhicules électriques”, justifie Stellantis dans un communiqué.
Malgré des rappels très nombreux sur de multiples marques ces derniers mois, le groupe indique que “la demande pour ces versions est soutenue, en particulier de la part des clients professionnels, et reste supérieure aux capacités actuelles d’approvisionnement”.
Dans le détail, quatre usines vont être concernées par une période d'arrêt allant de cinq à 15 jours : Sochaux, Rennes, Mulhouse et Poissy.
Pour Sochaux, source notamment des Peugeot e-3008 et e-5008, la fermeture aura lieu du 23 au 30 octobre. La production en France, à Douvrin, de batteries par ACC (coentreprise entre Stellantis, Mercedes et TotalEnergies) semble donc encore insuffisante. L'usine de Rennes sera, elle, à l'arrêt du 22 au 30 octobre. Du côté de Mulhouse, plus durement touché, il est question du 15 au 30 octobre.
Pour cette dernière, c'est surtout la fin de cycle des Peugeot 308 et 408 qui est en cause, tandis que des aides financières et de nouveaux modèles en 2029 devraient faire relancer la machine dans les années à venir. À la CGT, ce choix du chômage technique ne plaît pas : “Si nous produisons moins de voitures, gardons tout le monde, y compris les intérimaires, baissons les cadences et profitons-en pour améliorer les conditions de travail et former les salariés à Mulhouse.”
Enfin, l'unité de production de Poissy, qui sera bientôt reconvertie, fermera ses portes sur une courte période, du 19 au 23 octobre, “pour adapter la production à la demande du marché dans une logique de gestion fine des stocks”.

articles.title: Elon Musk pronosticó qué pasará con los trabajos ante el avance de la IA y anticipó una "era de abundancia"
articles.text:
Elon Musk afirmó ante la prensa que, gracias a la inteligencia artificial y la superinteligencia, los empleos cambiarán pero no desaparecerán. Asimismo, proyectó una futura “era de abundancia” con acceso universal a bienestar.
El magnate tecnológico respondió el martes, a la salida de la Casa Blanca, una pregunta directa sobre el futuro laboral en la era de la IA. Trump y ejecutivos de las principales empresas tecnológicas del mundo acababan de firmar un pacto voluntario de seguridad para la inteligencia artificial, en un encuentro que también puso sobre la mesa la expansión de los centros de datos y la competencia con China.
PUBLICIDAD
Musk tomó la palabra cuando un periodista preguntó qué harían quienes veían el intercambio y se preocupaban especialmente por los empleos de oficina. Su respuesta fue optimista y polémica a partes iguales: la inteligencia artificial —o “superinteligencia”, según la nueva terminología que Donald Trump acaba de ordenar usar en el gobierno federal— no conducirá al desempleo masivo, sino a una transformación profunda del trabajo.
Musk dijo que los empleos cambiarán con la inteligencia artificial, no que desaparecerán
“Los empleos van a cambiar. Siempre han cambiado”, declaró Musk ante los periodistas reunidos en la entrada del ala oeste de la Casa Blanca, según consta en el video difundido por CBS News y recogido por Reuters. Para ilustrar su argumento, recurrió a un ejemplo histórico: ser “computadora” solía ser una profesión.
PUBLICIDAD
“Antes había edificios llenos de personas haciendo cálculos. Pero ahora las computadoras digitales realizan esas tareas y no creo que nadie anhele volver a hacer cálculos todo el día para calcular las tasas de interés bancarias, que era lo que solían hacer”, consideró el empresario.
Su argumento es que la IA producirá una transformación comparable —aunque de alcance mucho mayor— en una amplia variedad de ocupaciones. No sostuvo que el empleo permanecería intacto, sino que la naturaleza del trabajo evolucionaría.
“Creo que veremos una evolución de los roles. No es como si el desempleo hubiera aumentado. De hecho, hay una enorme demanda de personas”, explicó. “Así que creo que el resultado más probable es increíblemente beneficioso. Es un futuro que, si pudieras mirar hacia adelante, querrías”, concluyó.
PUBLICIDAD
La promesa de una “era de abundancia” y una renta alta universal
El pasaje más comentado de la intervención de Musk fue su descripción del escenario que considera más probable. “Creo que, con mucha diferencia, el resultado más probable es una era de abundancia, en la que no solo tendremos una renta básica universal, sino una renta alta universal”, afirmó.
El fundador de Tesla y SpaceX fue más allá de la discusión habitual sobre renta básica universal —una propuesta que ya circula en debates de política económica— y planteó una variante más ambiciosa: que la combinación de robots y superinteligencia podría generar tal volumen de bienes y servicios que el nivel de vida de cualquier persona en el mundo superaría al de los más privilegiados de hoy. Puso como ejemplo el acceso a atención médica de calidad.
PUBLICIDAD
“Cuando tienes robots y superinteligencia, eso significa que todas las personas en el mundo pueden tener una atención médica mejor que la de cualquiera aquí, incluyéndome a mí”, proyectó.
Uno de los presentes le replicó “no si no tienen trabajo”, Musk respondió con la afirmación sobre la evolución de los empleos citada más arriba.
El contexto: Trump, los líderes tecnológicos y la expansión de los centros de datos
Las declaraciones de Musk tuvieron lugar el 29 de septiembre de 2026, tras un almuerzo a puerta cerrada en la Casa Blanca entre Trump y ejecutivos de las principales empresas del sector. Según Reuters, entre los asistentes estaban Greg Brockman (presidente de OpenAI), Dario Amodei (director ejecutivo de Anthropic), Mark Zuckerberg (director ejecutivo de Meta), Sundar Pichai (director ejecutivo de Google), Jensen Huang (presidente y director ejecutivo de Nvidia) y Lisa Su (directora ejecutiva de AMD).
PUBLICIDAD
Lo que comenzó como un almuerzo privado derivó en una conferencia de prensa: Trump se unió al presidente de la Cámara de Representantes, Mike Johnson, y al grupo de ejecutivos en la entrada de la Casa Blanca —un espacio que el mandatario rara vez usa para atender a periodistas— y respondió preguntas durante unos 30 minutos, con los directores ejecutivos de pie a sus espaldas.
Durante ese intercambio, el mandatario y las compañías firmaron un acuerdo voluntario de seguridad que contempla controles internos, auditorías externas independientes y supervisión a nivel de junta directiva para los sistemas de IA, según la copia publicada por el propio mandatario en sus redes sociales. La jornada también incluyó el lanzamiento de una herramienta de IA impulsada por asesores de Trump para facilitar el acceso de la ciudadanía a los servicios gubernamentales.
PUBLICIDAD
Trump también reiteró su respaldo a la rápida expansión de los centros de datos y advirtió que China quería “cada centro de datos que nosotros no queramos”, en referencia a la competencia tecnológica entre ambas potencias. Musk respaldó esa caracterización con un escueto “sí”.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
	
	
	
Plan Tasks, Resources, and Deadlines in One Place With Microsoft Project 2024 for $49.97
Microsoft Project Professional 2024 is built for managing projects from the initial plan through completion, with tools for organizing tasks, coordinating resources, monitoring progress, and creating reports. For a limited time, you can get the desktop application for $49.97 on one Windows PC, with the license lasting a lifetime.
Rather than building every project schedule from scratch, you can start with pre-built templates and customize them to fit your needs. Define tasks and dependencies, and Project can calculate start and finish dates based on how those tasks relate to one another. Multiple timeline views also make it easier to get a visual overview of complex project schedules.Gantt chart task-path highlighting shows how individual tasks relate to one another. What-if scenarios allow project managers to test different assignments before committing resources. Baselines preserve the original plan so actual progress can be measured against initial schedules.
Microsoft Project also includes built-in reports such as Burndown and Resource Overview. These reports help communicate schedule, workload, and progress information to executives, clients, and other stakeholders.
Timesheets record hours spent on project and non-project work. That information can support payroll, invoicing, and internal resource management. The application can also synchronize with Project Online and Project Server.
Microsoft Teams for Business integration allows users to check a team member's online presence and begin chats or calls from a project plan. Teams for Business must be licensed separately.
The licensing terms are specific: The lifetime license covers one PC and connects to that device rather than a Microsoft account. Buyers should select the installation computer carefully.
Lifetime access to Microsoft Project Professional 2024 is available for $49.97 through October 4.
