articles.title: « C’est la folie en ce moment » chez Apple : John Ternus voudrait bouleverser la stratégie du groupe
articles.text:
Le 10 juillet dernier, nous avions jugé la performance de John Ternus lors de sa première keynote. Nous avions trouvé que la passation de pouvoir entre Tim Cook et Ternus était sobre et élégante, mais aussi que le nouveau patron d’Apple avait manqué quelque peu d’audace. Mais cette audace qui semblait manquer lors de l’événement ne pointerait-t-elle pas le bout de son nez, et pas qu’un peu ? Le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, est venu rapporter des discussions de Ternus en interne avec ses collègues, et autant dire qu’un chamboulement semble s’annoncer chez Apple.
Une restructuration chez Apple
Alors que John Ternus occupe le poste de CEO d’Apple depuis maintenant presque un mois, une restructuration s’annonce au sein de l’entreprise. Selon Mark Gurman, Ternus voudrait supprimer certains postes de cadres intermédiaires afin de réduire les niveaux hiérarchiques. Sans grande surprise, Ternus aurait considéré l’intelligence artificielle pour les remplacer, soit une stratégie également étudiée par Mark Zuckerberg. L’objectif serait d’accélérer le développement des produits en supprimant certaines couches hiérarchiques. In fine, Apple présenterait une organisation plus légère, davantage axée sur l’ingénierie.
Plus globalement, Ternus aurait comme objectif de réduire les coûts, tout en trouvant de nouvelles rentrées d’argent. Pour ce faire, l’entreprise miserait sur ses produits existants en proposant de nouveaux services, et donc de nouveaux abonnements. Il faut préciser que le chiffre d’affaires des services d’Apple s’est contracté au deuxième trimestre, une première depuis 2022, même s’il reste supérieur à celui enregistré un an plus tôt. Par ailleurs, l’Apple Store connaît lui aussi un ralentissement de son chiffre d’affaires dans un contexte marqué par de nouvelles réglementations américaines et européennes. John Ternus voudrait ainsi restructurer l’entreprise et se concentrer sur les services, mais pas seulement.
Produire plus, plus fréquemment et dans des délais plus courts
Toujours selon Mark Gurman, John Ternus souhaiterait s’éloigner du calendrier habituel d’Apple, marqué par une keynote au printemps et une autre à l’automne. L’objectif serait de lancer de nouveaux produits à d’autres moments de l’année, et ainsi accélérer le rythme de sortie. Ce nouveau mode opératoire passe inévitablement par une accélération du développement des produits. John Ternus voudrait que les équipes d’Apple livrent plus de produits, plus fréquemment et dans des délais plus courts. Par ailleurs, Ternus souhaiterait que l’entreprise se montre plus expérimentale afin de rester compétitive à l’ère de l’intelligence artificielle.
Une pression conséquente serait d’ores et déjà ressentie par certains employés de l’entreprise. Selon Gurman, l’un d’entre eux, qui a désiré rester anonyme, a expliqué que « tout est beaucoup plus opérationnel qu’avant », avant de préciser ensuite : « C’est la folie en ce moment. » Nous espérions davantage d’audace de la part de John Ternus, mais peut-être pas à ce point.

articles.title: "Think of it as Kubernetes for agents": OpenClaw lands in the enterprise with Nvidia and Red Hat on board
articles.text:
“Think of it as Kubernetes for agents”: OpenClaw lands in the enterprise with Nvidia and Red Hat on board
OpenClaw has come a long way since it emerged as a viral weekend project less than a year ago. Created by Austrian developer Peter Steinberger in late 2025, the self-hosted AI agent exploded in popularity and by February — when OpenAI hired Steinberger — it had already amassed more than 100,000 GitHub stars.
In the intervening months, OpenClaw has gone to great lengths to bring more rigor to the project, tightening up its persistent-agent architecture, investing heavily in security, adding new agent harness options, and establishing the independent OpenClaw Foundation to oversee the project. This included sponsors such as OpenAI, Nvidia, Red Hat, and GitHub, as well as a slew of other big-name companies who committed to contributing resources.
Now, it’s making perhaps its clearest push yet into becoming a serious business play with OpenClaw Enterprise (OCE), an open-source, “vendor neutral” platform for managing agents.
OpenClaw gets an enterprise control plane
Giving persistent agents access to codebases, credentials, plugins, messaging channels and other company systems creates an obvious problem for enterprise IT: the more useful those agents become, the more consequential their permissions and actions can be.
In a blog post published on Tuesday, Kevin Lin, a member of technical staff at OpenAI leading OCE efforts, argues that many companies still see agent platforms as too difficult to police centrally, leaving prohibition as the default.
“The default stance of IT in most organizations is to ban agentic platforms like OpenClaw altogether.”
“The main feedback we hear from organizations is that a stronger common security, safety, and governance standard is needed before agents can be fully adopted,” Lin writes. “As a consequence, the default stance of IT in most organizations is to ban agentic platforms like OpenClaw altogether.”
OpenClaw Enterprise is still in its embryonic phase. Lin says that the project is currently “being developed in the open before its 1.0 release” later this year, adding that it’s suitable for internal pilot projects only right now.
So there is still some distance to travel before OCE can reasonably be considered a finished enterprise platform. But much of its intended shape is already visible.
At the center of OCE is the OpenClaw Control Plane (OCC), which gives administrators a central place to deploy agents, separate them into isolated namespaces, manage configuration and credentials, set permissions, and keep a record of changes made through the platform. The agent activity itself happens separately: gateways receive messages, while harnesses handle agent turns, model calls and tool execution.
Ultimately, OCE is being built for environments where multiple agents, users and teams may share the same underlying infrastructure, with controls around who can access what, and how individual agent deployments are isolated from each another.
In terms of gaps, OpenClaw’s architecture documentation says its API, console, persistent worker, PostgreSQL backend, and Kubernetes packaging are already implemented, while areas including external gateway admission, workload authentication back to OCC and some approaches to model authentication remain unfinished.
“OCE is built to run on your own infrastructure and will always be free for any organization to use.”
That unfinished state is at least partly why OpenClaw has released OCE as an open-source project this early. The idea is to let companies inspect and adapt the software themselves, while giving outside developers a chance to shape the project before the formal release. The code is already available on GitHub, with a getting started guide for running it locally or deploying it inside an organization.
“OCE is built to run on your own infrastructure and will always be free for any organization to use,” Lin notes.
The Kubernetes playbook, applied to agents
OpenClaw Enterprise has an interesting provenance. OpenAI was its original home before the company handed the project over to the OpenClaw Foundation. Red Hat and Nvidia have since contributed to its development, while OpenAI and Red Hat are already testing the software internally.
“Think of it as Kubernetes for agents.”
There’s also a fairly explicit Kubernetes-inspired idea permeating the project: OpenClaw wants OCE to provide a common layer for managing agents across different environments. “Think of it as Kubernetes for agents,” the project’s official documentation notes.
That comparison carries through to how OCE is actually deployed. Its full local development environment runs the control plane, PostgreSQL, and agent workloads inside a Kubernetes cluster, while companies can install OCE into Kubernetes infrastructure they already operate. The documentation does include a Docker or Podman Compose option, although that’s currently limited to a control-plane preview and cannot deploy agents through OCC.
Taking to LinkedIn, Lin also draws a clear Kubernetes (K8) comparison, reflecting OpenClaw’s longer-term ambitions for the project.
“Similar to how K8 became the standard for deploying containers in the cloud, we want OCE to be that for agents.”
“Similar to how K8 became the standard for deploying containers in the cloud, we want OCE to be that for agents,” Lin writes.
Red Hat, for its part, sees the emergence of enterprise agents through a similar lens. In a separate blog post published on Tuesday, Joe Fernandes, VP and general manager of Red Hat’s AI business unit, drew a line from the move away from proprietary Unix systems to Linux, through the rise of containers and Kubernetes, and now to agents. His argument is that Red Hat can apply what it learned helping bring those earlier technologies into enterprise environments to this next generation of software.
“Throughout Red Hat’s history, some of the biggest changes in enterprise computing have been driven by fundamental shifts in how applications are built and operated,” Fernandes writes. “Red Hat engineers are already contributing to OpenClaw, and we’re expanding that investment with expertise in Linux, Kubernetes, distributed systems, security and enterprise infrastructure.”
Security remains the main area OpenClaw says it’s concentrating its efforts. The project is combining isolation between trusted and untrusted workloads with sandboxing, granular permissions, and LLM-assisted review, and says it plans to publish a reference architecture showing how those pieces fit together in practice.
For now, OCE is still very much a work in progress. The control plane is taking shape, but much remains unfinished, and OpenClaw is still inviting developers, operators, and security teams to help influence what the project becomes before 1.0.
“We are early, and there is much more work ahead,” Lin adds.

articles.title: ATK Launches Blazing Sky Phantom: 44 g Carbon Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse for $100-120
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
	
	
	
ATK Launches Blazing Sky Phantom: 44 g Carbon Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse for $100-120
ATK has officially launched the Blazing Sky Phantom, a new wireless, carbon fiber composite gaming mouse that is promises a lightweight shell, flagship internals, and a reasonable price—at least compared to big gaming brands, like Razer and Logitech. ATK claims that the Blazing Sky Phantom weighs in at 44 g, although it has had to use honeycomb cutouts on the back of the shell in order to achieve this weight. The Blazing Sky Phantom is available on ATK's website for $99.98 during its pre-order period, after which it will increase to $119.98. Unlike most other carbon fiber mice, the Phantom is available in four different colors: Eon (Black) Prime (White), Verge (Blue), and Dune (Sand). 
The mouse shape is the typical symmetrical shape reminiscent of something like a Razer Viper V4 Pro, but with a few notable changes. For starters, the ATK is notably smaller, measuring in at 119.7 × 62.5 × 37.3 mm, compared to the V4 Pro's 127.1 × 63.9 × 39.9 mm, and potentially making it a better fit for a variety of grip types. It also has an updated Nano coating, which is meant to give gamers better grip during tense moments. The side buttons on the ATK Blazing Sky Phantom also appear to be located further forward compared to the Razer. Internally, the ATK Blazing Sky Phantom features the new PixArt PAW 3955 Master sensor combined with a Nordic 54LM20 MCU, giving it an 8 kHz polling rate in both wired and 2.4 GHz modes and a peak sensitivity of 50,000 DPI. The brand claims that the mouse has a 0.174 ms of latency, although it's never specified whether this is motion latency or click latency.The ATK Phantom's mouse switches are Omron Optical switches, and the scroll wheel uses a Raesha Optical encoder, making the whole thing a lot more resistant to wear and tear. ATK has put a 300 mAh battery inside the Blazing Sky Phantom, which it claims can deliver up to 200 hours of use at 1 kHz polling. Increasing that to 4 kHz or 8 kHz will dramatically reduce battery life. The mouse also ships with two dongles: The Gem 8K Dongle and the Nano 8K Dongle.

articles.title: AMD acquires World Labs AI startup, upping the ante against Nvidia
articles.text:
Chipmaker AMD and world models company World Labs announced that AMD will acquire the AI company by the end of the year, pending regulatory approval. The transaction is valued at $8.2 billion.
In 2024, computer vision scientist Fei-Fei Li founded World Labs with fellow researchers Justin Johnson, Christoph Lassner, and Ben Mildenhall with $230 million in funding, some of which came from AMD.
The company began working on new world models, which are AI models that aim to provide a useful, predictive simulation of the physical world. Competing architectures exist (earlier this year, Ars interviewed World Labs co-founder Ben Mildenhall and others in the field about exactly that), but many involve training a model on vast amounts of video data.
That was the case for Marble, World Labs’ first publicly usable tool. Marble can generate small 3D spaces using Gaussian splats. They can then be exported as 3D assets for use in film production, game development, and other applications. The company has since introduced additional models and tools with different emphases or use cases, such as Atlas.
One use case that has justified enormous investment in the space is generating synthetic data for training robots. That’s a field where Nvidia, AMD’s direct competitor, has a strong lead. AMD has produced its own AI models before, including Micro-World, an open source world model, but it has not produced a stack that competes with Nvidia’s Cosmos and related models and applications.

articles.title: Amazon's new Fire TV Stick 4K comes with an actually good remote | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As part of its fall hardware refresh, Amazon on Wednesday introduced the next version of its Fire TV Stick 4K, which is now slimmer, faster, and can be directly charged via a TV’s USB port.
But the real news is that the device comes with an actually good remote control. No more blue Alexa button, a home button you can feel in the dark, a button for adding favorites, and a new shape that makes it more comfortable to hold in the hand.
It may seem funny that a remote control is the best part about the new streamer, which Amazon claims is 20% to 40% faster than leading competitors. But true TV connoisseurs know that a bad remote can ruin what would otherwise be a great watching experience. Amazon’s older voice remote wasn’t terrible, but it had plenty of room for improvement.
The new one features a different shape and curvature that make it easy to hold and point at the TV. Its buttons and layout have also been redesigned with an eye towards how people often use their remote controls: in a dark room.
If you’ve spent any time with remote controls, you know that you can sometimes struggle to find and mash the right button when you can’t see the device well, especially if the icons on the buttons don’t make much sense.
That was the case with the older remote, which featured a prominent, blue Alexa voice button at the top center. That button has now been replaced with a more subtle black microphone button at the top right, which also has a slight dish at the top, so you can find it by feel.
The new remote’s home button can also be found with touch only, as it has a metallic finish (and an orangeish-reddish hue) that makes it feel distinct. The power button at the top left is recessed, which helps you avoid accidentally turning off the device, and the D-pad is flatter, which makes it easier to roll your thumb around. Lastly, the center of the D-pad now has a more tactile click.
And, in response to user feedback, there’s finally a favorites button you can program to launch a preferred app or even enable an oft-used option, like toggling Closed Captions or Dialog Boost.
The new remote control will come with the Fire TV Stick 4K, but is also being sold separately for those who just want an upgrade.
The 4K Stick itself has 8GB of internal storage, a quad-core 1.7 GHz processor, and support for Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3, and Bluetooth Low Energy. It also supports HDR10, HDR10+, HLG, H.265, H.264, VP9, and AV1 video formats, and can output at 2160p, 1080p, and 720p resolutions at up to 60 frames per second.
The 4K Stick joins the full lineup, which also includes an HD Stick, a 4K “Max” Stick (faster, more storage), and the Fire TV Cube.
The Fire TV 4K Stick is priced at $59.99, but will launch at a discounted price of $29.99. It’s initially available in the U.S., Canada, Japan, Mexico, United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Australia and New Zealand.
The remote will ship in late October, and costs $14.99 in the U.S.

articles.title: „Es gibt viel Spielraum“: Wie KI-Firmen für ihre abtrünnigen KI-Agenten haftbar gemacht werden könnten
articles.text:
KI-Agenten außer Kontrolle: Warum OpenAI, Anthropic und Google in den USA nicht haftbar sind
In den vergangenen Monaten hat eine Flut von Cyberangriffen durch KI-Agenten die Welt verblüfft. Im Juli hatte OpenAI bekannt gegeben, dass ein Schwarm seiner Agenten aus ihrer „Sandbox“ – eine isolierte, kontrollierte Testumgebung – entkommen war und sich in die KI-Plattform Hugging Face gehackt hatte, um bei einem Cybersicherheitstest zu schummeln. Kürzlich haben zudem externe Forscher entdeckt, dass OpenAI-Agenten im Mai eine deutsche Wiki-Seite und die Programmierplattform RubyGems gekapert hatten, um Testantworten auszutauschen.
Anfang September gab dann auch Anthropic vier Vorfälle bekannt, bei denen sein Modell „Claude“ während Cybersicherheitsübungen in Systeme von Drittanbietern eingedrungen war. Und erst letzte Woche bestätigte Google, dass sein Modell Gemini ebenfalls beim Hacken anderer Unternehmen erwischt worden war.
Expert:innen: Der nächste Fall mit KI-Agenten kommt bestimmt
Der Forscher, der die Übernahme der OpenAI-Website aufgedeckt hat, warnte, dass es wahrscheinlich noch weitere, bisher unentdeckte Vorfälle dieser Art gibt. Viele Expert:innen sagen, es sei nur eine Frage der Zeit, bis es zu einem weiteren, möglicherweise noch schwerwiegenderen Vorfall kommt, bei dem KI-Agenten Sandboxen umgehen, um auf Systeme zuzugreifen, auf die sie keinen Zugriff haben sollten. Die große Frage lautet also: Wie können wir Unternehmen zur Verantwortung ziehen, wenn sie die Kontrolle über ihre KI-Agenten verlieren?

articles.title: Divorcée de Meta, la start-up chinoise Manus dévoile une IA concurrente
articles.text:
Fin décembre 2025, Meta annonçait le rachat de Manus, jeune pousse de l’IA agentique, pour un montant rapporté d’environ 2 milliards de dollars. Le régulateur chinois a bloqué l’opération au printemps, avant une rupture officialisée à la mi-juin. Lundi, la même Manus a dévoilé Cue, une application d’agents personnels lancée trois semaines à peine après Muse, le majordome numérique de Meta.
Un e-mail, un numéro et un portefeuille par agent
Chaque agent créé dans Cue reçoit « son propre e-mail, son numéro de téléphone, son portefeuille et son ordinateur ». De quoi envoyer des messages, régler des achats dans la limite d’un budget fixé par l’utilisateur et mener une tâche de bout en bout sur sa propre machine, sans monopoliser celle de son propriétaire. L’agent répondrait aussi au téléphone et passerait commande en scannant un QR code.
L’accès reste gratuit à ce stade, sur invitation, avec un code d’accès anticipé réservé aux 1 000 premiers inscrits. L’application existe sur le web, sur ordinateur et sur mobile, la déclinaison iPhone attendant encore la validation de l’App Store. Aucune grille tarifaire définitive n’a été communiquée.
Sous le capot, Cue repose sur Manus 2.0 et Cascade, une nouvelle architecture maison que l’entreprise crédite de tâches accomplies avec 23,2 % de jetons en moins, 28,2 % plus vite et pour un coût réduit d’un tiers. Ces chiffres émanent du seul intéressé et attendent une vérification indépendante. La mise à jour embarque aussi Studio, un espace de travail partagé entre humains et agents, et un ordinateur dans le nuage où chacun d’eux opère.
Le rachat que Pékin a défait
Le rachat annoncé fin décembre n’a pas tenu six mois : enquête du ministère chinois du Commerce dès janvier, blocage de la transaction le 27 avril, rupture officialisée par Meta le 15 juin. Les parts du groupe américain auraient été rachetées à leur prix d’origine par Tencent et d’autres investisseurs de la jeune pousse.
Redevenue indépendante le 11 août, Manus a relancé ses activités le 1er septembre, une semaine avant que Meta ne présente Muse. Ce dernier lit et envoie des e-mails, s’intègre à WhatsApp et reste pour l’instant réservé aux États-Unis. Meta le décrit comme gratuit pour l’essentiel des usages, avec des abonnements pour aller plus loin, et le fait tourner sur Muse Spark, son modèle maison présenté au printemps. La riposte arrive donc avant même que la cible ne soit disponible ailleurs, et elle vise le même terrain, celui de l’assistant qui agit à votre place.
La disponibilité de Cue en Europe n’a pas été précisée, et Muse ne franchit pas encore l’Atlantique : pour les utilisateurs français, ce duel d’agents qui téléphonent et paient se regarde depuis les tribunes. L’agent doté d’un portefeuille finira pourtant par arriver jusqu’ici, avec une question que ni Manus ni Meta ne tranchent aujourd’hui, celle du responsable quand la machine paie de travers.

articles.title: Why Featherless says you don't need a tank to deliver a pizza
articles.text:
Why Featherless says you don’t need a tank to deliver a pizza
The debate over what size, shape, and scale of model best suits each task isn’t going away any time soon. Joining the fray now is serverless inference provider Featherless. The company has released Simple Jev, an open-source library that converts open-source AI models into high-speed, zero-shot classification engines.
Building on this month’s TypeSafe launch of closed-source, text-only Jev, Featherless’s Simple Jev extends structured decision functionality to open-source models, with image capabilities on Featherless’s hosted endpoints. It enables applications to evaluate incoming data and return categorical assignments or binary choices without generating conversational text.
Don’t use a tank to deliver a pizza
Eugene Cheah, CEO and co-founder of Featherless, tells The New Stack that using bleeding-edge frontier models to classify something like a support ticket is “like using a tank to deliver a pizza” in terms of tooling overload.
“Sure, the pizza tank gets there eventually, but it’s slow, it’s expensive, and it’s the wrong vehicle,” Cheah says. “Businesses need the fast reflexes, the instant they are called for, and that’s a different kind of AI that the industry has neglected for far too long.”
Featherless’s hosted Simple Jev endpoints also include vision support for decision workflows. Currently available only with Gemma or Qwen models, this feature lets developer teams use images as context for instant classification. By bypassing conversational text, the software reduces latency and cuts compute usage.
“The pizza tank gets there eventually, but it’s slow, it’s expensive, and it’s the wrong vehicle.”
Featherless has carefully positioned its stance on multi-modal vision support. Cheah concedes that big closed-source models can work on these tasks. Still, he insists that “it’s the wrong tool for the job”, because they get there by generating text through “enormous multi-trillion-parameter LLMs”, and developers obviously pay frontier prices for that kind of service.
“The industry has been so focused on the size of LLMs it hasn’t stepped back to think about cost and efficiency for a while. Simple Jev never ‘writes’ an answer: we stop the model right where it would choose, read its scores for each allowed option, and output the probabilities,” explains Cheah.
What is a zero-shot classification engine?
For the uninitiated, zero-shot engines use pre-trained language models to classify inputs into unseen target categories without task-specific training data. Because a zero-shot engine classifies inputs it wasn’t explicitly trained on, it relies on transfer learning to predict categories for new inputs without prior exposure.
“But classifiers aren’t new; it’s what universities taught for AI before ChatGPT. What’s new (and credit to Jev here) is a well-designed zero-shot API for it. The core pieces were already there, and we knew them well, which is why we got it up so quickly. What was old is new again,” enthuses Cheah.
Illustrating how his team built the new tooling, Cheah thinks that “Any graduating AI/ML PhD could reimplement Simple Jev from one sentence.”
“They would implement a ‘shared-prefix, two-stage, prefill-only, logit-based classifier’ to do it. We’re open sourcing it to make it easier to replicate and more efficient, and I expect hundreds more open source Jev clones,” adds Cheah.
“Any graduating AI/ML PhD could reimplement Simple Jev from one sentence. I expect hundreds more open source Jev clones.”
Featherless is also introducing free public endpoints, which it says will let developers test classification models without API keys or logins (the demo is capped at 2,000 tokens of context and two requests per second). For production use, Simple Jev pricing starts at $0.03 per million input tokens, with output tokens free, compared with TypeSafe’s $0.042 per million input tokens for Jev. That is a beta floor price that may rise, and Featherless’s own listings put its Qwen-based classifiers at $0.28 and $0.30 per million input tokens. So is that expensive, or as cheap as a Little Caesars pizza deal?
“It’s almost too cheap to meter in a literal sense,” details Cheah. “Let’s say a typical decision when classifying an image/paragraph of text is roughly 500 to 1,200 tokens, so at $0.03 per million you’re paying about three thousandths of a cent for a decision. To put that in perspective, that’s about $15–35 per million decisions. And the output is free, too.”
Moving on from monolithic generalist models
Urging us to move on from what it has called “monolithic generalist models,” Featherless has offered its latest tooling, promising that millions of lightweight, dedicated models will drive the future.
“First they said open models would never catch up. Then they said open only wins in isolated cases. Soon they’ll be saying closed models only win in isolated cases,” adds Cheah.
As the Featherless CEO conceded, classifiers are not new. As a sub-classification of model toolset engineering, other zero-shot vision and multi-modal classification technologies have been around for a while.
Other models that work in the zero-shot arena
First introduced in early 2021, OpenAI’s CLIP might reasonably be called an early open pioneer for zero-shot image classification. The model learns visual concepts from natural language supervision and can be applied to any visual classification benchmark.
Microsoft’s Florence-2 arrived in summer 2024 as an open-weight vision-language foundation model. It promised to overcome the complexities of “spatial hierarchy and semantic granularity” and is said to be well-suited to zero-shot and fine-tuning tasks, including visual object detection, grounding and segmentation, and image captioning. Other contenders in the zero-shot visual tagging and object classification arena include Roboflow and Mixpeek.
“Everyone in this space is standing on each other’s shoulders; that’s how open source works. CLIP and the rest are great tools that changed the industry. We’re bringing an old idea back with today’s models, because sometimes you don’t need the tank; you need something small and fast,” concludes Cheah.
Simple Jev is now available as a fully open-source library on GitHub. Featherless says it offers developers a dedicated model distillation workflow (a process that transfers capabilities from large frontier models into smaller, efficient architectures) to compress complex prompts and decisions from large frontier models into smaller, highly efficient open models for production.

articles.title: Technics Introduces the EAH-A1000 Flagship Wireless Headphones, a New Standard in Premium Listening
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
	
	
	
Technics Introduces the EAH-A1000 Flagship Wireless Headphones, a New Standard in Premium Listening
Technics today announced the EAH-A1000, its new flagship wireless headphones. Built around a newly developed 40 mm Magnetic Fluid Driver, the EAH-A1000 brings together acoustic technologies derived from Technics speaker development, a new generation of Adaptive Noise Cancelling and the newly designed Flow Arm. The model brings Technics' long-standing sound philosophy to personal audio for listeners seeking a greater music experience.
Elevating Personal Listening Through Technics Acoustic Technologies
Technics approach to sound has always centered on faithfully reproducing music with careful attention to avoiding excessive coloration. The EAH-A1000 continues that philosophy, seeking to reproduce the atmosphere of the original performance, the attack and decay of each note and the sense of space to draw listeners more deeply into the music. To achieve this, Technics reconsidered every element of its over-ear headphone, including the driver mechanism, diaphragm material, surround structure, acoustic design, and the fit and seal around the ears.Newly Developed 40 mm Magnetic Fluid Driver Reproduces Music with Clarity and Accuracy
In developing the EAH-A1000, Technics set out to combine low-distortion music reproduction with the expansive soundstage and sense of scale offered by over-ear headphones. Precise driver control was essential to that goal.
Larger-diameter drivers are generally more difficult to control, as even slight tilting or misalignment of the moving diaphragm, or flexing of the diaphragm itself, can create distortion. To address this challenge, the EAH-A1000 uses a newly developed 40 mm Magnetic Fluid Driver, drawing from Technics magnetic fluid technology which has been previously employed in its in-ear models, including the EAH-TZ700 and EAH-AZ100.
Magnetic fluid is a functional material with both magnetic and liquid properties. Placed between the voice coil and driver magnet, it supports precise driver movement. This helps suppress unwanted vibration and distortion that can occur in large-diameter drivers, enabling high-precision music reproduction.SST Edge and Pure Carbon Fiber Diaphragm Deliver Accurate, High-Resolution Sound
To further enhance the performance of the 40 mm Magnetic Fluid Driver, the EAH-A1000 incorporates an SST (Symmetrical Surround Technology) Edge, also used in Technics Hi-fi flagship speakers. By improving the symmetry of the edge's back and forth movement as it supports the diaphragm, the design minimizes distortion.
The diaphragm uses lightweight, rigid carbon fiber. Its cone shape also helps suppress the flexing that can occur in a large-diameter diaphragm, supporting fast response and stable movement.
Together, these technologies better preserve the sense of scale in the bass and the spacious soundstage associated with over-ear headphones while reproducing music more faithfully created by any artist.
Designed for Natural, Spacious Presentation Without Compromising the Sound Field
The EAH-A1000 also features a redesigned acoustic path that better preserves the air movement generated by the driver, all the way to the ear.
A new Baffle Flat Structure reduces uneven surfaces around the driver to limit unwanted reflections and create a more natural sound field with clear imaging.
Behind the driver, an Acoustic Control Chamber better manages airflow. By balancing the low and midrange frequencies, it delivers a more balanced sound without overemphasizing a specific frequency range.
Adaptive Noise Cancelling Supports Immersive Listening
The EAH-A1000 features Adaptive Noise Cancelling, which seeks to optimize noise-canceling performance based on ambient noise and the fit of the headphones. Three feed-forward microphones and one feedback microphone on each side detect and suppress noise entering from different directions. From listening at home to traveling, the system helps create an environment that allows listeners to immerse themselves fully in music.
Premium Design Balances a Lightweight Look with Elegance
The EAH-A1000 introduces a more modern, refined design for a flagship model. The new Flow Arm uses a distinctive structure that transitions from a square shape at the slider to a triangular shape at the hanger. Its single-sided support design pairs with Technics' signature circular housings for a light, streamlined appearance.
Metal is used for the arm and the top panels of the housings, with a finish that highlights the material's natural character. The design also carries forward the circular machining associated with Technics headphones as an expression of the brand's identity.
The EAH-A1000 will be offered in Black and Platinum Greige. New to the line, Platinum Greige is a soft tone that blends gray and beige. It offers a more premium finish designed to complement fashion and everyday style.
Comfortable Fit for Extended Listening
The fit has also been completely re-engineered. An optimized range of ear cup movement, a refined headband shape, and improved slider-based position adjustability distribute pressure evenly across the head, reducing strain. The design accommodates a range of head shapes.
The ear pads use high-density memory foam designed to balance durability and comfort during extended listening.
Technology and Usability for Longer, Immersive Listening Sessions
The EAH-A1000 supports high-resolution audio playback via LDAC and USB Audio. It also offers up to 45 hours of continuous playback and multipoint connectivity with up to three devices. Physical buttons and a slide control provide intuitive operation.
From everyday listening to long-distance travel, the EAH-A1000 is designed for a wide range of listening occasions. It delivers an enhanced listening experience through more exceptional sound quality, lasting comfort and intuitive convenience.

articles.title: Karnataka approves Global Technology Centres in Belagavi and Hubballi
articles.text:
Karnataka approves Global Technology Centres in Belagavi and Hubballi
Karnataka approves Global Technology Centres in Belagavi and Hubballi as the state expands its tech ecosystem beyond Bengaluru.
Karnataka is expanding its technology infrastructure beyond Bengaluru, with the state government approving Global Technology Centres (GTCs) in Belagavi and Hubballi.
The move comes as the state prepares to showcase its growing AI and deeptech ecosystem at Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026.
Announced on September 29, the two GTCs will be established under the Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP), with the government aiming to give local talent, startups and technology-driven enterprises access to infrastructure closer to home.
Two new centres for North Karnataka
The Belagavi GTC will be set up across approximately 10,000 sq ft at Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU), with plug-and-play facilities. The project will cost Rs 82.80 lakh over three years, with Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) as the implementing agency.
The Hubballi centre will also cover around 10,000 sq ft at the Hubballi IT Park, on rent-free premises. It will involve Rs 5.80 crore in expenditure over three years, including Rs 4.90 crore in capital expenditure and Rs 90 lakh in operational expenditure.
KDEM will implement the Hubballi project, while Karnataka Rural Infrastructure Development Limited (KRIDL) will undertake the infrastructure development.
Both centres will be funded through LEAP's allocation for creating incubators and accelerators. The programme has a total allocation of Rs 1,000 crore over five years, with Rs 200 crore approved for the first year and Rs 110 crore earmarked for incubators and accelerators.
The 2025-26 state Budget had already announced GTCs through Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation (KEONICS) in Mangaluru, Hubballi and Belagavi, with plug-and-play facilities.
The government says the centres will strengthen links between educational institutions, startups, technology companies and industry while creating opportunities for local talent and technology enterprises.
AI and robotics take centre stage at BTS 2026
The move comes as Karnataka prepares for the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, scheduled for November 17–19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre under the theme ‘AI & Beyond’.
A dedicated AI and Robotics Pavilion will span more than 50,000 sq ft and is expected to bring together nearly 101 robotics and drone startups. The pavilion will feature humanoid robots, quadruped racing, autonomous systems, warehouse drones, industrial AI robots and an AI Digital Twin Simulator of Bengaluru.
The space will also include live demonstration zones, startup exhibits, a robotics racing arena, research displays and a pitchathon stage. The focus will be on technologies that take AI beyond software and into physical systems that can perceive, process information, navigate and act.
BTS 2026 is expected to bring together more than 1,800 exhibitors, 1,000 technology startups and 25,000 delegates from India and overseas.
Together, the GTCs and the summit reflect two parts of Karnataka's technology push: building infrastructure and startup ecosystems outside Bengaluru while continuing to position the state capital as a meeting point for emerging technologies and global investment.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship finally reaches orbit and puts 26 Starlink satellites into space
articles.text:
What just happened? SpaceX's Starship reached orbit for the first time Monday and released 26 of the company's newest Starlink satellites, a milestone that gives the rocket a direct role in expanding SpaceX's broadband network. The flight was Starship's 14th test mission and its first to complete a full orbital insertion. It also marked the first time SpaceX placed commercial-grade Starlink V3 satellites into orbit. The spacecraft are too large for Falcon 9, making Starship essential to their deployment.
Starship lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility in South Texas as its Super Heavy booster, powered by 33 Raptor engines, sent the 407-foot rocket east over the Gulf of Mexico. The booster separated from Starship and turned back toward the Texas coast, later splashing down in the Gulf.
Starship continued into space, but the launch was not without trouble. One of the six Raptor engines on the upper stage shut down early. Two engines on Super Heavy also appeared to fail, one during ascent and another during the booster's return.
The upper stage had enough momentum to follow the suborbital path SpaceX had used on earlier tests. Reaching orbit, however, required restarting a Raptor engine after the main ascent burn. SpaceX paused before committing to the maneuver while controllers reviewed the engine issue.
One of Starship's Raptor engines restarted for 19 seconds, adding about 204 mph to the vehicle's speed. That was enough to place Starship into an orbit about 171 miles above Earth.
The orbit was important because it let SpaceX deploy the payload. Starship released 26 Starlink V3 satellites through a cargo-bay deployment system that pushed the flat-packed spacecraft out one at a time. SpaceX said it contacted all 26 satellites after separation.
The V3 satellites are significantly larger than the Starlink spacecraft Falcon 9 carries today. Each weighs about 2 metric tons at launch and includes larger solar arrays and upgraded antennas. SpaceX says each can add 1 terabit per second of network capacity, about 10 times the capacity of older Starlink satellites.
Starship can eventually carry as many as 60 V3 satellites on one mission. Falcon 9 cannot launch them because they do not fit inside its payload fairing.
The new spacecraft are expected to expand broadband capacity and strengthen Starlink's direct-to-device service. Future V3 satellites could also support Starshield, SpaceX's government-focused satellite business.
SpaceX flew Starlink V3 satellites on a previous Starship test in July, but that mission followed a suborbital course. The satellites reentered soon after their release. Monday's launch was the first time the company could send V3 satellites into an orbit where they could join the constellation.
SpaceX said the new satellites could begin service within weeks.
 – Elon Musk (@elonmusk) September 28, 2026
After deploying the satellites, SpaceX shortened the planned mission because of the engine issue during ascent. The company fired Starship's engines for a deorbit burn and targeted a pre-cleared splashdown area in the northern Pacific Ocean.
"Out of an abundance of caution given the engine issue experienced during ascent, the flight control team decided to limit the duration spent on orbit and proceeded with de-orbiting Starship to a splashdown location in the northern Pacific Ocean," SpaceX said.
Starship reentered over the Pacific and endured temperatures of up to 2,600 degrees Fahrenheit. It descended belly-first, then flipped upright for a landing burn before splashing down near Hawaii roughly three hours after liftoff. The vehicle tipped over and broke apart after reaching the water, as SpaceX expected.
The mission gave SpaceX a strong result despite the engine failures. Starship reached orbit, deployed satellites and completed a controlled deorbit and reentry. At the same time, the flight added to a growing list of issues with the Raptor 3 engine.
SpaceX has reported engine problems on all three Starship flights using Raptor 3. The newer engine is designed with fewer parts, lower mass and higher thrust. Elon Musk said the simpler design is harder to refine and repair.
 – SpaceX (@SpaceX) September 28, 2026
"While deleting parts sounds easy in theory, it is actually very difficult to figure out how to do so in practice and requires many iterations," Musk wrote.
The Federal Aviation Administration will not require a formal mishap investigation, saying the flight events fell within authorized activities. SpaceX is preparing more Starship flights from Texas and is activating a new launch site at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The next tests are expected to include longer orbital missions, in-orbit refueling and, eventually, attempts to return Starship to Starbase for recovery by the launch tower's mechanical arms. But the vehicle's most immediate use is likely to be Starlink. SpaceX now has a way to launch the larger satellites it has been building, even as it works through the remaining Raptor issues.

articles.title: Oracle CISO puts humans at the center of AI security governance - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Oracle CISO puts humans at the center of AI security governance
As enterprises face AI-driven cyberattacks, AI security governance must control autonomous systems that can reach data, connect applications and act on users’ behalf. That makes human accountability a core security requirement.
Traditional controls remain necessary, but security teams must also understand the data flows and processes agents create. People, therefore, need a new role in supervising consequential actions, according to Brennan Baybeck (pictured), senior vice president and chief information security officer of Oracle Customer Success at Oracle Corp.
“Humans have never been more critical to help control these robots, as we call them,” he said. “We used to say humans are the weakest link. But now what I’m saying is that robots are the most powerful and potentially dangerous link, and humans are now an essential link.”
Baybeck talked with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at Oracle’s “AI Cyberattacks Are Escalating: How to Secure Your Data Now” event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed human oversight of AI agents, AI security governance and the shared responsibility between customers and technology providers. (* Disclosure below.)
AI security governance returns to first principles
That oversight must rest on basic controls, including least privilege, authorization, network segmentation and monitoring. Yet Baybeck sees three recurring gaps as organizations put AI into production.
“There’s definitely some patterns that we’re seeing, and there’s three of them that I want to highlight,” he said. “The first one is a lack of a solid foundational governance program for AI. The second one is not having the security basics in place to start with, especially in their Oracle ecosystems. And then not understanding the shared security responsibility model when it comes to AI services with service providers.”
The shared model assigns security duties to both providers and customers. At the same time, AI can help security teams produce policies, standards and assessment tools faster, Baybeck added.
“Security professionals can leverage AI and actually create a governance program, associated policies, standards, processes and best practices in a matter of hours,” he said. “There is no excuse anymore of why we don’t have a governance program in place at any company because you can literally use AI services to create that and have a very well-thought-out and deployable governance program.”

articles.title: Vigilance rouge dans le Gard et l'Hérault : un épisode méditerranéen « remarquable, voire exceptionnel » frappe le sud-est
articles.text:
Le dispositif FR-Alert a été de nouveau déclenché en France. Ce mercredi 30 septembre 2026, la préfecture du Gard a envoyé un message d’alerte sur tous les téléphones situés dans le département. La préfecture transmet ainsi plusieurs consignes, demandant aux habitants de rester chez eux, de ne pas utiliser leur véhicule, et d’évacuer seulement si les autorités en donnent l’ordre.
À l’origine de ces consignes et de cette mise en garde, une vigilance rouge pluie-inondation dans le Gard ainsi que dans l’Hérault, émise ce mercredi depuis 8 heures. Météo-France décrit une situation météorologique nécessitant une vigilance absolue : « Orages et forts cumuls de pluie d’abord sur les Cévennes puis s’étendant aux plaines, permettant de parler d’épisode méditerranéen remarquable, voire exceptionnel sur le Gard et est de l’Hérault », peut-on lire dans le bulletin publié avant midi ce mercredi.
Un épisode cévenol en cours en France : de quoi s’agit-il ?
C’est un épisode cévenol, qui correspond au blocage de pluies intenses sur le massif des Cévennes. Plus largement, on parle d’épisode méditerranéen, quand de très fortes précipitations (l’équivalent de plusieurs mois de pluie) touchent les départements du pourtour de la Méditerranée, sur une durée très brève (1 à 24h).
Ces épisodes surviennent surtout à l’automne, trois à six fois par an en moyenne, selon Météo-France. Celui de ce mercredi est le premier de la saison, qui s’étend généralement de septembre à décembre (le dernier s’était produit en décembre 2025).
Keraunos, l’Observatoire français des tornades et des orages violents, confirme dans son bulletin ce « risque orageux marqué à sévère du Languedoc jusqu’à l’ouest du Var ». En fin de matinée, l’observatoire a souligné des « cumuls localisés atteignant 300 mm [qui] sont relevés dans le Gard, à Saint-Hippolyte-du-Fort » et une « humidité de la masse d’air […] remarquable » dans la zone.
La situation inquiète aussi le spécialiste en agroclimatologie Serge Zaka. « Les dernières prévisions sont terrifiantes entre 300 à 400 mm de pluie en plaine et en villes. La population est invitée à se confiner chez elle », a-t-il écrit sur X ce mercredi.
Vigilance requise, les conseils à suivre impérativement
Comme le rappelle Météo-France, les fortes précipitations représentent un risque réel. Les dangers sont divers : inondations par ruissellement et par débordement des cours d’eau, glissements de terrain, coulées de boues et de débris. C’est pourquoi il est crucial d’éviter les déplacements, de se tenir éloignés des cours d’eau, de ne pas s’engager sur des routes immergées, de rester informés de la situation et de disposer d’un kit urgence.
Une comparaison, diffusée sur Bluesky ce mercredi matin par Sébastien Brana, vice-président de l’association Info-Climat, montre la vitesse de la montée des eaux. Un des membres de l’association a installé une caméra « à la confluence de l’Argentesse (à gauche) [et] du Vidourle (à droite) ». Un petit pont, que l’on distinguait encore mardi sur la photo, est couvert ce mercredi par la montée des eaux. « La caméra va probablement être emportée dans les minutes qui viennent… », s’inquiète Sébastien Brana.
Des événements qui deviennent plus intenses et plus fréquents
Le changement climatique renforce l’intensité de ces épisodes méditerranéens. Selon Météo-France, ces événements sont plus intenses aujourd’hui que dans les années 1960. « Les évènements les plus extrêmes sont également plus fréquents. Dans le climat futur, on s’attend à une augmentation de l’intensité de ces évènements. »
À l’horizon 2100, dans une France à +4 °C, « les précipitations intenses pourraient augmenter de 15 % en moyenne sur la France, avec des hausses allant jusqu’à 20 % sur la moitié nord du pays », selon la trajectoire de réchauffement de référence retenue par l’État (TRACC), citée par Météo-France.

articles.title: Google and Henry Cavill are making a video game to promote Googlebook
articles.text:
Google has partnered with former Superman and The Witcher star Henry Cavill to create a video game using Googlebook. The collaboration is intended to promote the new Android-powered laptop line that’s designed specifically for Google Intelligence.
Google didn’t provide any details on what this game will actually be, but presumably, it will involve at least some AI use given the Googlebook’s focus on the technology. In a blog post, Google mentioned that Cavill was approached because of his well-documented love of both video games and PCs. (It’s worth noting that he’s also been a fan of Google phones going back at least until the Pixel 2.)
“After being hands on and spending some time with their team, I believe this has the potential to be the start of something rather special,” said Cavill in a statement to Google. “Time and technology are marching forward at a breakneck pace, this, and all that Google are trying to do with it, has the whispers of the next generation.”
Google says Cavill’s game will be revealed in November. For now, the company says to stay tuned to this dedicated website for updates.

articles.title: Blockchain-assisted cyberattacks surge fivefold, driven by Iranian and North Korean state actors, Russia-linked groups
articles.text:
Blockchain-assisted cyberattacks surge fivefold, driven by Iranian and North Korean state actors, Russia-linked groups — open-weight LLMs are linked to an increase in attacks
Blockchain dead drops technique stores malicious payloads on blockchains
Blockchain-assisted cyberattacks have risen more than fivefold since last year, driven largely by North Korean and Iranian nation-state actors and Russian-speaking criminal groups, according to a report by blockchain data and intelligence platform Chainalysis. Rather than storing malicious payloads on servers that are susceptible to disruption, the attackers store them on public, censorship-immune blockchains. The technique, named Blockchain Dead Drops (BDD), stores payloads in on-chain transactions and smart contracts where infected devices can retrieve them on demand.
What makes BDD particularly dangerous is that it gives cyberattack campaigns unprecedented durability. Because blockchain data is public, immutable, and replicated worldwide, takedowns become immensely difficult. Threat actors can use this resilient infrastructure for command and control without worrying about losing the layer to domain seizures, repository removals, hosting takedowns, and additional disruptions.
The report notes that the widespread availability of Chinese open-source AI tools has significantly lowered the technical barrier to entry for cybercrime. Meaning that less-experienced attackers can now launch complex cyberattacks, which is linked to a reported 440% rise in BDD attacks.
Understanding the Blockchain Dead Drops technique
While blockchain dead drops vary across cyberattack campaigns, attackers typically store either malware payloads or dynamic command-and-control (C2) configuration pointers on the blockchain itself. In C2 setups, the on-chain data does not carry out the attack. Instead, it holds configuration information, such as domains, IP addresses, or other pointers, that direct compromised devices to the attacker’s current infrastructure. Malware on the victim's machine retrieves and decodes this data, which then connects to the real C2 server off-chain, where subsequent commands and malicious activity take place.
In payload-delivery setups, attackers store malicious code or encrypted payload components on-chain for victim machines to retrieve and execute locally. In both cases, once the malware has what it needs, the operation moves off-chain, where the attacker executes the actual compromise, which, depending on the campaign, can mean infostealers targeting crypto wallets and credentials, or remote access trojans that give attackers persistent control over systems.
Chainalysis identified several techniques threat actors use to hide malware on-chain, primarily using transaction-based storage and contract-based storage. In transaction-based storage, attackers publish C2 configurations, payload references, or infrastructure pointers inside blockchain transactions for malware to retrieve later, embedding the data in fields such as memos or calldata. This can occur on a single chain or spread across several blockchains.
On the other hand, contract-based storage uses smart contracts as resilient storage for the same kinds of data, with the contract's state holding the current C2 pointer. This is the model behind EtherHiding, where malware queries the contract for up-to-date information, while the attackers' visible on-chain activity is typically limited to deploying and periodically updating the contract.
Beyond these two approaches, threat actors continue to develop new, less detectable ways to hide malicious data on-chain. One such technique involves “phantom wallets”, blockchain addresses that have no corresponding private key. Instead of placing their C2 server's IP address in a transaction or smart contract, attackers encode it directly into the bytes of the wallet address itself, then send zero-value transactions to that address. Malware on the victim's machine is programmed to decode the IP address from the phantom wallet and connect to the attacker's C2 server.
Nation-state actors are driving a surge in attacks
The BDD technique has been around for over a decade. One of the earliest instances was in 2013, when a Necurs botnet variant stored its C2 domain info on Namecoin, a Bitcoin fork. Then, in 2019, attackers encoded C2 IP addresses for banking malware into Bitcoin transactions. That same year, Glupteba crypto-mining botnet stored malicious info in Bitcoin’s OP_RETURN field.
EtherHiding, the implementation of BDD on EVM chains, began in Mid-2023, following Cloudflare crackdowns that blocked their infostealer malware distribution servers. The ClearFake malware crew moved malicious code into smart contracts on the BNB Smart Chain. This allowed the campaign to keep going, as the chain couldn't be taken offline. Within days, other groups began testing ways to replicate the move, and by late December 2023, the Smargaft DDoS botnet was also using smart contract-based C2 on BSC.
State-level actors entered the scene in 2024, when Iranian actors linked to the country's Ministry of Intelligence first embedded C2 data in Bitcoin transactions. By 2025, North Korean actors began using EtherHiding in fake job interview campaigns. Since then, daily malicious blockchain writes have increased from 2.06 to 11.1, a 440% increase that Chainalysis attributes to AI. Before the launch of powerful open-weight Chinese LLMs — which can be uncensored through a process known as abliteration — building effective BDDs required substantial cybersecurity and crypto experience. Now, far less experienced threat actors can deploy BDDs easily.
Tracking BDD activity across five major blockchains and over a dozen named malware strains, Chainalysis reports that by Q2 2026, “state-actor-linked groups were responsible for roughly two-thirds of new BDD activity each quarter, and half of total BDD activity,” despite only just entering the scene in mid-2024. The campaigns are being perpetrated by Iranian, North Korean, and Russian-speaking operators.
Circumventing blockchain dead drops
A seemingly obvious fix, blocking blockchain traffic, is out of the question. For example, cutting off Ethereum access would mean blocking every public RPC endpoint that providers such as Cloudflare and Alchemy run. This would also impact legitimate wallets and DeFi services. Even then, the attackers could just go back to running their own nodes off-chain. Similarly, restricting what can be written to a public blockchain at the protocol level is impractical, as the fundamental changes this would require would likely cause more harm than the malware.
This leaves detection, identifying the attackers, and disrupting the off-chain parts of the operation as the only viable options. In this case, the same blockchain properties that make BDD attractive to attackers work against them. Every time an operator rotates infrastructure by publishing a new transaction or updating a contract, the change is permanently recorded and timestamped on a public ledger. By tracing operator wallets, resolver contracts, funding sources, and update histories, investigators can link seemingly unrelated campaigns back to the same actors.
For organizations, one practical early-warning signal is outbound JSON-RPC traffic to public blockchain endpoints, particularly from machines with no legitimate reason to query a blockchain. A workstation or build server reading data from a smart contract should probably sound some warning bells. The technique also maps to an existing MITRE ATT&CK entry, T1102.001 (Web Service: Dead Drop Resolver), giving security teams an established framework for building detections.
In the case of individuals, it's important to note that BDD comes into play only after something malicious is already running on a device. The blockchain tells the malware where to go next, but it doesn't get the malware onto the machine in the first place. North Korea's fake job interview campaigns, for example, still require developers to first download and run malicious code. Therefore, being wary of unsolicited outreach — especially when it involves coding tests that require running unfamiliar repositories — remains the first and most effective line of defense.
Etiido Uko is a news contributor for Tom's Hardware covering the latest updates in big tech and the PC industry. He is a mechanical engineer and senior technical writer with over nine years of experience in documentation and reporting. He is deeply passionate about all things engineering and technology, and is an expert in gadgets, manufacturing, robotics, automotive, and aerospace.

articles.title: 'We really wanted the Operators to feel unique and to serve unique purposes' — Rainbow Six Tactics director says it was 'crucial' to design its 15 Operators with 'unique gadgets, playstyles, and progression' so they didn't 'overlap' with each other
articles.text:
Rainbow Six Tactics game director says the game's 15 Operators have 'unique' loadouts so they didn't 'overlap' with each other — but there was still room for 'community favorites' and 'operators that were impossible to not include'
The director says it was important to include fan-favorite Operators
- Rainbow Six Tactics game director Martial Potron says it was "crucial" that the development team designed a unique roster of Operators
- Each of the 15 Operators has unique gadgets, playstyles, and progression to avoid "overlap"
- He says it would have been "impossible" not to feature fan favorites like Ash and Sledge
Rainbow Six Tactics game director Martial Potron has said that it was important for Ubisoft to design the game's Operators with unique loadouts and progression to avoid overlap.
"My team really wanted the operators to feel unique and to serve unique places," Potron told TechRadar Gaming at Gamescom. "It was part of the creative process to make sure that every Operator would serve one turf course in the experience, so we really made sure that all Operators were unique: unique gadgets, unique playstyles, unique progression. It was crucial for us, in fact, that we didn't have too much overlap with other Operators."
The upcoming turn-based tactics spin-off will offer 15 Operators in total, with Ash, Sledge, Glaz, Montagne, Doc, and Nokk confirmed so far, and you won't be able to play them repeatedly due to the game's new gameplay systems. While that's far from the entire roster fans are familiar with in the core series, Potron explained that it was also important to include "community favorites."
"We really did the operators that were impossible not to have, [like] Sledge and Ash," the game director said, adding that there are a few that he's personally disappointed aren't included.
"I love Tachanka. We don't have Tachanka; we don't have Lion." Potron said. "We had to make [tough] choices. It's part of my job to make [tough] choices."
As for the possibility of adding more Operators in the future, Potron said there are no current plans to do so, saying, "For the launch, it's not something we are digging into. We are very close to releasing a fantastic single-player experience, and so [we're] focused on the release date; shipping something amazing, and we'll see [about] the future."
Rainbow Six Tactics releases in 2027 for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S.

articles.title: KI-Agenten für KMU: So entlastet Agentic AI den Mittelstand
articles.text:
Warum KI-Agenten für KMU jetzt relevant werden
Der Mittelstand steht unter Druck: knappe Ressourcen, komplexere Lieferketten, mehr Dokumentationspflichten und steigende Erwartungen an Geschwindigkeit. Genau hier können KI-Agenten ansetzen. Sie übernehmen nicht einfach einzelne Textaufgaben, sondern können Informationen bündeln, Daten prüfen und Arbeitsschritte beschleunigen.
Eine aktuelle YouGov-Umfrage im Auftrag von Alibaba.com und dem Bundesverband E-Commerce und Versandhandel (bevh) zeigt: Rund ein Drittel der KMU sieht administrative Überlastung als konkretes Problem. Rund 40 Prozent nennen Auftragsabwicklung und Kundenservice als besonders zeitintensive Bereiche. Mehr als die Hälfte der KMU ab zehn Mitarbeitern sieht zudem das Potenzial, durch KI-Agenten mindestens zehn Prozent operativer Routineaufgaben einzusparen.
Vom Admin-Overload zu mehr Entscheidungsstärke
Der größte Hebel liegt dort, wo Unternehmen heute besonders viel Zeit verlieren: in fragmentierten Informationen, wiederkehrenden Prüfungen und manuellen Abstimmungen. KI-Agenten können Daten aus verschiedenen Quellen zusammenführen, Dokumente vorstrukturieren, Kriterien abgleichen und nächste Schritte vorbereiten oder ausführen.
Das entlastet Teams im Tagesgeschäft und schafft bessere Grundlagen für Entscheidungen. Besonders relevant ist das in Bereichen wie Auftragsabwicklung, Kundenservice, Compliance, Produktrecherche, Angebotsvorbereitung und internationaler Beschaffung.
Jüngere Entscheider treiben die Nutzung voran
Besonders dynamisch ist die Entwicklung bei jüngeren Führungskräften. In der Gruppe der unter 35-Jährigen nutzen mehr als 62 Prozent bereits Agentic AI. Gleichzeitig investiert in dieser Altersgruppe fast jeder Vierte gezielt in KI-Weiterbildung und ein Drittel sieht ohne KI-Agenten mittelfristig Risiken für die eigene Wettbewerbsfähigkeit. Auch beim Vertrauen in KI-gestützte Ergebnisse liegen jüngere Entscheider klar vorn, etwa bei der Prüfung von Produktinformationen, Lieferantenangaben oder der Vorbereitung von Geschäftsdokumenten. Die Entwicklung ist damit weniger ein Hinweis auf Zurückhaltung im Mittelstand als vielmehr ein positives Signal: Eine neue Generation von Entscheidern zeigt, wie schnell KI-Agenten vom Experiment zum produktiven Werkzeug werden können.
Accio: Agentische KI für den B2B-Alltag
Accio zeigt, wie dieser Wandel praktisch aussehen kann. Die Agentic AI-Plattform unterstützt Unternehmen dabei, Produktideen zu entwickeln, Markt- und Trenddaten zu analysieren, Lieferanteninformationen zu vergleichen, Spezifikationen und Zertifikate schneller einzuordnen und Geschäftsprozesse von Anfang bis Ende zu automatisieren.
Damit adressiert Accio zentrale Engpässe im B2B-Alltag: Recherche, Datenabgleich, Dokumentenprüfung, Angebotsvorbereitung und Beschaffungsentscheidungen. Unternehmen gewinnen Zeit, reduzieren Routineaufwand und können sich stärker auf Bewertung, Strategie und Wachstum konzentrieren.
Alibaba.com lädt Unternehmer aus Deutschland und ganz Europa ein, diese technologischen Möglichkeiten durch den CoCreate Pitch Europe in die Praxis umzusetzen. Der Startup-Wettbewerb unterstützt kleine Unternehmen dabei, den nächsten Schritt in der KI-Nutzung zu gehen. In diesem Jahr werden alle Bewerbungen über Accio eingereicht, von der Marktforschung über Produktideen bis hin zur Bewertung geschäftlicher Chancen. Die europäischen Finalrunden finden am 19. und 20. November in London statt. Weitere Informationen finden Sie auf der Event-Seite zum CoCreate Pitch.
Fazit: Die Chance liegt im Jetzt
Für den Mittelstand liegt die Chance nicht in einem radikalen Bruch, sondern in einem pragmatischen Produktivitätsschub. Wachstumsstarke KMU und jüngere Entscheider machen bereits vor, wie KI-Agenten operative Arbeit erleichtern können. Wer jetzt erste Anwendungsfelder identifiziert, kann Effizienzpotenziale heben, bevor aus Vorsprung Nachholbedarf wird.

articles.title: Papelera de WhatsApp: cómo vaciarla y qué archivos se pueden borrar del celular
articles.text:
La papelera de WhatsApp funciona como un espacio de almacenamiento intermedio en el que se acumulan fotos, videos, audios y documentos que parecían eliminados, pero todavía ocupan memoria en el celular. Revisarla permite identificar contenido innecesario y liberar espacio sin borrar conversaciones completas.
Para encontrarla, hay que ingresar a WhatsApp, tocar “Ajustes”, ir a “Almacenamiento y datos” y seleccionar “Administración de almacenamiento”.
PUBLICIDAD
Allí aparece debajo de la sección “Revisa y elimina elementos”, desde donde se pueden revisar los archivos que permanecen guardados en la aplicación.
Para borrar contenido, se debe pulsar “Seleccionar”, elegir los archivos deseados y tocar el ícono de la papelera. Esta sección también permite recuperar un archivo eliminado por error antes de que se borre de forma definitiva.
Qué se puede borrar de la papelera de WhatsApp
En esta sección se pueden eliminar fotos, videos, audios y documentos que siguen almacenados en el teléfono. Con el uso diario de la aplicación, esos archivos pueden acumularse y ocupar una cantidad considerable de espacio.
Los videos suelen ser uno de los contenidos que más memoria consumen, especialmente cuando fueron enviados en grupos activos o se descargaron de forma automática. Los documentos, los audios y los GIF también pueden aumentar el espacio que utiliza WhatsApp.
PUBLICIDAD
Antes de borrar archivos, conviene revisarlos para evitar eliminar fotos, videos o documentos que todavía puedan ser necesarios. Una limpieza periódica ayuda a mantener la aplicación más liviana y a optimizar el rendimiento del celular.
Qué otras formas hay de ahorrar espacio en WhatsApp
Los grupos con mucha actividad suelen concentrar una gran cantidad de archivos multimedia. Revisar los chats más activos y eliminar contenido pesado o repetido permite reducir el espacio que ocupa la aplicación.
Es posible modificar la configuración de descarga automática de archivos. En “Almacenamiento y datos”, WhatsApp permite desactivar la descarga automática de determinados contenidos, como videos o documentos, para evitar que se acumulen sin que el usuario lo advierta.
PUBLICIDAD
Las copias de seguridad de las conversaciones también pueden incluir archivos multimedia y ocupar espacio tanto en el teléfono como en la nube. Revisar la configuración de los respaldos ayuda a evitar que crezcan de manera sostenida.
Por qué WhatsApp consume espacio en el celular
WhatsApp guarda los archivos que se reciben y envían en los chats, incluidos fotos, videos, notas de voz, documentos, GIF y stickers. Cuanto mayor es la actividad en grupos y conversaciones, más contenido puede quedar almacenado en el dispositivo.
El problema puede extenderse a otros elementos del teléfono. Eliminar aplicaciones que no se usan, borrar contenido duplicado de la galería y mover fotos o videos a servicios en la nube, como Google Fotos o iCloud, son opciones para recuperar capacidad de almacenamiento.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, los datos temporales de las apps pueden ocupar varios gigabytes con el tiempo. Limpiar la caché de las aplicaciones permite liberar espacio y mejorar el funcionamiento general del celular.
Qué nuevas funciones hay en WhatsApp
WhatsApp incorporó nuevas funciones para mejorar las llamadas, reforzar la seguridad de las cuentas y facilitar la gestión de conversaciones desde distintos dispositivos.
Entre las actualizaciones más recientes, la aplicación permite hacer y recibir llamadas de audio y video desde WhatsApp Web, tanto individuales como grupales. La versión para navegadores incluye opciones como compartir pantalla, enviar reacciones, consultar el historial de llamadas y acceder a contactos favoritos.
La plataforma también habilitó la transferencia de llamadas activas entre dispositivos, una sala de espera para enlaces de llamadas grupales, video en alta definición desde los primeros segundos y una herramienta de supresión de ruido para mejorar el audio en entornos ruidosos.
PUBLICIDAD
En los grupos, WhatsApp sumó encuestas con horario de cierre, la posibilidad de ocultar los nombres de quienes votan y una opción para editar la pregunta durante los primeros 15 minutos. También incorporó la mención @all para notificar a todos los integrantes de un chat.
Para liberar memoria, la aplicación permite localizar y eliminar archivos grandes desde cada conversación, sin borrar el historial del chat. Además, los usuarios pueden tener dos cuentas activas en un mismo iPhone y transferir el historial entre dispositivos iOS y Android.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Le Poco X8 est meilleur et moins cher que le Redmi Note 17 Pro si vous vous fichez de l'ultra grand-angle — Frandroid
articles.text:
Présenté le 1er septembre en même temps que les Poco F9 Pro et F9 Ultra, le Poco X8 est disponible en France depuis ce mercredi 30 septembre sur la boutique en ligne de Xiaomi. Poco mise tout sur sa batterie de 8 340 mAh, soit 63 % de plus que les 5 110 mAh du Poco X7 sorti en janvier 2025. Par contre, le prix a grimpé lui aussi. Le Poco X7 démarrait à 323 euros en 8 Go + 256 Go, alors que le X8 est affiché à 403 euros dans la même configuration.
Poco est une marque de Xiaomi, connue pour ses smartphones bien équipés à prix serrés. Jusqu’au 7 octobre, une offre de lancement fait baisser la note : 319 euros en 8 Go + 256 Go, et 369 euros en 12 Go + 256 Go (au lieu de 453 euros). Le téléphone existe en blanc, noir et orange.
La batterie utilise la technologie silicium-carbone. Son anode contient 13 % de silicium, un matériau qui stocke plus d’énergie que le graphite classique dans le même volume. Poco promet plus de deux jours d’autonomie et 80 % de capacité conservée après 1 600 cycles de charge, soit environ six ans selon ses calculs. La charge monte à 67 watts, et le téléphone peut recharger un autre appareil par câble à 22,5 watts.
Autour de cette batterie, Poco a installé un écran AMOLED de 6,83 pouces en définition 1,5K, annoncé à 3 500 nits en pic sur un quart de la dalle, et un capteur photo principal de 50 mégapixels stabilisé. Côté puce, on trouve un Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 gravé en 4 nm, un SoC d’entrée de milieu de gamme. Le châssis cumule les certifications IP66, IP68, IP69 et IP69K. Il résiste donc à une immersion à 2 mètres pendant 72 heures et aux jets d’eau à 80 °C sous haute pression.
Un jumeau du Redmi Note 17 Pro, en moins cher
Le concurrent le plus direct du Poco X8 vient de chez Xiaomi. Arrivé en France en septembre, le Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G a la même puce, la même batterie de 8 340 mAh et la même charge à 67 watts. Pourtant, il démarre à 449 euros avec seulement 6 Go de mémoire vive. Le Poco coûte donc 46 euros de moins, avec 2 Go de plus et les certifications IP69 et IP69K, alors que le Redmi s’arrête à l’IP68. Seul point en faveur du Redmi, il est équipé d’un ultra grand-angle.
Une grosse batterie ne garantit pas pour autant une autonomie record. Mais ce n’est pas le cas du nouveau Poco ou du Redmi. Ce dernier affiche plus de 18h30 en rafraîchissement adaptatif et 24h en 60 Hz. Il devrait en être de même sur le Poco X8. Attention tout de même, le Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 est gourmand quand il est fortement solicité. En jeu, l’autonomie fond beaucoup plus rapidement.
L’écart se creuse face à Samsung. Samsung vend le Galaxy A37 469 euros en 6 Go + 128 Go et 589 euros en 8 Go + 256 Go. Il coûte donc 186 euros de plus que le Poco X8 dans la même configuration, pour une batterie de 5 000 mAh qui charge à 45 watts. Samsung s’engage aussi sur 1 200 cycles de charge minimum, contre 1 600 annoncés par Poco.
À 319 euros, le Poco X8 est donc une bonne affaire pour tenir deux jours sans chargeur avec un téléphone qui supporte l’eau et les chutes. Par contre, il ne fera pas de miracle en jeu, et les Poco F9 sont bien mieux armés pour ça. L’offre de lancement s’arrête le 7 octobre, puis la version 8 Go + 256 Go repassera à 403 euros, un prix qui reste inférieur à celui du Redmi Note 17 Pro.
