articles.title: Moins de 40€ pour la barbe et le corps : le Philips OneBlade 360 connecté perd 35€ sur Amazon
articles.text:
Pour ses offres anticipées des Jours Flash Prime, Amazon baisse de 47 % le Philips OneBlade 360 connecté Visage + Corps. Lame pivotante, kit corps et application : voici ce que ce rasoir hybride fait bien, et où il reste en retrait.
Le Philips OneBlade 360 avec connectivité Visage + Corps (QP4631/65) reprend le principe maison d’un outil unique pour tailler, dessiner les contours et raser, auquel il ajoute un kit pour le corps et une liaison avec une application. Il est proposé à 39,99 € sur Amazon au lieu de 74,99 €, son prix conseillé, soit 35 € d’économie dans le cadre des offres anticipées des Jours Flash Prime.
Elle vise d’abord celles et ceux qui portent une barbe courte et veulent un seul appareil pour le visage et le corps. Si vous recherchez un rasage de très près, il faudra en revanche composer avec un choix de conception assumé par Philips.
Le Philips OneBlade 360 Visage + Corps connecté est affiché à 39,99 € au lieu de 74,99 € sur Amazon, pendant les offres anticipées des Jours Flash Prime.
Pourquoi choisir le Philips OneBlade 360 Visage + Corps ?
- Une lame qui suit les courbes : Elle pivote dans toutes les directions pour rester au contact de la peau sous le menton et le long de la mâchoire. Selon Philips, les zones difficiles à atteindre demandent ainsi moins de passages.
- Un vrai kit pour le corps : Le sabot corps de 3 mm et le système de protection clipsable pour les zones sensibles permettent d’utiliser le même manche du visage au torse. Étanche IPX7, l’appareil s’utilise à sec, avec de la mousse ou sous la douche.
- Une application qui assure le suivi : L’application gratuite Philips OneBlade vous prévient quand il faut changer la lame ou recharger la batterie. Elle propose aussi un guide pas à pas et un essai de styles de barbe en réalité augmentée.
Barbe courte, contours et corps : ce qu’il fait au quotidien
Sur le visage, le sabot réglable 5 en 1 couvre des longueurs de 1 à 5 mm, de quoi entretenir une barbe de quelques jours sans changer d’accessoire. Son design ouvert est conçu pour ne pas se boucher, même sur des poils longs et épais. Sans sabot, la lame double sens dessine les contours dans les deux directions, puis rase les joues ou le cou. Philips annonce 12 000 mouvements par minute et une coupe quelle que soit la longueur du poil.
Ce modèle parle d’abord aux porteurs de barbe courte qui veulent un seul appareil pour le visage et le corps, et à ceux qui voyagent léger : 60 minutes d’autonomie pour une heure de charge, avec une recharge en USB-A. Il est moins pertinent si vous portez une barbe longue, puisque le sabot plafonne à 5 mm. Il ne conviendra pas non plus si vous attendez une peau parfaitement lisse : Philips précise lui-même que le OneBlade ne rase pas d’aussi près qu’une lame traditionnelle.
Face au OneBlade 360 Face et au OneBlade Pro 360, où se situe-t-il ?
Cette version ajoute le kit corps et la connexion à l’application. Le OneBlade 360 Face, sans kit corps, suffit si vous ne comptez l’utiliser que sur le visage, et nous l’avons déjà relayé à 29,99 € sur Amazon. À l’inverse, le OneBlade Pro 360 vise ceux qui changent souvent de style, avec un sabot de 20 hauteurs entre 0,4 et 10 mm, mais nous l’avions relayé à 79 € lors des French Days. Entre les deux, cette version à 39,99 € couvre aussi le corps sans monter en gamme.
✅ Les points forts
- Lame 360 pivotante qui suit le cou et la mâchoire
- Kit corps : sabot 3 mm et protection des zones sensibles
- Étanche IPX7, utilisable à sec ou sous la douche
- 60 minutes d’autonomie pour 1 heure de charge
- Application qui signale l’usure de la lame et la batterie faible
❌ Les limites
- Rasage moins près qu’une lame traditionnelle, de l’aveu même de Philips
- Sabot limité à 5 mm, trop court pour une barbe longue
- Lame à remplacer, prévue pour durer jusqu’à 4 mois selon Philips
- Charge en USB-A, adaptateur secteur non inclus
Le prix de 39,99 € est lié aux offres anticipées des Jours Flash Prime : vérifiez qu’il s’affiche toujours sur la fiche Amazon avant de commander.
À 39,99 €, ce OneBlade 360 Visage + Corps devient une option cohérente pour entretenir une barbe courte et le corps avec un seul appareil. La lame pivotante, l’étanchéité IPX7 et le kit dédié au corps couvrent l’essentiel des besoins d’un rasoir hybride. L’application n’a rien d’indispensable, mais le rappel de changement de lame évite de continuer avec une lame usée. À 10 € de l’offre que nous avions relayée sur la version Visage, le kit corps se justifie vite si vous comptez vous en servir.
Les porteurs de barbe longue et les adeptes du rasage de très près peuvent passer leur chemin : le sabot s’arrête à 5 mm et la coupe reste volontairement moins rase qu’avec une lame classique. Si vous alternez souvent les styles de barbe, le OneBlade Pro 360 et ses 20 hauteurs méritent un coup d’œil lors d’une prochaine promotion. Pour un entretien régulier du visage et du corps, celui-ci réunit l’essentiel dans une seule boîte.
Pour profiter du Prime Day, n'oubliez pas de devenir membre Amazon Prime. Vous bénéficiez d'un essai gratuit de 30 jours, c'est donc le bon moment pour tester.

articles.title: Starship : de sublimes vidéos au ralenti du vol 14 - Numerama
articles.text:
On a eu droit au spectacle brut, ce lundi 28 septembre, lorsque SpaceX a mené à bien son quatorzième vol d’essai du Starship. Un lancement qui a constitué une grande première pour l’entreprise américaine, car c’était son tout premier tir orbital. Place maintenant aux premières vidéos montées par SpaceX.
Ce mardi 29 septembre, le compte X de la société a diffusé quatre vues au ralenti du décollage du Starship, avec des caméras placées sur le pas de tir et sur la tour de lancement de Starbase, le centre d’essais du groupe basé au Texas. Les images jouent sur des angles marqués, en plongée et en contre-plongée.
Quelques heures plus tard, SpaceX a publié un plan centré sur l’allumage des 33 moteurs Raptor 3 du Super Heavy, le premier étage de la fusée géante. On y voit en détail les 33 moteurs au moment de l’allumage.
Un premier vol orbital écourté de près de sept heures
Ce 14e vol d’essai était le premier à placer le Starship en orbite autour de la Terre. Il a aussi déployé 26 satellites Starlink V3. Les treize vols précédents suivaient une trajectoire suborbitale, qui ramène le vaisseau dans l’atmosphère sans qu’il ait besoin de freiner lui-même.
Pourtant, dans son récapitulatif officiel du vol, SpaceX reconnaît que l’un des trois moteurs Raptor Vacuum du vaisseau, la version conçue pour fonctionner dans le vide spatial, s’est coupé trop tôt pendant la montée. Les cinq autres moteurs du vaisseau ont tourné plus longtemps pour compenser.
Par prudence, SpaceX a fait redescendre le vaisseau au bout d’environ trois heures au lieu des dix prévues, pour un amerrissage dans le Pacifique nord. Le Super Heavy a lui aussi perdu un moteur pendant la montée. Il n’a ensuite rallumé que 31 de ses 33 moteurs pour faire demi-tour, puis 11 des 13 prévus pour freiner, avant d’amerrir dans le golfe du Mexique. SpaceX ne comptait pas le récupérer.
SpaceX n’a pas encore expliqué pourquoi le moteur Raptor Vacuum s’est arrêté. SpaceX devra le comprendre avant le 15e vol. L’entreprise n’a annoncé aucune date, mais des documents de l’aviation civile américaine le placent au plus tôt le 19 octobre.

articles.title: Hub à écran, HomePod mini, Apple TV : Apple relancera enfin sa maison connectée le 13 octobre — Frandroid
articles.text:
Après des mois de rumeurs, Apple va enfin dévoiler sa nouvelle gamme maison connectée. D’après Mark Gurman, journaliste de Bloomberg qui suit la marque de près, Apple présentera le mardi 13 octobre un hub domestique à écran (nom de code J490), un nouveau HomePod mini et une nouvelle Apple TV. Pour John Ternus, CEO depuis le 1er septembre, c’est un premier test face à l’Echo Show d’Amazon et au Nest Hub de Google.
Le HomePod Hub d’Apple
Le hub serait un écran carré d’environ 6 pouces, à poser sur un comptoir ou à fixer au mur dans sa version J491. Posé, il rappellerait l’iMac G4 « Tournesol » de 2002, avec son écran perché sur une base en demi-dôme.
Il reconnaîtrait chaque membre du foyer à la voix ou au visage, puis afficherait ses contacts, ses messages, son agenda et ses notes. En cas de soucis avec la reconnaissance faciale, l’iPhone servirait de solution de secours pour reconnaitre l’utilisateur.
Le HomePod mini, inchangé depuis 2020, et l’Apple TV, inchangée depuis 2022 et dont une image interne avait déjà trahi l’arrivée, gardent leur design. Tous deux reçoivent une puce plus rapide pour faire tourner Siri AI. Le HomePod mini arrive aussi en nouvelles couleurs, dont le vert et le rose.
Deux ans de retard à cause de Siri
Apple visait 2024 pour ces trois appareils, mais les retards de la nouvelle version de Siri ont tout décalé.
Siri AI étant désormais disponible, seulement sur Mac en Europe, la marque peut lancer ses nouveaux produits. On imagine qu’ils proposeront Siri AI en Europe, puisque ces catégories de produits ne sont pas concernés par la réglementation de l’UE, contrairement à l’iPhone et l’iPad.
Une caméra et un écran robotisé en préparation
Apple préparerait aussi J450, une caméra et un capteur de sécurité capable de détecter dans quelle pièce se trouve une personne, sans enregistrer de vidéo. Sa sortie serait prévue plus tard. Un hub plus haut de gamme serait lui aussi en développement, avec un écran de 9 pouces monté sur un bras robotisé qui pivote à 360 degrés.
En parallèle, Apple élargirait HomeKit, sa plateforme domotique, et travaillerait avec des fabricants tiers sur des appareils compatibles Siri AI. Aucun prix n’a encore fuité pour le hub, le HomePod mini ou l’Apple TV.

Actualización urgente en iPhone: Apple corrige falla de seguridad que puede usarse en ciberataques
articles.text:
Apple corrigió una vulnerabilidad de seguridad en iOS 26, iPadOS 26 y macOS 26 que, según la compañía, “podría haber sido explotada” en ataques dirigidos contra usuarios específicos.
La actualización para iPhone y iPad, identificada como iOS 26.7.1 y iPadOS 26.7.1, fue publicada el 28 de septiembre de 2026.
PUBLICIDAD
Apple indicó que el fallo afectaba a versiones de iOS anteriores a iOS 27 y que pudo haber sido utilizado en un “ataque extremadamente sofisticado” contra objetivos concretos.
La vulnerabilidad está registrada como CVE-2026-86950 y fue detectada por Meta Product Security. Apple no divulgó detalles sobre posibles víctimas ni sobre los responsables de una eventual explotación.
El problema se encontraba en CoreGraphics, el componente encargado de procesar gráficos e interfaces visuales en los dispositivos. De acuerdo con Apple, el procesamiento de un archivo manipulado con fines maliciosos podía permitir la ejecución de código arbitrario.
Qué corrigió Apple
Apple solucionó un problema de escritura fuera de límites mediante una comprobación de límites mejorada. Este tipo de falla puede producirse cuando un programa intenta escribir datos fuera del espacio de memoria asignado.
PUBLICIDAD
Según TechCrunch, la vulnerabilidad podía comprometer dispositivos que aún utilizan versiones de iOS 26, iPadOS 26 y macOS 26. La compañía señaló que los equipos con iOS 27, iPadOS 27 y macOS 27 no estaban afectados por este error.
La corrección llega después de otro parche de seguridad publicado este mes para la vulnerabilidad CVE-2026-86869. Ese fallo podía activarse a través de un mensaje de iMessage especialmente diseñado, sin que la víctima necesitara abrir un enlace o interactuar con el contenido.
Qué modelos de iPhone son compatibles con la actualización de iOS
La actualización iOS 26.7.1 está disponible para el iPhone 11 y modelos posteriores. También pueden instalarla los iPad Pro de 12,9 pulgadas de tercera generación y posteriores, los iPad Pro de 11 pulgadas de primera generación y posteriores, los iPad Air de tercera generación y posteriores, los iPad de octava generación y posteriores, y los iPad mini de quinta generación y posteriores.
PUBLICIDAD
Apple publicó el parche como parte de sus actualizaciones de seguridad para corregir la vulnerabilidad detectada en CoreGraphics. La empresa no detalló cuántos dispositivos pudieron haber sido comprometidos ni quiénes habrían explotado el error.
Los usuarios que permanezcan en versiones anteriores de iOS 27 deben instalar la actualización de seguridad disponible para su dispositivo, dado que Apple reconoció que recibió un informe sobre una posible explotación del fallo en ataques dirigidos.
Cómo actualizar la versión de iOS de un iPhone
Para actualizar el iPhone a la versión más reciente de iOS, primero realiza una copia de seguridad en iCloud o en una computadora. Luego, conecta el dispositivo a una red WiFi y a la corriente. Abre Configuración, ingresa en General y selecciona Actualización de software.
PUBLICIDAD
El sistema mostrará la versión instalada y las actualizaciones disponibles. Si aparece una nueva versión, toca Descargar e instalar y sigue las indicaciones en pantalla.
Es posible activar las actualizaciones automáticas desde ese mismo menú para que el iPhone descargue e instale versiones durante la noche mientras está cargando y conectado a WiFi.
Qué características tienen los nuevos iPhone 18 Pro y iPhone 18 Pro Max
Los iPhone 18 Pro y iPhone 18 Pro Max incorporan el chip A20 Pro, una cámara principal de 48 megapíxeles con apertura variable y un sistema de refrigeración por cámara de vapor.
Ambos conservan cámaras traseras de 48 megapíxeles y suman controles manuales para fotografía y video, incluida la velocidad de obturación.
El Pro tiene una pantalla OLED de 6,3 pulgadas, mientras que el Pro Max alcanza las 6,9. Los dos ofrecen ProMotion de hasta 120 Hz, una Dynamic Island más pequeña y una cámara frontal de 18 megapíxeles. El modelo Max añade mayor autonomía por su batería más grande.

articles.text:
Tuesday, September 29th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Framework Desktop with Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 Gets Official Pre-Order Date
After teasing the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 upgrade to the Framework Destkop mini PC, Framework has officially announced that pre-orders for the SFF desktop will start on Wednesday, 30 September. The announcement came in a post on the OEM's official X account, where it also confirmed that, as is typical with its Framework Laptop upgrades, the rest of the motherboard and case will remain the same, for backwards compatibility purposes. 
Currently, it is unclear how much the new AMD Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495-powered mini PC will cost, but it'd be a safe bet to assume it will be more expensive than the current-generation Ryzen AI Max+ 395 model, especially on the high-end version, topping out at 192 GB of LPDDR5X-8533 memory where the 395 version tops out at 128 GB.Having an identical design means that the SFF Framework Desktop will still use a full-size Flex ATX PSU, feature a PCIe ×4 slot—primarily for networking—and a choice of cooling fans, ranging from the Noctua NF-A12×25 HS-PWM to the Cooler Master Mobius 120 or 120P. Framework has also said that it will continue shipping the Framework Desktop with either Fedora or Windows 11 for the pre-built versions.

Other Strix halo mini PCs often have 2 additional USB 2 ports for this purpose, and have other options like a built in sd card reader. IDK why framework refuses to put those on the board, there is plenty of room. And don't forget the expansion slot awkwardly placed in a case with no external slot so you have to modify the case to fit most cards.Can you point to all these other Strix halo mini ITX boards?
Because of the nature of the soldered RAM, it seems most OEMs are releasing entire mini PCs, but sometimes in barebones, where you supply your own ssd and os.
The big selling point of frameworks build is that it uses an actual mini ITX board, a standard flex ATX psu, and can use normal cases. The only other brand to do that is minisforum.
The Mini-PCs I understand since they are typically much smaller.
The full ITX builds I understand because they are fully modular.
This Framework seems a mish-mash of both, with some of the advantages of both, but most of the disadvantages, too. It's not cheap either. I consider it to be laptop hardware with a PCIE slot and better cooling.
The soft benefits are what sell here. Being able to get ahold of an actual support team from framework, being able to use your own case, and having a standard, replaceable power supply and re configurable ports are the benefits here.
As for it being a laptop chip, you have it backwards. This is a desktop class CPU that can be choked back to fit in a laptop. There is a noticeable performance increase from having the 120+ watt TDP available in desktop form that laptops cannot achieve.

articles.title: Government, Finance Orgs Targeted in Weeks-Long NetScaler Zero-Day Attacks
articles.text:
Google’s Mandiant and Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) have published details on attacks exploiting the NetScaler zero-days that Citrix patched over the weekend.
The vulnerabilities are tracked as CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, and they affect NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway instances. Attackers can exploit these critical flaws for unauthenticated remote code execution.
Before Citrix released patches, government cybersecurity agencies and security firms took the rare step of urging administrators to disconnect affected NetScaler appliances from the internet immediately while zero-day exploitation investigations were ongoing.
Mandiant and GTIG, whose report focuses on the exploitation of CVE-2026-88772, spotted attacks in late September. However, their investigation found that the zero-day campaign has been “ongoing since at least early September.”
The attacks likely impacted organizations in North America and Europe. These organizations are in the government, financial services, education, legal, and professional services sectors.
The attackers exploited the vulnerability to gain root access to NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances. They then changed the appliance’s web server configuration so they could plant web shells and run them with root privileges.
Mandiant found previously unseen malware in the attacks, including a PHP web shell named WHIPSHOT and a Python-based tunneling tool named SLAPSHOT. The two work together to give the attackers a path from the compromised appliance into the victim’s internal network.
According to Mandiant, the tools enable internal reconnaissance, lateral movement and credential theft. In at least one intrusion, the hackers used the tunnel to manually explore the internal network and steal credentials.
Mandiant also saw signs that the threat actor may be managing similar web shells in multiple compromised environments.
Mandiant CTO Charles Carmakal noted that dozens of organizations have been hit, including by suspected state-sponsored threat actors.
“We expect broad and opportunistic exploitation of CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88771 by a variety of threat actors in the near term,” Carmakal warned.
Cybersecurity expert Kevin Beaumont reported being aware of more than 100 victim organizations as of Tuesday, noting that the attacks appear to be part of an espionage campaign.
Security firm WatchTowr, one of the first to confirm in-the-wild exploitation, has released technical details on both CVE-2026-88772 and CVE-2026-88771.
Threat intelligence company GreyNoise observed zero-day exploitation attempts on September 24, several days before the flaws were disclosed and patched.
“The [malicious cyber actor] attempted to set both the Set User ID (setuid) and Set Group ID (setgid) bits on /bin/sh to obtain a root shell and install a password-protected webshell that accepts communication by the cookie value sent by the adversary. This may be to avoid persisting their commands in web logs,” GreyNoise explained.
Palo Alto Networks reported that there had been roughly 50,000 potentially exposed NetScaler instances as of September 27.
Related: Microsoft SharePoint Flaw CVE-2026-65660 Now Exploited in Attacks
Related: Apple Patches Zero-Day Linked to ‘Extremely Sophisticated Attack’

articles.title: OpenAI halves $200 plan allowance, launches $500 plan
articles.text:
OpenAI halves $200 plan allowance, launches $500 plan
On Tuesday, OpenAI introduced a new $ 500-per-month Pro plan that gives subscribers the highest included usage of the company’s subscription plans.
The new plan includes 25x the usage allowance of ChatGPT Plus and provides access to its Ultrafast tier for GPT-6 Astra — which promises to generate tokens at up to 8x the standard speed in Codex.
Ultrafast for GPT-6.1 Sol is coming soon.
The $200 Pro plan cut
But what’s also coming soon will upset quite a few people: Starting October 30, OpenAI is cutting the usage allowance in its $200 Pro plan for ChatGPT Work and Codex from 20x the allowance of the $20 Plus plan to only 10x.
In addition, subscribers to the $200 Pro plan will also see their GPT-6 Pro allowance in Chat fall from 200 messages per week to 100.
Existing subscribers will keep their current limits through October 29. After that, they will get a grant of 62,500 usage credits (worth $2,500, OpenAI says) that will expire on December 31, 2026.
If you’re looking for a glimmer of good news: OpenAI says it won’t reintroduce the 5-hour limit for subscribers on the $200 plan, so you can now burn through your weekly usage at your own pace (and likely faster than you want).
OpenAI’s argument: you’ll still get more done
Tibo Sottiaux, the company’s head of product and platform, previewed this change on X ahead of the official announcement. The developer reactions were expectedly negative (“Ok guys, back to claude. RIP openAI 🪦”).
Sottiaux argues that developers will “still get more work done than if you were on the Pro $200 subscription one month ago.”
Cheaper, more efficient models, OpenAI argues, will let subscribers get more work done than they could a month ago, even with half the included allowance.
And that may be true in some form, but that’s not what users signed up for when they bought the $200 plan. What they want is for OpenAI to pass down the efficiencies it gains so they can do far more work — without having to pay for a $500 plan.
OpenAI DevDay 2026 coverage:
OpenAI was likely also aware of how this would be perceived; otherwise, it might not have decided to front-run the announcement.
As of now, it’s unclear what exactly the included allowance in the $500 plan will be.
For now, existing subscribers will keep their current limits during this transition period, though it’s unclear how long it will last. OpenAI also promises to give those users a one-time credit “to help with the change.”
The 20x standard across labs
For the longest time, the 20x allowance of the highest-priced tier was the standard among frontier labs. For Google, that’s true for the top Gemini AI Ultra plan, which costs $200 per month, as well as Anthropic’s top-tier $200-per-month plan. Google’s plan, though, also includes storage and other benefits.
All of these labs also offer $100 plans with what remains the standard 5x allowance. Let’s see whether OpenAI sets a trend here or whether negative pushback is so strong that the company undoes the change.

articles.title: Bell, Cisco sign MOU on sovereign AI infrastructure in Canada
articles.text:
Bell signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Cisco to collaborate on sovereign AI infrastructure for Canada.
According to the companies, the MOU will bring together Bell’s data centres, network, and operations capabilities with Cisco’s AI, security, infrastructure monitoring, and Sovereign Critical Infrastructure (SCI) technology.
SCI is Cisco’s offering for customers who want to run their own on-premises sovereign infrastructure with full control. Initially aimed at Europe, Cisco touts SCI as an option for governments, banks, healthcare providers, and more.
Together, Bell and Cisco aim to help Canadian organizations deploy and manage AI infrastructure in Canada. The companies also want to support sensitive workloads that may have strict security and other requirements.
The companies’ collaboration will focus on building a Canadian platform for sovereign AI, supporting modular AI infrastructure, and developing flexible commercial models that can help customers align cost with how they actually use AI.
This is the latest development in Bell’s ongoing AI push. The telecom giant recently launched a cybersecurity AI model in partnership with Cohere, and earlier this month detailed plans to quadruple capacity of its planned AI data centre hub in Saskatchewan. Further, Bell is working on a larger AI Fabric project that will see data centres constructed in B.C. and beyond.

articles.title: Cryptography was the last slow problem | EU-Startups
articles.text:
On 28 July of this year, it took an AI about sixty hours to find a cryptographic flaw that two years of expert review had not uncovered.
In the following 24 hours, the findings were confirmed and the digital signature submission intended to be secure against both classical and quantum computers, HAWK – a lattice‑based post‑quantum signature scheme under evaluation – was withdrawn from consideration. It will never be standardised.
A static security system
For fifty years, cryptography has been the one part of technology you could pretty much set and forget. RSA, a foundational public-key cryptography algorithm used for secure data transmission, arrived in 1977, became mainstream in web traffic security by 1994, and is still useful today.
Minor attacks on it have accumulated slowly, parameters have increased, and it has taken decades for meaningful advances.
That slowness has been baked into everything we have built with cryptography: standards bodies deliberate for years, migration programmes are planned in five-year blocks, and procurement assumes that what you buy today will still be adequate in 2033.
Even the US government’s Executive Order 14412 that moved post-quantum deadlines to 2030 and 2031 is considered aggressive. They pulled the timeline forward by half a decade and the industry called it a shock. However –
Sixty hours.
AI broke one candidate algorithm in no time at all, changing the price of the discovery cycle. When the time required to find a cryptographic weakness collapses from years to days, and the time required to fix a weakness across a large organisation stays at years, you are left with a gap. Bad things live in that gap.
The uncomfortable arithmetic is that the half-life of a cryptographic assumption may now be plausibly shorter than the duration of a cryptographic migration project. If that is even a possible truth, then every organisation whose plan is “arrive at post-quantum by 2030” has been designed for the wrong world.
The nearing threat
The realistic AI threat to encryption over the next three years actually has almost nothing to do with breaking an algorithm, but in implementation.
Every large organisation is carrying cryptography throughout: expired certificates later renewed with a weak key, a service still negotiating a deprecated cipher suite, a hardcoded credential in a repository that arrived with an acquisition in 2019, a random number generator that perhaps isn’t very random.
A new economics in finding the flaw has developed. Discovering a flaw took highly skilled humans to go looking, and the obscure corners of the enterprise were protected only due to the fact auditing them wasn’t worth anyone’s time.
AI has just changed that. Attackers can easily and continuously read all code, certificates and network configurations at next to zero cost. Every weakness should now be assumed to be found.
Nothing I have described requires a quantum computer to exist, only what already happened in July: finding cryptographic weakness became dramatically cheaper, and fixing it has become no faster.
Even if Q-Day, the hypothetical moment when quantum computers become powerful enough to break standard public-key encryption, never comes, every word of this still holds because you will be exposed to AI-assisted attackers exploiting classical flaws.
Cryptographic agility is the unusual security investment that pays out under every scenario.
A surprisingly humdrum solution
His four core banking platforms: two of them inherited through acquisitions; several thousand certificates across three cloud providers; payments integration whose cryptography is contractually the supplier’s responsibility.
This is a capable person, well-funded, running an expert team at a serious institution describing the reality of the industry.
You cannot fix what you cannot find, which is why a cryptographic inventory matters, and why the June executive order directs CISA, working with NIST, to publish guidance on the minimum elements of a “cryptographic bill of materials” by March 2027.
Inventory tells you where you stand. Agility is the ability to move. In practice, that means four things: knowing what cryptography you run and where it lives; being able to replace an algorithm without rewriting the application; requiring your suppliers to demonstrate they can do the same; and having actually exercised all of it, at least once.
That last one is what everybody skips. A migration capability you have never used is a disaster recovery plan you have never tested.
What next?
I would encourage all companies not to wait until March 2027 for CISA to define what a cryptographic bill of materials ought to contain. This quarter, ask your security to lead the question I asked that CISO in the spring. If the answer is longer than a week, you have found your project.
Q-Day may well be a decade away. What’s for certain is that the sixty hours have already happened, and that nothing about most organisations’ ability to respond changed that week, and losing that gap is entirely within your control.

articles.title: Cloudflare Adds Configurable HTTP Vary Header Support to Prevent Cache Thrashing
Report finds that Microsoft Copilot's human reviewers can see users' uploaded photos and sexualized AI edits
articles.text:
In brief: Human contractors reviewing Microsoft Copilot's image editor can see users' prompts, uploaded photos and AI-generated edits. Documents show that some of those assignments contain sexual, disturbing or potentially illegal material. Yet the reviewers are not there to flag the content – they are paid to decide how well Copilot carried out the request.
In a typical assignment, a contractor receives the user's prompt and original image, along with two edits produced by Copilot, and must decide which version better follows the instructions. The assessment covers four areas. Reviewers check whether Copilot completed the requested edit, left unrelated parts of the image unchanged, avoided visible defects and produced a strong image overall. If the prompt asks the system to add a cup to a table, for example, the cup should be the only change.
The instructions reviewed by 404 Media also tell contractors to rely on subjective judgment. "Trust your intuition – when you glance at the two edited images side by side, which one immediately feels like the better edit? Your gut reaction as a human viewer matters," one set of instructions says.
"When in doubt go with your first impression," the instructions continue. "Human intuition is good at catching subtle quality differences that are hard to articulate."
But many assignments go beyond routine image editing. Contractors said that they had seen requests to enlarge women's breasts, shorten their skirts, reveal more of their legs or place people in sexual positions. Other assignments included upskirt photos, pro-anorexia material and fetish images involving children's cartoon characters.
"Faces are always uncensored, and many of the prompts are sexual in nature and dubiously consensual," one contractor told 404 Media. The publication granted the worker anonymity because the person was not permitted to speak to the press.
The reviewers are not being hired to moderate those requests or determine whether Copilot should have accepted them. Their job is to judge the quality of its response. In some cases, that means deciding which output more closely matches a user's request for a sexualized edit.
"Who is writing these prompts and who is deciding that basically generating porn is what Copilot is now focused on? It's hard to take things seriously when my focus has to be what model generated the appropriate bust size or which middle-aged woman was put in the appropriate sexually suggestive position," one contractor wrote on an internal message board.
Other contractors said they sometimes opened assignments without knowing what they contained. "I just came across an image set that consisted of eight upskirt photos," one reviewer wrote while asking for an unsafe-content warning. Other posts mentioned an apparent animal sacrifice and prompts involving sexual acts or positions. One contractor wrote, "I recoiled," after encountering pro-anorexia content.
The documents indicate that at least hundreds of human reviewers sometimes see Copilot submissions. That means photos users upload for editing may be viewed by a contractor as part of Microsoft's process for evaluating the model.
At least one company hiring contractors for the work is Prolific, which offers human feedback for preference tuning, safety evaluations and AI benchmarks. Prolific guidelines included in the material acknowledge that generative AI can expose workers to content that researchers did not expect.
Prolific did not respond to 404 Media's request for comment. A Microsoft spokesperson told the publication, "Microsoft uses customer data as described in our terms of use, including to improve our products and enforce our code of conduct."
Tech companies have long used contractors to moderate online content and label data used to train AI systems. The Copilot assignments described in the documents serve a different purpose. Rather than screening material for safety, contractors are comparing outputs to help improve the image editor's accuracy, consistency and ability to follow prompts.

articles.title: La película de 'Juego de Tronos' de Aegon el Conquistador ya tiene director y fecha de estreno
articles.text:
La primera película de Juego de Tronos ya tiene fecha de estreno oficial. Warner Bros. está preparando un ambicioso proyecto antes de unirse definitivamente a Paramount, y lo harán con una de sus franquicias más importantes. Tras muchos años expandiéndose únicamente con series para HBO, la saga medieval de George R.R. Martin está lista para dar el salto a los cines.
Lo hará con una película live-action que será precuela de la serie original. Concretamente, el filme se centrará en Aegon Targaryen el Conquistador, uno de los personajes clave de todo el universo Juego de Tronos. Se trata del fundador de la dinastía Targaryen y unificador de seis de los Siete Reinos. Su historia es una de las más importantes de la saga y por fin podremos verla en pantalla.
Ahora, se ha desvelado que la película de Juego de Tronos sobre Aegon el Conquistador se estrenará en cines el 1 de junio de 2029. Además, también se ha confirmado que Owen Harris, quien ya ha trabajado en la serie El caballero de los Siete Reinos, será el director. El guion correrá a cargo del nominado al Oscar Beau Willimon, showrunner de House of Cards y guionista de Andor.
Quién fue Aegon el Conquistador
Aegon Targaryen fue el segundo hijo de Lord Aerion Targaryen y Lady Valaena Velaryon, los Señores de Rocadragón. Este era el título máximo que, por entonces, tenía la Casa Targaryen. Aegon tuvo una hermana mayor, Visneya, y una menor, Rhaenys, y se casó con ambas. Con la primera, por tradición valyria. Con la segunda, por amor.
Aegon Targaryen vivió y creció en la isla de Rocadragón, en el extremo más occidental de lo que antaño fue el Feudo Franco de Valyria, destruido casi un siglo antes en la Maldición de Valyria. Eventualmente, a sus 25 años, puso su vista en Poniente y en los Siete Reinos. Se dice que incluso pintó un mapa del continente en una mesa, pero sin fronteras, simbolizando toda su unión. Su plan era unificar los Siete Reinos y convertirse en el rey.
Date de alta en HBO MAX y tendrás acceso a las mejores series y películas exclusivas como The Wire, Los Soprano o Casa del Dragón. Incluye todo el catálogo de Warner, los clásicos de Cartoon Network, los grandes estrenos y el mejor deporte.
Junto a su enorme dragón Balerion (el más grande de todo Juego de Tronos) y los de sus hermanas/esposas, Vhagar (sí, el mismo de La Casa del Dragón) y Meraxes, lideró a sus ejércitos a una victoria tras otra. Así, consiguió lo que parecía impensable, conquistar todo Poniente a excepción de Dorne, que siempre resistió. Aun así, el Septón Supremo le ungió como Aegon de la Casa Targaryen, el primero de su nombre, Rey de los Ándalos y los Rhoynar y los Primeros Hombres, Señor de los Siete Reinos y Protector del Reino.

articles.title: The internet is convinced Elon Musk's xAI trolled OpenAI's 'Dots' launch | TechCrunch
articles.text:
On Tuesday, OpenAI launched a new product called Dots, an always-on AI agent with a bubbly, blobby avatar. While the colorful avatar might evoke a smile, the biggest laugh from the launch is (we imagine) being had by Elon Musk, the former OpenAI founder who left, launched competitor Grok, and unsuccessfully sued.
That’s because the domain “dot.com” belongs to Musk’s xAI, and it currently redirects to the download page for xAI’s Grok chatbot app. According to the Whois domain owner registry, that domain name was just transferred in July.
It is entirely possible that xAI bought the domain for normal domain-buying reasons. “Dot” could be a typo of “bot,” so it nabbed it to grab mistyped searches. We’ve reached out to xAI and asked. But xAI doesn’t own the “bot.com” name, nor does it own other obvious typo domains like “vot.com,” which is listed for sale.
The internet’s theory is far funnier: that Musk (or his team) pulled off a prank, getting wind of OpenAI’s new product and its name and buying the domain name.
In fact, anonymous X user and xAI watcher @birdabo (this person calls themselves “chief shitposting officer @SpaceXAI“) was first to spot the domain name in a now-viral post. Whatever the motivation, the circumstance is funny.
And as for the “dots.com” domain, a more direct fit to the product name, it currently belongs to a long-defunct company. So if a petty revenge prank was really the motivation, grabbing that name, too, would be next-level.

articles.title: Budget de l’UE : la France veut utiliser les amendes infligées à Google pour alléger la contribution des États
articles.text:
En Europe, de nombreux pays veulent moins contribuer. La France, qui cherche une position d'équilibre, lance une idée intéressante sur la table.
Pour faire respecter ses règlements, Bruxelles impose des amendes importantes depuis de nombreuses années aux géants américains de la tech, avec au premier chef, Google. Des amendes qui représentent à la fin un véritable trésor de guerre qui, pour les autorités françaises, pourrait bien permettre de moins payer pour faire fonctionner l'Union européenne !
4,6 milliards d'amende de Google à utiliser pour réduire la contribution des grands pays à l'UE
Que faire des milliards d'euros versés par Google, pour des infractions aux règlements du Vieux Continent ? Pour Benjamin Haddad, ministre délégué à l'Europe, ces fonds pourraient être bien utiles.
Car pour lui, comme il l'a exprimé dans un entretien avec France Info, « il s'agit d'une nouvelle source de recettes pour l'Union européenne - d'un montant de 4,6 milliards d'euros - qui devrait entraîner automatiquement une baisse des contributions de tous les États membres ». Une proposition qui s'inscrit dans un contexte assez particulier en Europe aujourd'hui.
Six pays européens veulent trancher dans les fonds de la Commission européenne
En effet, les six pays que l'on appelle souvent « frugaux » (Allemagne, Pays-Bas, Autriche, Danemark, Suède et Finlance) sont actuellement en pleine rébellion. Ils souhaitent réduire la taille du budget de l'UE, comme on a pu l'apprendre grâce au Financial Times, qui a pu jeter un oeil à leur lettre commune.
Le budget en question est, pour la période 2028-2034, programmé pour être de près de 2000 milliards d'euros - en hausse de 65%. Ces pays voudraient à la fois réduire la taille de l'enveloppe, ce qui réduirait leur contribution nette, mais aussi utiliser cet argent autrement, pour l'orienter vers trois domaines en particulier : la compétitivité, la sécurité et la défense. Est-ce que les quelques milliards payés par Google seraient suffisants pour calmer cette fronde?

articles.title: Verspätungen und Zugausfälle: Mit diesem Tool vermeidest du Stress beim Bahnfahren
articles.text:
Verspätungen und Zugausfälle: Mit diesem Tool vermeidest du Stress beim Bahnfahren
Wer regelmäßig mit der Deutschen Bahn unterwegs ist, kennt Frust und kurzfristige Planänderungen nur zu gut. Die Gründe für Verspätungen oder komplette Zugausfälle sind zahlreich und reichen von defekten Weichen über Baustellen bis zur verspäteten Bereitstellung. Laut Konzernangaben mussten im ersten Halbjahr 2026 3,6 Prozent der ICE- und IC-Züge ersatzlos gestrichen werden. Im gleichen Zeitraum erreichten nur 58,7 Prozent aller Fernverkehrszüge pünktlich ihr Ziel.
Als pünktlich gelten dabei Verspätungen unter sechs Minuten. Wer seine Zugfahrt trotz solcher Komplikationen möglichst stressfrei planen möchte, findet bei dem Onlinedienst Delay Bahn nützliche Funktionen. Seit Kurzem ist zudem die Live-Verfolgung von Zügen möglich.
Diese Züge sind besonders unpünktlich
Delay Bahn prüft, wie pünktlich Züge sind und ob auf einer bestimmten Strecke Verspätungen drohen. Anhand historischer Verspätungsdaten können Reisende so schon vor der Buchung einschätzen, wie zuverlässig eine Verbindung tatsächlich ist.
Anstatt nur die planmäßigen Abfahrts- und Ankunftszeiten anzuzeigen, beantwortet Delay Bahn praktische Fragen. Auf der Website geben Fahrgäste eine gewünschte Verbindung, etwa von Hamburg nach München, ein und wählen historische Daten der letzten sieben, 15 oder 30 Tage aus.
Die Übersicht zeigt, wie viel Verspätung eine Verbindung üblicherweise hat, wie oft sie in dem angegebenen Zeitraum ausgefallen ist und ob die Umsteigezeit realistisch ist. Gerade Letzteres kann bei der Reiseplanung entscheidend sein, denn eine Verbindung kann auf den ersten Blick schnell wirken.
Wenn es aber regelmäßig zu Verspätungen kommt, ist eine Alternative eventuell die bessere Wahl. Historische Daten liefern hier eine realistischere Einschätzung als der reine Fahrplan. Reisende können zudem nach Zügen mit der geringsten Verspätung oder dem niedrigsten Anschlussrisiko filtern.
Neue Funktion zeigt Züge in Echtzeit an
Shashank Tripathi, der Entwickler der Website, hat jetzt die neue Funktion „Wo ist mein Zug?” hinzugefügt. Auf einer Karte lässt sich dort die aktuelle Verkehrslage sowie die Position der Züge in Echtzeit verfolgen. Über den neuen Menüpunkt können Nutzer:innen eine Live-Karte aufrufen, einzelne Züge verfolgen und eine Route mit anderen teilen. Letzteres ist besonders nützlich, wenn sich Reisende am Bahnhof abholen lassen möchten.
Anstatt ständig in Kontakt bleiben oder sich auf Angaben der Bahn verlassen zu müssen, können Nutzer:innen so in Echtzeit verfolgen, wo sich der Zug gerade tatsächlich befindet. Ähnlich wie bei Google Maps können Reisende zudem Probleme auf einer Fahrt melden, wovon auch andere profitieren, die ebenfalls möglichst pünktlich und stressfrei ans Ziel gelangen möchten.
Hat die Deutsche Bahn den Dienst blockiert?
Delay Bahn ist erst seit Mitte August online. Der Dienst verbindet reale Bahndaten zu anstehenden Verbindungen mit historischen Statistiken zu Ausfällen und Verspätungen der Deutschen Bahn. Diese wiederum berechnen sich aus den realen Verkehrsdaten des Konzerns, die über eine API bereitgestellt werden. Wie mehrere Medien, darunter Chip und Caschys Blog, berichten, wurde der Zugriff auf diese Daten zwischenzeitlich blockiert.
Der Entwickler fand allerdings eine alternative Lösung, sodass Delay Bahn inzwischen wieder nutzbar ist. Die Gründe für die Sperrung sind bisher unklar. Für alle, die regelmäßig mit dem Zug fahren, kann die Website dennoch eine nützliche Ergänzung zu den offiziellen Informationen der Deutschen Bahn sein und schon bei der Planung einer Reise Frust vorbeugen.

articles.title: Why the next commerce battle will be for the gap between discovery and access
articles.text:
Why the next commerce battle will be for the gap between discovery and access
Digital content has made product discovery increasingly accessible across India, but affordability, assortment and convenience remain gaps for consumers beyond the metros. The next phase of ecommerce will depend on how effectively businesses bridge that gap between aspiration and access.
Discovery leading to a purchase decision used to happen through friends or family and was built around trust through word of mouth. This is still somewhat true in today’s era but the medium has changed from physical to digital with content creators influencing their decision making.
Today, from Mumbai to Meerut, discovery through content happens at the same platform, of the same product, almost at the same time. The closing of the knowledge gap and hence the aspiration is an underrated catalyst for Indian retail which is now changing user behaviour one reel at a time.
The numbers make the stakes plain. According to a report by Bain & Company, India's e-retail market is around $60 billion today and is expected to roughly triple to $170-190 billion by 2030, on a base of more than 270 million online shoppers. The engine is not the metros. Tier II and smaller cities already drive around 80% of ecommerce growth. GenZ accounts for 40%-45% of India’s online shoppers with spend per shopper rising more than twice as fast as any other cohort. This is the segment to build for since digital behaviour and aspiration run deep here. They carry metro taste with non-metro budgets. The demand has already moved. The infrastructure to serve it well has not.
Access still remains a significant gap for the Bharat consumer and here it means affordability and convenience. They can still get the branded products online through traditional ecommerce platforms to fulfil their growing aspirations. But most products available on those platforms don't fit their budgets and are often not what mass Bharat buys. What mass Bharat usually buys is available in unorganised offline city markets, usually 30-50% lower priced products than what's available on traditional ecommerce platforms.
But the offline city market lacks aspiration. What is lacking in their life today is the option to buy better brands, better products with better service within their budget. The ecommerce and qcommerce model in metros isn’t built to cater to this problem and this consumer. Hence a copy paste approach will not work.
This is why value comes first. A product is "inaccessible" to the Bharat consumer not because it is not available online but because it sits outside their budget. The willingness to buy branded goods over an unbranded substitute is real, but does not lead to paying a metro premium for it. The moment aspiration costs meaningfully more than the alternative, the purchase does not happen. Access, in this market, begins with a better brand or product at a price the consumer considers fair.
Convenience is the second lever, and it is just as decisive. Local retail does not offer the same assortment as online. Even the online marketplaces that stock it deliver too slow and carry a lingering doubt about product fidelity. Fast delivery and a wide, trustworthy assortment are not premium features in Bharat. They are the difference between a successful order and an abandoned cart.
Now look at why the incumbents do not close this gap, yet. Horizontal marketplaces reach these cities but arrive slow and don't fit their budget. Quick commerce, for all its promise, was built for grocery-adjacent convenience in the metros and maybe for affluent audiences in Tier II cities, not for curated aspirations at a Bharat price point.
A straight copy-paste of the metro quick commerce model into these markets misreads the customer entirely. On the other hand, offline retail cannot deliver the convenience and assortment these consumers actually want. Each was built for a different customer, in a different city, in a different decade.
This is where the opportunity sits, and it is enormous. The next defining commerce company in India will not win on discovery, because discovery is already free and universal. It will win on access, redefined for this consumer as the right brands and products, at a price they find fair, delivered fast, from an assortment far wider than any shop in their city can offer. Deliver aspiration while solving value and convenience together, and you unlock a consumer that everyone can already see but almost no one is serving well.
Discovery was the last decade's battle and it is over. Access, redefined around value and convenience, is the next one–it is wide open.
(Naman Lahoty is a Partner at Stellaris Venture Partners)
(Disclaimer: The views and opinions expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of YourStory.)

articles.title: Bitget hacked via zero-day in third-party security products
articles.text:
Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget revealed today that attackers who stole $387.5 million last week breached its systems after exploiting a zero-day flaw in third-party security products.
According to Bitget, two separate investigations by blockchain security firm SlowMist and Google Cloud's cyber-defense arm Mandiant said the threat actors accessed Bitget's wallet environment after compromising two security appliances with zero-day exploits.
After the breach, the attackers dropped web shells on one of the hacked appliances and malware on the crypto exchange's production wallet job server, as well as a custom withdrawal tool used to launch the cryptocurrency theft after midnight on September 25.
"The earliest malicious activity identified in the available logs dates to August 31. A service running on one of Product A's nodes was affected by a zero-day vulnerability. The attacker ran a hidden script under the service process, launched a command to read the environment variable containing the database password, and connected to the database. Similar hidden-script activity was observed on two other nodes on September 23 and September 25," SlowMist said.
"Forensic findings indicate that on September 24, 2026, a threat actor gained unauthorised privileged access to Bitget's third party security appliances A and B. The threat actor deployed a web shell onto the security appliance B and established a Command-and-Control (C2) connection. Using the persistent access on security appliance B, the threat actor moved laterally to Bitget's production wallet job server and deployed malicious packages," Mandiant added.
SlowMist added that the earliest crypto theft transfer occurred on September 02:31 (UTC+8) and the last took place at 05:23, with the attack spanning nearly 3 hours across multiple blockchains.
Bitget suspended all withdrawals on Thursday after detecting multiple unauthorized transfers from its hot and warm crypto wallets and discovering that attackers had stolen $387.5 million from them.
CEO Gracy Chen noted the incident affected multiple assets, including ETH, XRP, BNB, AVAX, USDT, USDC, and other tokens, and involved the Ethereum, XRP Ledger, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, BSC, and Base chains.
Chen also blamed the attack on North Korean hackers, citing IP behavior patterns and on-chain analysis as evidence, and added that they breached a critical backend system within Bitget's wallet infrastructure that was later used to spoof transaction data, triggering the exchange's authorization process to move funds out of compromised hot/warm wallets.
North Korean hackers have been behind many other major crypto heists, including the Bybit hack, in which they stole $1.5 billion from the crypto exchange's ETH cold wallet.
Since the breach, Bitget has launched a Recovery Bounty Program that offers bounties of 5% to those who help recover or freeze funds stolen in the attack.
A Bitget spokesperson was not immediately available when BleepingComputer contacted them earlier today for more information on the zero-day flaw and the third-party security products compromised in the attack.

articles.title: Microsoft déploie sa mise à jour Windows 11 26H2, voici ce que ça change
articles.text:
La mise à jour majeure annuelle de Windows 11 est en cours de déploiement. Windows 11 26H2 ne devrait néanmoins pas changer grand-chose sur votre PC. Cette mise à jour ne contient en effet aucune nouveauté par rapport aux précédentes mises à jour mensuelles. Car pour cette mise à jour, Microsoft a adopté un schéma similaire à celui qu’elle avait mis en place avec la version 25H2 de son système d’exploitation.
Windows 11 26H2 est un simple paquet d’activation qui ne pèse guère plus de quelques kilo-octets et dont le déploiement ne permet rien d’autre que d’activer les fonctionnalités déjà existantes sur votre PC mais dormantes. Cette mise à jour annuelle, qui repose donc sur la même branche que Windows 11 24H2 et 25H2, ne devrait prendre que quelques minutes à s’installer avec un seul redémarrage. Elle fera par ailleurs passer le numéro de version de votre système à la build 26300 (au lieu de 26200 pour la mise à jour 25H2).
L’objectif principal de cette mise à jour pour Microsoft et de prolonger la durée du support de son OS. Les versions Famille et Professionnel de Windows 11 24H2 atteignent en effet leur fin de support pour ce 13 octobre 2026. L’arrivée de la mise à jour 26H2 repousse ce support jusqu’au mois d’octobre 2028. En conservant le même code que celui utilisé dans les version 24H2 et 25H2, Microsoft entend privilégier la stabilité en limitant les risques de bugs ou de conflits de pilotes.
Des nouvelles fonctionnalités enfin activées chez tout le monde
Comme nous l’avons mentionné, cette mise à jour 26H2 de Windows 11 n’introduit aucune nouvelle fonctionnalité exclusive. Elle intègre les améliorations que Microsoft a déployées au compte-gouttes au cours des derniers mois.
Parmi les plus importantes, vous retrouverez donc la possibilité de repositionner la barre des tâches en haut ou sur les côtés gauche et droit du bureau dans les Paramètres de personnalisation de Windows 11. L’option permettant d’afficher une barre des tâches avec une taille réduite devrait également être accessible à tous après l’installation de cette mise à jour.
Autre nouveauté activée chez tous les utilisateurs, le nouveau menu Démarrer personnalisable. L’option, qui a déjà été activée chez certains utilisateurs au cours des dernières mises à jour permet de choisir la taille du menu Démarrer, mais également d’opter pour un nouvel affichage des applications.
Le moteur de recherche de Windows qui intégrait jusqu’à présent les résultats du Web issus de Bing peut à présent être configuré pour désactiver ces derniers. De la même manière, il est possible de supprimer les suggestions du Microsoft Store pour privilégier la recherche de fichiers stockés localement sur la machine.
Votre PC est-il compatible avec Windows 11 26H2 ?
Après avoir testé Windows 11 26H2 dans le canal Release Preview auprès des membres de son programme Insider, Microsoft avait commencé à diffuser, il y a quelques jours, les images disques ISO des versions d’évaluation de sa mise à jour 26H2 auprès des entreprises.
Cette mise à jour sera proposée via Windows Update à toutes les machines fonctionnant sous Windows 11 24H4 et 25H2, qu’elles soient animées par une puce Intel, AMD ou Snapdragon X de première génération.
À noter toutefois que les PC équipés d’une puce Snapdragon X2 ou Nvidia RTX Spark fonctionnant sous Windows 11 26H1 ne passeront pas à la version 26H2 via le module de mise à jour de Windows. Elles seront directement mises à jour vers Windows 11 27H2 à compter de la fin de l’année 2027, Microsoft ayant a priori prévu de regroupe les branches 26H1 et 26H2 à ce moment.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Microsoft

articles.title: How 297 job applications led Bode Roberts to build Dataleum
articles.text:
When Bode Roberts struggled to break into the workforce, he realised the problem was not his drive; the system itself was broken. So, instead of waiting for a seat at someone else’s table, he built his own. In his latest My Life in Tech feature, JOHN ADOYI chronicles how Roberts turned years of job-hunting silence into Dataleum, an award-winning EdTech platform transforming African talent into a global export.
297 applications. 48 interviews. Three years without a job.
For Bode Roberts, co-founder of the edtech platform Dataleum, those numbers were more than a record of an unsuccessful job search. They represented three years of hope, rejection, and uncertainty, and eventually forced him to confront what it meant to measure his worth by whether someone would employ him.
“It was a cycle of hope followed by the heavy silence of rejection,” Roberts says.
Some interviews seemed promising. Some applications carried the possibility that things might finally change. Then came the silence, again and again.
“There were moments of genuine confusion and tears,” he says. “The weight of ‘not having work’ began to feel like a commentary on my worth.”
The experience changed the question Roberts was asking. Instead of asking how he could find his place in the workforce, he began thinking about how to make it easier for others to find theirs.
Looking back, Roberts says the experience changed how he understood unemployment.
“I realised that if someone with my background and drive was struggling this much, the system itself was broken,” he says.
That realisation changed the question he was trying to answer. Instead of asking how he could find his place in the workforce, Roberts began thinking about how to make it easier for others to find theirs.
Years later, that shift would help shape Dataleum, the edtech platform he co-founded.
“I am actually grateful for those 48 rejections,” Roberts says. “They were the fuel I needed to build my own table.”
But Roberts’ concern with opportunity began long before he started applying for jobs.
His understanding of opportunity began taking shape in childhood.
Roberts attended a private school while his mother taught in the public school system. He says he sometimes accompanied her to work, where he saw classrooms meant for dozens of pupils packed with more than 300 children. He also saw students sitting on the floor and struggling with basic literacy.
“Talent is universal, but opportunity is not,” Roberts says.
Roberts says he also spent much of his childhood around people older than him. While other children played typical playground games, he played Monopoly, Ludo and cards with adult neighbours.
“Those weren’t just games; they were my first lessons in negotiation, strategic thinking, and emotional intelligence,” he says. “My environment taught me how to navigate spaces where I was the youngest person in the room.”
He says he was drawn to numbers from an early age and became the top mathematics student in his primary school. In 2002, he won the Milo Nestlé award for his mathematical abilities. His interest in solving problems also led him to start his first business while he was still in secondary school.
In 2009, Roberts began studying Computer Engineering at Covenant University, a private university in Ogun State, southwest Nigeria. But he was interested in more than how machines worked. He wanted to understand how technology could be used to solve problems for people.
He treated his university years as a period of experimentation. Roberts says he started about 16 businesses as an undergraduate, using each one to learn about suppliers, customers, marketing, negotiation, and sales.
“Those weren’t just side hustles; they were my real-world classroom,” he says. “I was negotiating with suppliers, sourcing products, managing customer experiences, and marketing to my peers.”
He graduated in 2014 and later pursued a master’s degree in Production and Operations Management because, he says, he wanted to understand how technology could be implemented and scaled within businesses.
His time at Lagos Business School further changed how he thought about building businesses. Roberts says the programme shifted his focus from business survival to long-term sustainability.
“It wasn’t just about learning theory; it was about building relationships with leaders across various sectors who were all grappling with the same question: How do we build businesses that last in Africa?” he says.
After school, Roberts moved into banking. It was there, while working at a financial institution, that he said he encountered a problem that would later lead to Dataleum.
Despite working in a high-growth environment, he says he struggled to find accessible opportunities to upskill. Training was either unavailable or too expensive.
He discussed the problem with his friend and future co-founder, Titilola Bello. They realised that if working professionals were struggling to access quality digital training, the problem could be even greater for unemployed young people.
That conversation became the starting point for Dataleum.
Building Dataleum
Roberts and Bello tested the idea before building a business around it. Roberts says they spoke to 20 people during an early feasibility study, 15 of whom validated the need for accessible and affordable digital skills training.
When they launched their first marketing campaign, 27 people expressed interest. One organisation then paid upfront for 10 training slots, giving Dataleum its first revenue.
“That initial revenue allowed us to build gradually,” Roberts says.
As the company grew, it began working with organisations including the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund, Access Bank, the United Nations, Coca-Cola and Flutterwave.
Building Dataleum also meant making a difficult decision about his career. Roberts left his banking job to lead the company full-time, a move he says was followed by “incredibly rough” months that tested his resolve.
Seven months after Dataleum launched, the company was still operating from a physical training centre when the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted operations in March 2020. It forced Dataleum to rethink how it delivered training.
In March 2020, Dataleum launched a virtual data hackathon, or what he calls “Datathon”. The event brought data analysts from different locations together online.
“Despite the global standstill, we saw data analysts from all over logging in to compete,” he says.
Roberts says the Datathon changed how he viewed Dataleum’s reach. What had started as a physical training centre in Lagos could now bring people together regardless of where they were.
Dataleum expanded into the UK in 2023. Roberts says it became a registered learning centre with the UK Register of Learning Providers within two months.
But the expansion exposed a different challenge. Roberts says many Nigerian Dataleum alumni who had moved to the UK were struggling to navigate the labour market, particularly those from underrepresented groups and people of colour.
“While Nigeria is a familiar, high-volume market for us, the UK is a market of high standards and specific community needs,” he says.
Roberts says Dataleum responded by placing greater emphasis on community-building and support for immigrants and minority communities navigating the UK labour market.
Three years after Dataleum launched, the company won the Lagos State Startup of the Year award. In 2023, it also received the Best EdTech Startup in Africa award at the Global Startup Awards.
“Standing on a stage with innovators from across the globe and hearing Dataleum named the best on the continent was a profound testament to our impact,” he says.
Becoming a builder
Running Dataleum has also changed how Roberts thinks about leadership.
He says he began as an operator, shaped by the hands-on approach he developed while running businesses at university. When Dataleum launched, he was still experimenting with different leadership styles as he worked to get the company off the ground.
As the company grew and he began leading professionals from different generations, Roberts says he realised that leadership required something different.
“High-performance teams aren’t built on ‘command and control,’ but on servant leadership,” he says. “To lead the younger generation, you must be a listener.”
Today, Roberts describes himself as moving into what he calls the “Legacy Builder” phase. His focus, he says, is less on managing every operation and more on creating an environment where other leaders can emerge.
“My goal is no longer just to manage operations, but to architect an environment where other leaders can emerge. I want to ensure that impact isn’t just something we do internally; I want to inspire a movement of young leaders who are on that same ‘impact thread.’”
That shift is tied to what Roberts sees as a larger challenge for Africa. He calls the continent’s talent the “African Asset” and believes much of it remains untapped.
“I believe African talent is the untapped engine the world needs to solve its most complex problems,” he says. “My greatest pressure is ensuring we are building the right infrastructure to make that talent economically viable.”
For Roberts, the impact of developing talent extends beyond the person who takes a course or gets a job. He says he also thinks about the families and businesses that can benefit when people gain access to better opportunities.
“It’s not just about the student who takes a course today,” he says. “It’s about the family that is lifted out of poverty because that student got a global job.”
His experience with the UNDP’s Young Africa Innovates programme in 2025 also exposed him to entrepreneurs who are often excluded from mainstream opportunities, including people with disabilities and founders from underserved communities. Roberts says the experience reinforced his belief that Africa’s progress must include people who are often left behind.
For Roberts, the longer-term goal is to build systems and develop people who can outlast his time as CEO.
“I want to ensure that impact isn’t just something we do internally,” he says. “My leadership today is about building systems and people that will outlast my own tenure as CEO.”
‘The catalyst of human potential’
Roberts’ ambitions now extend beyond Dataleum. Over the next 10 years, he wants the company to become what he describes as a sustainable African talent ecosystem, helping Africa move from consuming technology to exporting innovation.
He is also pursuing a PhD at Covenant University on the impact of artificial intelligence on operational efficiency in systemically important banks. Roberts says he wants to understand how emerging technologies can be applied in the African context and contribute to global knowledge.
But when asked what would remain if everything he had built disappeared, Roberts returns to the qualities that existed before Dataleum, the awards and the titles.
“At my core, I am a practitioner of ‘opportunity maximization.’ Even with nothing, I would still have my faith in God, the resilience my parents instilled in me, and the integrity that has guided every decision.”
He says he would still be a builder, with problems to solve and people to empower.
“I hope the narrative isn’t about the awards I won, but about the thousands of tables I helped create for others to sit at,” he says.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: MrBeast cambia las cámaras de YouTube por Shark Tank y se prepara para invertir en emprendedores
articles.text:
MrBeast, uno de los creadores de contenido más populares de YouTube, se sumará a Shark Tank como inversor invitado de su temporada 18. Jimmy Donaldson, su nombre real, participará en el programa de ABC, donde tendrá que evaluar propuestas de emprendedores y decidir si invierte su propio dinero en sus negocios.
La nueva temporada se estrenará el 30 de septiembre de 2026 con un episodio especial de dos horas. Además de MrBeast, el programa contará con otros invitados, como la actriz Mindy Kaling, el exjugador de la NFL J. J. Watt y el empresario Steven Bartlett. También participarán Erin y Sara Foster, fundadoras de la marca Favorite Daughter.
PUBLICIDAD
La presencia de Donaldson supone un nuevo paso en su trayectoria empresarial. El creador de contenido, conocido por sus desafíos con premios millonarios, ha construido un negocio que va mucho más allá de YouTube y ahora tendrá que analizar los proyectos de otros emprendedores.
MrBeast llega a Shark Tank como inversor invitado
En la temporada 18 de Shark Tank, MrBeast se incorporará al grupo de empresarios que evalúan propuestas de inversión. Su participación consistirá en escuchar a los emprendedores, conocer sus proyectos y decidir si está dispuesto a aportar capital a cambio de una participación en sus empresas.
El programa cuenta con un elenco habitual integrado por Barbara Corcoran, Lori Greiner, Robert Herjavec, Daymond John, Daniel Lubetzky, Kevin O’Leary, Kendra Scott y Rashaun Williams. A ellos se sumarán diferentes inversores invitados a lo largo de los episodios.
PUBLICIDAD
Donaldson no llegará únicamente por su popularidad en internet. ABC lo presenta como el creador del canal MrBeast y fundador de Beast Industries, la compañía que agrupa buena parte de sus negocios. Su experiencia en el desarrollo de marcas y productos de consumo constituye parte de su trayectoria empresarial.
La promoción oficial de la nueva temporada también apunta a que podría participar en el episodio de estreno, que tendrá una duración de dos horas. Sin embargo, ABC no ha confirmado de manera individual qué inversores invitados aparecerán en esa primera emisión.
Los negocios de MrBeast más allá de YouTube
La participación de MrBeast en Shark Tank coincide con la expansión de su negocio fuera de las plataformas digitales. Una de sus principales apuestas es Feastables, su marca de alimentos que comenzó con barras de chocolate y amplió posteriormente su catálogo. Sus productos se comercializan en grandes cadenas estadounidenses, como Walmart, Target, Costco y 7-Eleven.
PUBLICIDAD
Otra de sus iniciativas es Beast Games, un programa de competencias que trasladó el formato de sus populares videos de YouTube a Amazon Prime Video. La producción reúne a participantes que compiten en desafíos por premios económicos y ya ha avanzado en la preparación de su segunda temporada.
Donaldson también incursionó en el mercado de los alimentos con Lunchly, una marca que desarrolló junto a Logan Paul y KSI. A esto se suma Viewstats, una plataforma de análisis y herramientas para creadores de contenido que cofundó para facilitar el seguimiento del rendimiento de los videos.
Su expansión también llegó al mundo editorial. En septiembre de 2026, publicó junto al escritor James Patterson la novela The Most Dangerous Games, un thriller centrado en una competencia extrema cuyo premio asciende a 1.000 millones de dólares.
PUBLICIDAD
Estos proyectos muestran cómo Donaldson ha diversificado sus actividades, desde los contenidos digitales hasta los productos de consumo, el entretenimiento y la publicación de libros.
Cuándo se estrena Shark Tank y dónde verlo
La temporada 18 de Shark Tank se estrenará el miércoles 30 de septiembre de 2026 en ABC, con un episodio especial de dos horas. En Estados Unidos, los espectadores también podrán acceder a la producción a través de Hulu.
Además de MrBeast, la nueva entrega contará con invitados de distintos ámbitos, desde el entretenimiento hasta el deporte y los negocios. Entre ellos figuran Mindy Kaling, J. J. Watt, Steven Bartlett y las hermanas Erin y Sara Foster.
PUBLICIDAD
La incorporación de Donaldson permitirá que los espectadores vean al creador de contenido en un papel diferente al que lo hizo conocido en internet. En lugar de organizar desafíos con premios millonarios, tendrá que analizar las propuestas de otros empresarios y decidir en cuáles está dispuesto a invertir su dinero.

articles.title: Opus siempre fue el modelo caro de Anthropic. Ha bastado con poner a Fable encima para que empiece a parecer más accesible
articles.text:
Anthropic lanzó hace una semana Claude Opus 5.5, un modelo que según sus propias pruebas rinde como Fable 5.1 en buena parte de las tareas y cuesta menos que el Opus anterior: 4 dólares por millón de tokens de entrada y 20 por millón de salida.
Nominalmente, ni siquiera es el modelo tope de la casa. Pero sí es el más comentado y además ha ganado enteros para ser usado en el día a día. El motivo no tiene tanto que ver con la tecnología como con la economía conductual.
Qué ha ocurrido. Anthropic asegura que Opus 5.5 mejora a sus predecesores en casi todas las áreas de una batería de unas 2.000 evaluaciones, con el salto más visible en programación y agentes, el terreno de Claude Code.
Eso explica una parte del entusiasmo. Pero la otra tiene nombre propio: Fable, el escalón que Anthropic colocó por encima de Opus hace unos meses.
El contraste. Opus ha sido durante años el techo del catálogo. El modelo que se sacaba para el trabajo difícil, como el cuchillo bueno que no se usa para untar mantequilla sino para el día de entrecot. Cada uso venía con una pregunta: "¿esta tarea merece lo que cuesta Opus, o me conformo con Sonnet y no quemo la cuota?".
Con Fable arriba, la duda ha cambiado. Ya no se discute si pagar el modelo caro, sino si hace falta subir hasta Fable o si basta con el de abajo. Opus ha pasado de lujo muy puntual a lujo asumible.
En mi caso he notado que uso más Opus desde que llegó 5.5, y no creo ser el único.
- En las pruebas de Every, Opus 5.5 ha desplazado a Fable como modelo de diario de uno de sus ingenieros en cuestión de días.
- En OpenRouter ha procesado más de un billón de tokens en su primera semana.
- Las cuentas ayudan porque Fable cuesta 10 dólares por millón de tokens de entrada y 50 por millón de salida, más del doble, y en la batería de pruebas de Endor Labs la misma factura ha sido de 116 dólares con Opus 5.5 frente a 672 con Fable.
Demasiado bueno para no tanta diferencia en rendimiento.
El trasfondo. Joel Huber, John Payne y Christopher Puto describieron en 1982 cómo una tercera opción altera la preferencia entre las dos que ya existían. Se llama 'efecto Decoy' ("efecto señuelo"). Dan Ariely, autor del estupendo 'Predeciblemente irracional', lo popularizó poniendo como ejemplo una oferta de suscripción a The Economist:
UN VISTAZO A...
- Digital: 59 dólares.
- Papel: 125 dólares.
- Papel más digital: 125 dólares.
Con las tres opciones, el 84% de sus alumnos del MIT, participando en un experimento, escogió el combinado y nadie el papel. Al retirar esa opción que nadie quería, el 68% se ha fue a la digital.
Sí, pero. Llamar señuelo a Fable sería forzar el concepto, porque Fable tiene sus propias capacidades únicas y tareas donde justifica perfectamente su precio. Lo que opera aquí se parece más al efecto compromiso, esa tendencia a huir de los extremos cuando hay tres niveles.
Es la lógica que se suele atribuir a la Triple Whopper de Burger King. Si ves la normal y la doble, la doble parece un exceso. Pero si añades a la triple justo al lado, la doble deja de parecer un exceso y pasa a ser la opción intermedia. Eso se traduce en más ventas de la doble que antes de introducir la triple
Entre bambalinas. En el último MWC le pregunté a la directora de marketing de Xiaomi cómo iban a medir el éxito del Xiaomi 17 Ultra. La respuesta predecible hubiese sido hablar de sus propias ventas. Pero su respuesta apuntó a si lograba impulsar las ventas de la serie T. La intermedia.
El móvil de 1.500 euros no necesita venderse mucho. Necesita que el de 600 o el de 800 parezcan una decisión adecuada y ganen tracción.
¿Principal ganador? Opus, y con él, la escalera que ha montado Anthropic. No sabemos si Anthropic ha diseñado Fable pensando en empujar el uso Opus, pero tampoco hace falta.
Quien antes dudaba entre el modelo de diario y el caro ahora duda entre el caro y el carísimo. En esa conversación, 20 dólares por millón de tokens suenan como un Xiaomi 15T Pro: equilibrio y sentido común sin excesos.
