articles.title: Egyptian fintech startup Paymob raises $35m pre-Series C funding round - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian startup Paymob, the leading payments infrastructure service provider in the MENA region, has secured US$35 million in a pre-Series C funding round to support its ongoing expansion across the region.
Founded in 2015 by Islam Shawky, Alain El Hajj and Mostafa Menessy, Paymob is an infrastructure technology enabler providing payment solutions to empower digital financial service providers through mobile wallet technology.
Its omnichannel gateway offers more than 60 payment solutions and empowers close to 350,000 merchants with access to innovative financial services. It has expanded to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Saudi Arabia and Oman.
Disrupt Africa reported in September 2024 Paymob had extended its Series B round to US$72 million, and it has now secured US$35 million in pre-Series C funding in a round co-led by Mubadala Investment Company, an Abu Dhabi-based sovereign investor, and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD). British International Investment, Global Ventures and DPI Ventures also took part in the raise.
The fresh capital will support Paymob’s ongoing growth across MENA, by scaling its core digital payments acceptance operations and by rolling out new products aimed at SME merchants and at agentic commerce use cases. Paymob has onboarded around 20,000 merchants across its three GCC markets since it received its Retail Payment Services Licence from the Central Bank of the UAE in January 2025.
“Paymob morphed into a regional platform over the past 18 months, propelled by the exponential growth of our GCC business. This pre-Series C funding round will help us accelerate our growth plan across the MENA region and fast-track our product roadmap to become the go-to payments platform for agentic commerce. We are very excited about Mubadala joining our cap table and grateful for the continued support of our existing shareholders,” Shawky, Paymob’s CEO, said.

articles.title: Spotify está caído a nivel mundial y millones de usuarios no pueden escuchar música
articles.text:
Spotify está experimentando fallas relacionadas con iniciar sesión tanto en la página web como en la aplicación móvil. De acuerdo con Downdetector, las fallas en países como Estados Unidos se concentran en un 57% en la app.
La plataforma streaming ya reconoció las fallas y afirmó que se encuentra trabajando para solucionar los errores.
PUBLICIDAD
“Somos conscientes de algunos problemas para iniciar sesión y los estamos revisando. Les mantendremos informados aquí”, fue la primera declaración de la compañía a través de la cuenta de X, Spotify Cares.
Más adelante, la empresa de streaming dijo en su cuenta principal: “Somos conscientes de los problemas que afectan a la aplicación de Spotify y estamos trabajando activamente para solucionarlos”.
Spotify recomienda activar las actualizaciones automáticas en el celular para acceder de forma inmediata a la solución cuando sea implementada.
La empresa en 2026 alcanzó los 761 millones de usuarios activos mensuales y 293 millones de suscriptores premium.
Qué fallas están reportando los usuarios de Spotify
El principal problema reportado por los usuarios ante la caída de Spotify, según Downdetector, fue la imposibilidad de iniciar sesión en la plataforma.
Además, algunas personas señalaron fallas para reproducir música y episodios de pódcasts, mientras que otras encontraron dificultades para buscar canciones, artistas o listas de reproducción. La interrupción afectó sobre todo a quienes intentaban cargar contenido nuevo o acceder a sus cuentas desde la aplicación.
PUBLICIDAD
En cambio, algunos usuarios que ya tenían música en reproducción o canciones descargadas pudieron continuar escuchándolas. Spotify reconoció que estaba al tanto de los inconvenientes y que investigaba el origen de la falla.
Ante las fallas de Spotify, usuarios también recurrieron a X para informar problemas de acceso, reproducción y búsqueda de contenido.
En esa red social, varias personas compartieron mensajes de error y dificultades para iniciar sesión o reproducir música y pódcasts. Spotify respondió que estaba al tanto de los inconvenientes y que revisaba la situación.
La empresa además recomienda mantener activadas las actualizaciones automáticas de la aplicación para recibir correcciones y mejoras cuando estén disponibles. La sugerencia apunta a que los usuarios cuenten con la versión más reciente de la plataforma, aunque no resuelve por sí sola una interrupción del servicio
PUBLICIDAD
Qué nuevas funciones hay en Spotify
Spotify incorporó nuevas funciones orientadas a que los usuarios encuentren contenido y controlen la reproducción mediante inteligencia artificial. Una de las principales novedades es Talk to Spotify, una herramienta que permite pedir música, pódcasts o audiolibros con la voz o por escrito.
Los usuarios pueden solicitar recomendaciones, ajustar el estilo de una lista, consultar datos sobre un artista o recuperar información sobre sus hábitos de escucha. La función se encuentra en fase beta para usuarios Premium mayores de 18 años en Estados Unidos, Irlanda y Suecia.
La plataforma también amplió Prompted Playlist, que crea listas a partir de instrucciones en lenguaje natural.
Esta herramienta ya se utilizaba para música y pódcasts, y ahora se extendió a los audiolibros: permite pedir selecciones según un género, una temática, el tiempo disponible o las preferencias personales. La novedad se habilitó en beta para usuarios Premium elegibles de Estados Unidos, Canadá, Reino Unido, Irlanda, Australia, Nueva Zelanda y Suecia.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, Spotify presentó Studio by Spotify Labs, una aplicación independiente para computadoras que permite generar experiencias de audio privadas y personalizadas, como resúmenes diarios, listas para viajes o pódcasts creados según los intereses del usuario.
La herramienta puede vincularse, con autorización, con servicios como el calendario, el correo electrónico y las notas. Su despliegue comenzó como una prueba para usuarios Premium mayores de 18 años en más de 20 mercados.
Otra incorporación es la integración con Muse, el agente personal de Meta. A través de conversaciones con ese asistente, los usuarios pueden reproducir canciones, guardar temas en su biblioteca, crear listas y buscar pódcasts o audiolibros.

articles.title: MTN’s US lawsuit moves to discovery after judge rejects appeal bid
articles.text:
MTN, Africa’s largest mobile network operator, has failed to halt two terrorism-related lawsuits in the United States (US) after a federal judge rejected its latest bids to reopen earlier rulings and appeal immediately, clearing the way for discovery.
In publicly available court documents, US District Judge Carol Bagley Amon denied MTN’s requests for reconsideration and permission for an immediate appeal in Zobay v. MTN Group Limited and the related Long case. The decision means the two cases will move into discovery, where both sides can seek and exchange evidence.
The ruling keeps alive claims that MTN’s former operations in Iran and Afghanistan assisted entities allegedly linked to terrorist attacks, exposing the telecoms group to further litigation in the US. The court has not found MTN liable, and the allegations remain unproven. MTN says it expects the evidence to demonstrate that it was not a culpable participant in the attacks.
The case centres on allegations concerning MTN’s former telecommunications operations in Iran and Afghanistan. The plaintiffs claim, among other things, that MTN’s activities involving Irancell, Iran’s second-largest mobile operator, assisted entities they allege were connected to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
The IRGC, which the US designated as a terrorist organisation in 2019, is central to the allegations, while the plaintiffs also claim that MTN’s operations in Afghanistan included shutting down cell towers at the Taliban’s request.
MTN maintains that the ruling does not determine whether the allegations against it are true. “The rulings are procedural and do not constitute a finding of wrongdoing or liability against MTN,” the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
The court’s earlier decisions only found that certain claims could proceed past the motion-to-dismiss stage. MTN said US procedure meant it could not challenge the factual allegations against it at that point.
“In the next phases of the litigation, MTN will, for the first time, have an opportunity to produce and solicit evidence to disprove plaintiffs’ allegations,” the company said.
The allegations have not been proven, but Judge Amon’s September 25 order offers a detailed explanation of why she declined MTN’s request to revisit her earlier decisions.
What MTN faces
MTN had argued that a 2025 Second Circuit ruling in Ashley v. Deutsche Bank changed the legal standard for terrorism-related aiding-and-abetting claims. Amon disagreed, finding that the later decision did not warrant reconsideration of her earlier rulings.
The judge distinguished the allegations against MTN from cases involving companies that allegedly provided routine services to customers later linked to terrorist activity.
In the Iran claims, the court pointed to allegations that MTN entered a joint venture with entities plaintiffs say were linked to the IRGC, helped source US technology for Irancell and discussed circumventing US sanctions.
The court described the alleged conduct as going beyond simply providing ordinary commercial services.
One allegation concerns “embargoed dual-use technologies” and alleged operational or technical support provided through the Irancell relationship. The court also referred to allegations that MTN knew a portion of Irancell’s profits would flow to the IRGC.
For the Afghanistan claims, the court said plaintiffs had alleged that MTN shut down cell towers at the Taliban’s request, and that the shutdowns “substantially contributed” to attacks. The judge found the allegation sufficient for the case to proceed at this stage, but the plaintiffs will ultimately need to prove it.
MTN disputes the allegations and says it expects the evidence to show that it was not responsible for the attacks at issue.
“MTN has deep sympathy for those who have been injured or lost loved ones as a result of the conflicts in Iraq and Afghanistan. MTN continues to believe that the evidence will demonstrate that MTN was not a culpable participant in the attacks at issue. MTN will continue to defend the proceedings vigorously, consider all available legal options and update shareholders on material developments as appropriate,” the company said.
More than a legal problem
The litigation also comes as the telco continues to unwind its Middle East exposure, with Iran remaining a significant financial complication.
In its interim results for the six months ended June 30, MTN said the escalation of conflict in Iran had affected Irancell’s operational performance. The group recognised its attributable portion of a R3.9 billion ($238.4 million) impairment relating to Irancell’s assets.
MTN said sanctions on Iran’s Central Bank create a secondary-sanctions risk if foreign currency is allocated to an MTN entity to facilitate repayment of receivables or loans.
“Considering the continued uncertainty of when the sanctions will be lifted, the Group has classified about R2 billion ($122.3 million) of the outstanding receivables as non-current as the settlement is neither planned nor likely to occur in the foreseeable future,” MTN said in its interim results.
The company’s latest legal disclosure therefore sits alongside a broader business problem: MTN is trying to exit a region where its remaining Iranian exposure is affected by sanctions, geopolitical instability and now continuing US litigation.
For the Zobay and Long cases, however, the immediate next step is narrower.
Discovery will allow the parties to obtain and exchange evidence before potential summary judgment applications. If the parties do not seek summary judgment, or if such applications are denied, the litigation can proceed further.
MTN said there were no material updates on the separate Cabrera and Chand & Davis cases. The Cabrera case concerns allegations linked primarily to MTN’s former operations in Afghanistan, while the separate Chand and Davis cases involve allegations concerning the company’s investment in Iranian operator Irancell and attacks in Iraq and Afghanistan. MTN disputes the allegations in both matters.

articles.title: Google fixe la date de mort de ChromeOS, à quelques jours du Googlebook
articles.text:
En septembre 2023, Google s’engageait publiquement sur dix ans de mises à jour pour les Chromebook. Trois ans plus tard, une page d’aide destinée aux écoles et aux entreprises fixe un horizon commun à tout le parc : des mises à jour et des correctifs de sécurité « jusqu’à mi-2034 ». Passé cette date, l’avenir s’appellera Googlebook OS, et tous les modèles n’y auront pas droit.
Lire aussi : Les Googlebooks débarquent – les 7 détails qui font des nouveaux PC Google des machines pas comme les autres
Dernier arrêt pour ChromeOS
La page indique que « les appareils ChromeOS continueront de recevoir des mises à jour régulières et des correctifs de sécurité jusqu’à mi-2034 ». Chaque machine conserve sa date de fin de support individuelle, fixée par la politique de mise à jour automatique, mais ce plafond s’impose désormais à toutes. Le document accompagne l’arrivée du Googlebook, le portable sous Android dévoilé en mai avec Acer, Asus, Dell, HP et Lenovo, qui arriverait en France dès les premiers jours d’octobre.
Pour la suite, « de nombreux modèles récents de Chromebook commerciaux pourront passer à Googlebook OS », parfois par migration directe. La liste des machines éligibles n’a pas été publiée, le sort des modèles écartés n’est pas évoqué, et les Chromebook grand public ne sont pas mentionnés dans ce plan de migration. Les outils d’administration pour les entreprises et les écoles n’arriveront pas avant le second semestre 2027, le lancement de cette année visant le grand public.
Un Chromebook commercialisé en 2026 aurait dû, promesse de 2023 oblige, recevoir des mises à jour jusqu’en 2036. Il s’arrêtera comme les autres à mi-2034, deux ans plus tôt, avec pour seule perspective une migration réservée aux modèles jugés compatibles.
La date de 2034 avait déjà émergé en février, au détour de documents versés au procès antitrust américain de Google. La page d’aide transforme cette pièce de procédure en politique officielle, sans billet de blog ni communiqué, à quelques jours du lancement commercial du Googlebook. Google ne parle d’ailleurs jamais d’abandon : le vocabulaire officiel s’en tient au support « jusqu’à mi-2034 » et à la transition vers le nouveau système pour les Chromebook récents qui n’auront (finalement) pas la décennie de mises à jour.

articles.title: Helsinki-based KHOY raises €2 million to take its vacuum-packed sofa beds across Europe and the US | EU-Startups
articles.text:
KHOY Company, a Helsinki-based direct-to-consumer design and furniture company, has raised €2 million in growth funding.
The round was led by Finnish private equity investor Virta Equity, with participation from Innovestor and several angel investors.
“KHOY has solved something the furniture industry has struggled with: how to sell and ship large, bulky products across borders without the cost eating the margin. We back businesses with real, profitable growth behind them, and KHOY has a combination of a defensible product innovation and proven demand across Europe,” said Heikki Kivirinta, CEO and Partner at Virta Equity.
Founded in 2022 by Visa Friström, András Kelemen (Creative Director) and Jukka Salmikukka (COO), KHOY is a Finnish D2C design and furniture company that sells exclusively online. It makes sofa beds that are vacuum-packed into compact cardboard boxes, which expand to full size once opened at home.
The company was previously called KOTA and adopted the KHOY name in 2026, a change it says reflects its international ambitions, with the same team and ownership. Its story began with a brief from its first customer, hospitality brand BobW, which wanted a sofa bed comfortable enough for daily sleep yet practical for apartments across Europe. The resulting design won a Red Dot Design Award in 2026.
KHOY launched its first sofa bed in June 2024 and posted €4.3 million in revenue in 2025, a 13-fold jump on the previous year. It is now growing 166% year-on-year and expects to more than double its revenue this year. Over 80% of sales already come from outside Finland, with Germany and France being its biggest markets in 2025. It also recorded notable sales in the Netherlands, Italy, Belgium, Austria, Ireland, Sweden and Denmark.
“We have proven that there is strong demand for a simpler way to buy furniture online. We have grown quickly while building a profitable business, and this funding allows us to accelerate from a strong position. Our ambition is to build KHOY into a major global online brand, with European quality,” said Friström, co-founder and CEO, KHOY Company.
Its strength lies in the design, which is a departure from traditional sofa bed designs, and vacuum-packing. The KHOY Company uses premium mattresses that unfold from a sofa into a bed. The company says vacuum-packing can cut delivery costs by as much as 95% compared with conventional furniture logistics, which lets it sell directly to consumers across several markets.
The funding will be used to scale its operations across the European Union, Switzerland, and the UK, while accelerating its push into the US, where the company launched operations around two weeks ago. The company will also keep developing its product portfolio, brand and operations.
“Furniture is still an unusually local industry. Large products are expensive to store and transport, which makes international expansion difficult. Vacuum-packing changes that equation. We already know the model works across borders – for us, the next phase is about scale,” added Friström.

O Logitech G Pro é um teclado mecânico gamer da linha profissional da Logitech, com formato TKL (Tenkeyless — sem teclado numérico) — mais compacto para setups gamer competitivos. Traz switches GX Blue Clicky (clique tátil e audível a cada acionamento — sensação clássica de teclado mecânico), RGB LIGHTSYNC (iluminação sincronizada com o sistema), cabo destacável (facilita transporte e substituição) e a durabilidade Logitech em periféricos gamer premium. Com 36% de desconto, sai por menos de R$ 450.
Como escolher entre essas ofertas
As 6 ofertas cobrem categorias bem distintas — a escolha depende do que você está buscando. Para festas domésticas e ambientes sociais com potência e iluminação de balada por preço acessível, a Philco PCX7100 é a maior queda percentual da lista. Para ambientes distintos (sala e quarto) ou uso multi-room com áudio Samsung otimizado, o combo com duas soundbars HW-B400F entrega solução completa. Para quem passa muito tempo fora de casa e precisa de bateria reserva confiável, o power bank i2GO 20.000mAh com display digital é oportunidade excepcional. Para quem quer intermediário Motorola com câmera de 108MP e tela AMOLED 1.5K por preço competitivo, o Moto G77 5G é escolha completa. Para gaming casual em 1080p com bom custo-benefício em monitor 120Hz, o Samsung Essential S3 24″ atende excelente. E para gamers acostumados com layout US e switch clicky clássico, o Logitech G Pro é referência da categoria — atente ao alerta do layout.
Perguntas frequentes sobre essas ofertas
Power bank 20.000mAh vale a pena? Quantas cargas garante?
Sim, para quem passa longos períodos fora de casa. Um power bank de 20.000mAh (como o i2GO desta oferta) recarrega em média: iPhone 15 (3.349mAh) — cerca de 4 a 5 cargas completas; Galaxy S24 (4.000mAh) — cerca de 3 a 4 cargas; tablets (7.000-10.000mAh) — 1 a 2 cargas. Vale destacar que eficiência real de conversão é de cerca de 70-80% (perda por calor no processo). Para viagens, festivais, camping, trabalho externo prolongado e uso móvel intenso, capacidade de 20.000mAh atende com folga. O display digital deste modelo é diferencial forte — mostra porcentagem exata (não apenas LEDs indicadores aproximados).
Moto G77 5G vs Moto G84 ou G85: qual escolher?
Depende de disponibilidade e recursos específicos. O Moto G77 5G (desta oferta) é nova geração da linha G intermediária — traz câmera 108MP Ultra-Pixel, tela 1.5K AMOLED 120Hz e resistência aprimorada por preço competitivo. Modelos G84 e G85 são gerações anteriores mais consolidadas — trazem câmeras 50MP OIS, tela Full HD ou 1.5K AMOLED 120Hz e podem estar com preços muito atrativos por serem modelos mais antigos. Para quem quer a geração mais atual com câmera de maior resolução, o G77 vence; para quem prioriza preço mínimo com boa configuração, gerações anteriores podem atender por menos.
Layout US vs ABNT2 em teclado: qual escolher?
O ABNT2 é o layout padrão brasileiro — traz tecla “ç” dedicada, acentos em posições familiares e adaptação nativa ao português. O layout US (americano) tem disposição diferente — o “ç” é acessado por combinação de teclas (Alt+C no Windows configurado como “US Internacional”), acentos ficam em teclas específicas e a tecla Enter é menor. Para digitação profissional em português brasileiro, ABNT2 é a escolha; para gaming intenso, uso predominante em inglês ou programadores acostumados, US atende bem — vantagem: teclados US costumam ter mais variedade de modelos premium disponíveis.
Switch GX Blue Clicky vs Brown Tactile: para quem?
Os switches se dividem em três categorias principais. Blue Clicky (do Logitech G Pro desta oferta) tem clique tátil e audível a cada acionamento — sensação clássica de teclado mecânico, ideal para digitação em ambiente solitário (home office isolado, uso pessoal) e para quem gosta do feedback sonoro clássico. Brown Tactile (do Logitech G515) é meio-termo — feedback tátil sem ser barulhento, versátil para gaming + digitação em ambiente compartilhado. Red Linear é suave, sem feedback, ideal para gaming rápido. Para quem valoriza o “click clack” clássico e trabalha em ambiente próprio, Blue Clicky é a escolha; para uso em videochamadas ou ambiente com outras pessoas, Blue Clicky pode incomodar — Brown Tactile atende melhor.
Combo com 2 soundbars idênticas: quando vale?
Vale em três cenários específicos: uso multi-room (uma na sala + uma no quarto — cada TV com sua soundbar), presente estratégico (uma para você + uma de presente para família), ou configuração especial para eventos. Também é oportunidade para casas com múltiplas TVs sem soundbar — permite equipar dois ambientes com investimento único. O preço unitário efetivo (abaixo de R$ 475) é muito competitivo para soundbar Samsung. Para quem só precisa de uma soundbar, comprar unidade única em ofertas separadas atende — não vale o combo.
Monitor Samsung Essential S3 24″ vs Odyssey: qual escolher?
São duas linhas com posicionamentos distintos. O Samsung Essential S3 (desta oferta) é a linha de entrada — atende gaming casual, uso escritório e streaming com bom custo-benefício e 120Hz. A linha Odyssey é a premium gamer da Samsung — traz painéis QLED curvos, resoluções 2K/4K, taxas de 165Hz+ e recursos exclusivos para gaming competitivo. Para gaming casual em 1080p e uso híbrido (jogos + trabalho + estudo), o Essential S3 24″ atende excelente; para gaming competitivo sério ou uso profissional criativo, Odyssey vale o extra significativo.
Caixa Philco 750W para festa doméstica vale a pena?
Sim, para uso social recreativo em festas domésticas e churrascos. A Philco PCX7100 traz potência adequada (750W) para ambientes médios, luzes sincronizadas com música para clima de festa e a marca Philco consolidada. Limitações: caixas de festa domésticas nesta faixa de preço têm qualidade sonora inferior a marcas premium (JBL PartyBox, Bose) em uso musical puro — priorize a experiência festa. Para quem quer investimento acessível em caixa festeira com iluminação e bom volume, atende excelente; para uso premium em qualidade sonora ou eventos frequentes, JBL PartyBox Club 120 vale o extra significativo.
Os preços e a disponibilidade dos produtos mudam com frequência, então não deixe para depois. Acesse os links, compare os modelos e aproveite os descontos enquanto eles ainda estão disponíveis.

Nenhuma empresa participou da escolha para os links e não existiu aprovação prévia deste conteúdo, que segue independente como sempre foi.

articles.title: CData's AI gateway governs agents’ access to enterprise data - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
CData’s AI gateway governs agents’ access to enterprise data
Data connectivity and integration firm CData Software Inc. today introduced Connect AI Gateway, a platform designed to control how artificial intelligence agents choose models, use tools and access company data.
The product enters early access today, extending the company’s existing Connect AI platform and its managed Model Context Protocol offering.
The gateway gives information technology teams one place to register models, MCP servers and agents, then set rules for what each can do. It also adds a context engine that draws on the structure of connected systems, business definitions and knowledge gathered from users’ interactions. CData said the combination can improve the accuracy of agents’ answers while limiting data exposure and model costs.
CData already provides connectors to hundreds of business applications and databases. The new gateway builds on those connections to enforce a person’s permissions when an agent retrieves data or takes an action on that person’s behalf. Policies can govern access to specific rows and columns, with an audit trail showing which prompt, model, tool and policy contributed to a response.
CData said a central question for companies deploying agents is whether an answer uses the same business definitions their employees use. A request for “revenue,” for example, can return different results depending on which systems and calculations the agent selects. CData’s context engine can reuse definitions maintained in tools such as Fivetran Inc.’s dbt and Microsoft Corp.’s Power BI, alongside information about fields and relationships in source systems.
The gateway can also capture less formal knowledge from documents, conversations and corrections to agent responses. That information is held in a context graph outside individual AI models, so an organization can apply it when changing models. People can review the graph and determine what becomes shared context.
“You don’t want AI redefining revenue every time you ask a question about revenue,” said Marie Forshaw, CData’s senior vice president of product marketing.
Model routing
The gateway includes separate routing and control functions for models, MCP tools and agents. It can set token budgets and route requests according to policies, allowing a company to use a the most appropriate model for a task based on characteristics like features and cost. CData plans to add the capability for the gateway to automatically select the cheapest model, executives said.
“Initially, it’s going to be based on policy,” said Will Davis, CData’s chief marketing officer. “Eventually, it will be intelligent enough to see the prompt, see the system behavior, and be able to select the lowest-cost model that connects to the task.”
CData said its data layer can also reduce the amount of work assigned to models to save on token costs. It can filter, join and aggregate records before sending a result to a model, potentially reducing the amount of data placed in the model’s context window.
In a company-run test of 378 enterprise queries, CData said Connect AI answered 98.5% correctly, compared with 65% to 75% for other MCP providers it tested. A separate test found a cost difference of up to 175-fold between models that produced the same correct answer. Those are CData benchmarks, not measured independent tests or documented savings from a customer deployment.
The gateway reflects a shift in what CData is trying to manage. Its earlier Connect AI offering concentrated on giving AI tools governed access to enterprise systems. The new product is meant to oversee the request from the initial prompt through model selection, data retrieval and any resulting action. That broader view could help administrators investigate an agent’s behavior when an answer is wrong or an action is blocked.
CData is positioning its context engine alongside existing data management tools. Executives said it can import business definitions from analytics products, but it is not intended to replace a full data catalog or semantic layer. The initial release doesn’t support imported definitions directly from data catalogs, although that capability is planned.
Although the gateway’s semantic graph has elements of a data catalog, CData doesn’t want to enter that market. “We by no means want to be the be-all and end-all of a catalog,” Davis said. “We just want to use that information to make sure that the interactions that people and agents have with AI are accurate, efficient, and well-governed.”
Customers will also have to decide which lessons from agent interactions become shared knowledge. A correction useful to one employee could mislead others. CData said human review will govern that promotion, making the approval process a consequential part of deployment.

articles.title: Microsoft lanza la actualización de Windows 11 2026 con una función que todos esperaban
articles.text:
Como ocurre cada otoño, Microsoft ha lanzado una nueva actualización para Windows 11 que incluye varias funciones y corrige algunos de los errores más molestos. Este año, Windows 11 26H2 sigue la misma línea, solo que no se siente tan fresca como otras ediciones debido a que varias de las novedades ya debutaron en los parches mensuales opcionales. Si todavía no los instalas y quieres probarla, puedes hacerlo gratis a partir de hoy.
De acuerdo con una publicación en la web de soporte, Windows 11 26H2 se ofrece como un "paquete de habilitación". En términos más sencillos, esta versión consiste en una actualización ligera que activa funciones ya presentes en el sistema gracias a los parches mensuales anteriores. A diferencia de las versiones anteriores, los usuarios solo tienen que descargar un archivo pequeño y hacer un reinicio rápido, por lo que parece más una actualización mensual que los paquetes tradicionales.
En cuanto a novedades, Windows 11 26H2 incluye el agente de Configuración, que permite ajustar opciones del sistema con ayuda de la IA. Solo necesitas teclear la instrucción usando lenguaje natural (por ejemplo, "Cambia mi resolución de pantalla") y el agente se encargará del resto. Además, el Administrador de tareas incorpora una nueva sección que monitorea el rendimiento de la NPU en las cargas de trabajo de la IA, siempre y cuando tengas un ordenador con este chip.
Pasando a la personalización, el menú Inicio ofrece varios tamaños para configurarlo. Atrás quedó el truco con el que tenías que editar el registro de Windows, ya que ahora puedes ajustarlo a la medida y desactivar otras opciones, como la foto de perfil y el nombre de cuenta. La barra de tareas también se transforma y ahora puede colocarse en cualquier borde de la pantalla o hacerse más compacta.
Microsoft afirma que Windows 11 26H2 no dará problemas (aunque está por verse)
Uno de los sellos distintivos de cada actualización de Windows es la cantidad de problemas que genera. Algunos van desde errores visuales o periféricos que dejan de funcionar, mientras que otros son tan graves que impiden usar el ordenador. En el caso de la versión 26H2, Microsoft está convencida de que no habrá inconvenientes y que será más rápida.
"Un paquete de habilitación es una actualización ligera que activa nuevas funciones ya incluidas en el sistema operativo mediante actualizaciones mensuales previas de mantenimiento. Debido a que las versiones 26H2, 25H2 y 24H2 comparten una rama de servicio común y una base de código subyacente, muchos de los componentes necesarios para la versión 26H2 ya están presentes en los dispositivos antes de que la actualización de características esté disponible".
De cualquier modo, el despliegue de esta actualización será escalonado y Microsoft puede aplicar un bloqueo en caso de que detecte un problema mayor de compatibilidad. La actualización de Windows 11 26H2 ya está disponible desde hoy para todos los usuarios; basta con hacer clic en el botón Inicio de Windows, seleccionar Configuración > Windows Update > Buscar actualizaciones.
No está de más sugerir que vale la pena esperar un poco hasta que se confirme que esta actualización está libre de errores. Cada mes surgen reportes de fallos y muchos usuarios han optado por desfasar los parches por varias semanas, lo cual les garantiza que no serán víctimas de un descuido y se quedarán sin usar el ordenador.
Para hacerlo, solo sigue estos pasos:
- Haz clic en el botón Inicio y selecciona Configuración.
- En el menú lateral, haz clic en Windows Update.
- Busca la opción Pausar actualizaciones y haz clic en el menú desplegable para elegir "Pausar durante 5 semanas".
- Una vez hecho, Windows Update mostrará un mensaje avisando que el sistema no buscará actualizaciones hasta la fecha definida.
- Al cumplirse el plazo, Windows Update se reactivará automáticamente, aunque puedes hacerlo de forma manual.

articles.text:
The Download: OpenAI’s chief research officer explains its hacking response
Plus: Trump and tech executives have agreed to “self-regulate” AI.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
“We’re not going to shoot ourselves in the foot” over hack fallout, says OpenAI’s chief research officer
Two months after OpenAI’s agents hacked into the computers of AI company Hugging Face, the company is still dealing with the fallout. Last week brought news of another hack, this time into Australia’s national health-care system, which the government says OpenAI did not report for 84 days.
But OpenAI insists it is not on the back foot. “I do kind of reject the premise that OpenAI is a company with visible impacts in the world and therefore OpenAI is not training safe and aligned models,” says Mark Chen, the company’s chief research officer.
In many ways, the buck stops with Chen. I sat down with him to talk about the fallout from the hacks, what his company is doing about it, and why he thinks things are not as bad as they seem.
Here’s what he told me about making models safer—and why the world is better off with OpenAI in it.
—Will Douglas Heaven
Our Roundables on the deadly failures of the virtual border wall is now available on demand
On Monday, MIT Technology Review hosted an exclusive Roundtables conversation about our investigation into the deadly failures of the US’s “virtual wall” of border surveillance towers.
Editor-in-chief Mat Honan, senior AI reporter James O’Donnell, and senior reporter for features and investigations Eileen Guo discussed what the investigation reveals about border surveillance technology and the people who have died in the borderlands.
The full event is now available to watch on demand. Subscribe to MIT Technology Review for exclusive access to the discussion and all our other Roundtables.
MIT Technology Review Narrated: smart glasses are already causing havoc in India
When Shubnam saw an Instagram video of a Delhi protest they had attended, they realized a content creator wearing Meta smart glasses had recorded them surreptitiously. The mocking reel drew millions of views, along with transphobic abuse and AI-generated memes.
Experts warn that many others will experience similar ordeals as smart glasses go mainstream. The risks are particularly acute in India, where covert recording and the circulation of images without consent are already pervasive.
The bigger issue is that the smart glasses aren’t just being used to turn ordinary people into targets of viral “pranks.” They’re also becoming a tool of police surveillance.
This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

The FBI is warning other members to turn themselves in. (NBC News)
+ Here’s what to know about the hackers and the breach. (NYT $)

The industry says permitting delays could lead to a collapse by 2028. (Axios)

The strategy saved the company nearly $4 billion last year. (NYT $)

The always-on agents can continuously perform tasks for users. (BBC)

Quote of the day
“The word super is the best word of all.”
—Donald Trump explains why federal agencies must now call AI "Super Intelligence,” The Verge reports.
One more thing
You have no choice in reading this article—maybe
  How do humans make decisions? The question has been on Uri Maoz’s mind since he read an article in his early twenties suggesting that… maybe they didn’t.
Had he even had a choice about whether to read that article in the first place? How would he ever know if he was truly responsible for making any decisions? “After that, there was no turning back,” says Maoz, now a professor of computational neuroscience at Chapman University.
Today, Maoz is a central figure in efforts to understand how desires and beliefs turn into actions. He’s also uncovered new wrinkles in the debate. Here’s what he’s discovered.

articles.title: Using Device Linking to Eavesdrop on WhatsApp and Signal - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
Using Device Linking to Eavesdrop on WhatsApp and Signal
Modern messaging apps allow users to link their phone accounts to their computer desktop. Eavesdroppers are taking advantage of this capability:
Apps such as WhatsApp Web and Signal Desktop allow people to use their accounts on other devices, such as laptops or desktop computers.
Germany’s Customs Office has been using these features to connect a police-controlled computer to a suspect’s account.
Once connected, messages can be delivered to that computer without the police having to crack the encryption protecting them.
Netzpoltik details that police are able to gain access in this way either through physical access to someone’s phone or by intercepting verification codes via a state-sanctioned phishing attack or intercepting SMS messages via telephone surveillance.
That last paragraph is important. Making this work requires user consent.
What we want is a feature that displays connected devices, so users could notice if a new device gets connected to their account.
Billy Jack • September 29, 2026 7:50 AM
I know some people who are going to hate learning that Signal is not the ultimate in security.

articles.title: OpenAI's latest features take direct aim at the app store model | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The focus of OpenAI’s Dev Day on Tuesday may have been on its agentic assistants known as Dots, or its new AI models, but combined, the AI company’s announcements pointed towards a bigger plan: a disruption of the traditional app store model. Taken together, today’s announcements turn ChatGPT itself into the place where software can be discovered, launched, and used by people and agents alike.
In addition, OpenAI introduced a way for people to bring their ChatGPT identity with them, while also allowing them to use their existing AI allowance in third-party apps.
This isn’t the first time OpenAI has experimented with how apps could operate within its familiar chatbot interface, but the current vision feels more fleshed out than before.
For starters, the company is turning ChatGPT itself into a surface for launching apps. The chatbot, which the company says now has 1.2 billion weekly users, has yet to fully capitalize on its potential as a discovery mechanism for finding and using apps that work with AI.
To change that, ChatGPT will begin to make app suggestions within the flow of conversation when it recognizes that a particular app could help the user complete their task. From there, the user will be able to connect the app and begin using it directly within ChatGPT.
This is also aided by the expansion of ChatGPT’s plugin architecture, which now supports extensions.
This allows app developers to build interactive panels where users can work with their tools while they’re chatting with ChatGPT. This essentially turns the apps and services that users would have previously used via the web or through a native desktop or mobile app into something that’s operated directly within ChatGPT.
Developers that sign on with the system can build AI-native versions of their apps through ChatGPT, the same way they would through the open web or a mobile app store. As more and more discovery happens through AI chat, it’s a distribution channel that’s hard to pass up.
Users get an incentive to use that channel too, because “Sign in with ChatGPT” will let them bring their AI allowance with them. (OpenAI has 16 launch partners on this effort, including Cognition’s Devin, Notion, Vercel, T3, OpenClaw, and Dactyl, but plans to add more soon, it says.)
In a demo at OpenAI’s Dev Day event, the company showed off how its own new meeting app could work inside ChatGPT, showing upcoming meetings from the user’s calendar. Here, the user could easily choose to use AI to take meeting notes, then receive a summary of follow-up items when the meeting wrapped.
In another example, users would work with design-focused apps like those from Figma and Adobe to work on revisions of their current project or use a particular feature that would have otherwise required a standalone app.
The apps can be shared with others, like work colleagues, in the lightweight websites ChatGPT now produces. From these ChatGPT sites, a user’s coworkers could sign in to the app with their own credentials and permissions, making the software experience personalized to them.
OpenAI also talked about improvements to how developers submit plugins for review — OpenAI’s version of Apple’s App Review process, if you will. Now, developers will be able to track their review, see what needs to be fixed, request a human review, and update their plugin’s tools without starting their whole submission over.
The company also announced a new enterprise app marketplace where partners can market their services. At launch, there are some 30-plus partners offering their app through the OpenAI Marketplace, including Adobe, Figma, Sierra, Decagon, HubSpot, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Harvey, Legora, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, Baseten, and others. Eligible customers can apply part of their OpenAI commitment toward approved partner software, OpenAI said.
Beyond turning ChatGPT into an app discovery tool where users connect with apps directly, OpenAI’s embrace of agents is gently pushing users into a new era where they don’t have to think as much about which app to use or why, relying instead on their AI agents’ suggestions.
With the launch of its autonomous AI agents known as Dots, agents will navigate the web for you, executing the tasks that need to be done in their own cloud infrastructure. Each Dot has its own cloud computer and browser, and can also use connected apps. Compare this to the old model, where users who wanted to manage some type of project — like building a website or coordinating a meeting calendar — would have to download different apps to their computer or phone to make that happen.
Now, users will instead tell an AI agent what they want to have done, and it will simply do it for them. In some cases, the agent’s work may require access to another AI model or a particular application. But this is something the agent may bring to the user, rather than the other way around — where the user is the one to go out and seek the particular tool for the job.
As OpenAI explains, the Dots will be able to connect to its ecosystem of now over 4,000 apps.
What’s more, the Dots can be proactive, perhaps jumping in to offer help with a project or bug, or handling a task the user forgot — but all done with the user’s approval. The Dots will perform what OpenAI calls “proactive research” in the background using connected apps in a read-only mode, but users would still have control over the actions they take.
This system could give app makers another way to reach customers outside of Apple and Google’s app stores. For instance, users could subscribe to a service through the app maker’s website, then connect that account to ChatGPT or Codex for their agent to use. OpenAI has not said, however, that these features would eliminate the need for separate third-party subscriptions or other charges.
Notably, OpenAI didn’t tease any plans on this front today, instead focusing on how it’s building the discovery, distribution, and interface pieces to counter the app store model, along with an identity layer and a mechanism for sharing a user’s existing ChatGPT AI allowance. It did not announce plans Tuesday for a billing or revenue-sharing system that’s comparable to the economic layer of traditional app stores.

articles.title: The Ace Ultra are what Sonos headphones Sonos should be
articles.text:
The original Sonos Ace headphones should have been a triumphant entry into a new product category. Instead, they were overshadowed by Sonos’s disastrous app redesign. And while the original Ace are well built, sound good, and are incredibly comfortable, they weren’t good Sonos headphones: Their flagship feature let you reroute audio from a Sonos soundbar to the Ace headphones so you could listen to your TV audio without disturbing anyone. But it was glitchy, and at launch it only worked with the $1,000 Arc soundbar, and only with one pair of Ace headphones at a time (Both of those have now been fixed). It also couldn’t connect to the rest of the Sonos system for music streaming.
The Sonos Ace Ultra are the headphones Sonos should have made the first time
With better sound, better ANC, and Wi-Fi audio streaming, the Ace Ultra are finally worthy of the Sonos name.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
Now the Ace Ultra are here, at the same $449 release price as the Ace (which are now $349). They’ve improved on what the Ace did well, while finally adding the ability to pass audio from your Sonos system to the headphones and back (although it’s in “early access”). They’re what the Ace should have been the first time.
The Good
- Can be used with Wi-Fi in a Sonos home system
- Improved sound profile and ANC performance
- Incredibly comfortable
The Bad
- Headphones can’t be grouped with Sonos speakers
- Sound and ANC still aren’t quite as good as competitors
- Wi-Fi audio during early access is lossy
The Sonos Ace Ultra have the same clean, understated look of the original, which I appreciate. They’re incredibly comfortable for hours on end, even while I’m wearing my glasses, and though they’re ever so slightly heavier than the Ace — 0.69 pounds to 0.71 pounds with the Ace Ultra — that weight was never a problem. The ear cups are squishy and spacious, and like the Ace’s ear cups, they’re also magnetic and easily removable; Sonos sells extras for $39 a pair. The battery is also user replaceable (a kit costs $25), although a statement on the battery kit listing does warn that “swapping out the battery requires disassembly and tools, plus some time and patience.”
The headphones also keep the tactile buttons and Content Key volume slider of the Ace instead of using capacitive buttons like the Sony XM series or Bose QuietComfort Ultra. I loved this setup and I’m glad Sonos kept the real buttons on the Ace Ultra. The Content Key reacts quickly and is easy to find while wearing the headphones. And its button functionality allows you to access the Sonos-specific features of TV audio swap and headphone linking.
While the original Ace came with TV audio swap, that was the extent of their Sonos system integration. The Ace Ultra have rectified that, albeit with a caveat, by adding headphone linking. The headphones now show up in your system list, and with a press of the slider button, you can move your music from any Sonos speaker or speaker group — not just TV audio from the soundbar — to the headphones and vice versa. That includes audio coming into the Sonos system from a record player or CD player or anywhere else. Both TV audio swap and headphone linking use a Wi-Fi connection.
It’s not flawless; sometimes I’d have to press the button a couple times to get the transfer to happen. If you pull the audio from your speakers to the headphones and decide to send it back later, it only goes to the closest speaker in your system, not whichever speaker or group was playing before. Adding it back to a speaker group has to be done in the Sonos app. The headphones also cannot be grouped with any speakers. I suppose the thinking is, if you’re listening to music on your headphones you don’t need it also playing from your speakers. One nice touch is that if you have different music playing on different speakers, pulling the music to the headphones from one doesn’t affect the rest of them. Headphone linking is in early access, according to Sonos, so it’s possible the experience will change.
As Sonos’ own Wi-Fi vs. Bluetooth explainer points out, one of the main benefits of Wi-Fi audio streaming is that the higher bandwidth allows for hi-res and lossless audio. But right now, the Ace Ultra don’t take advantage of that. During the headphone linking early access period, audio over Wi-Fi with headphone linking is lossy. (Sonos has not said how long the early access period will last). Senior director of product management Andrew Sutherland told The Verge via email, “our focus right now is making sure the core experience is genuinely solid and reliable for listeners by using a high-quality, lossy-compressed stereo audio stream optimized for listening over WiFi. We’ve been really happy with the results. We’ll continue to build out its capabilities from there.” I appreciate the cautiousness in making sure headphone linking works properly, but it’s disappointing that Sonos shipped a product with one of its flagship features still in beta.
At the moment, the Ace Ultra only support lossless audio over Bluetooth with aptX Lossless and a compatible device, or over USB-C. The wired USB-C or 3.5mm connection maxes out at 16-bit/48kHz, though, so there’s no high-res audio. There will surely be lots of debate on the forums about the tragic lack of high-res support, but the reality is most people won’t be missing anything.
Newly designed 40mm drivers sound better than those on the original Ace, and an adaptive EQ makes real-time adjustments based on fit and any obstructions — such as glasses’ temples or earrings. The bass is richer without overpowering vocals, which is most evident in songs with a thumping low end, like Billie Eilish’s “Bad Guy” (one of my go-to bass tests). The kick drum through the verse and chorus has weight and drives the energy forward while the rhythmic bass line supports the voice. There’s also good stereo separation on “Killer Queen” by Queen with lead guitars to the left and right of the soundstage.
I do wish the Ace Ultra had better midrange clarity, especially on busier tracks like Radiohead’s “The National Anthem” and its cacophonous middle section. The 8-band EQ Sonos added to the Ace Ultra (sorry original Ace owners, this isn’t for you) helps this a bit when I boosted the mids at 460Hz and 1kHz a little. While in there, I also added more high frequencies to open up the sound. With the tweaks, I got the Ace Ultra to a place where I enjoyed my listening across genres. It’s a good step forward from the original Ace, although I still prefer the Sony XM6’s default sound profile.
The Ace Ultra’s active noise cancellation (ANC) is better than the Ace’s and now includes an adaptive version. It’s still not as strong as the ANC on the Sony XM6, Bose Ultra Headphones, or Apple AirPods Max 2 — it lets in more midrange and a few higher frequencies, as well — so if you’re mainly using them to block out ambient noise, those three options are better choices. But if you’re using ANC paired with music playing, the Ace Ultra perform well.
Call quality is also better. When I was on a video call while my wife was having a phone conversation 20 feet behind me in the kitchen, the Ace Ultra kept her voice and other ambient noise quieted. They had a bit more trouble keeping out the noise when I went outside to a busy street — the Sony XM6 are much better at this — but I still sounded clear and easy to understand.
Sonos has upped the battery life, from up to 30 hours on the Ace to up to 35 hours with the Ace Ultra. They come with the same felt-covered case with a magnetic removable pouch that stores the USB-C to USB-C and USB-C to 3.5mm cables.
Sonos has taken a great first shot at headphones and followed up with an even better pair. They have improved sound, better ANC, and Sonos-specific features. And they’re one of the most comfortable pairs of headphones I’ve worn in a while.
But to get the most out of the Ace Ultra, you need to be an existing Sonos user, or be ready to spend hundreds more dollars. The cheapest Sonos soundbar that works with TV audio swap, the Ray, is still $219. And headphone linking is only useful if you have Sonos speakers.
If you do have a Sonos soundbar and speakers and you’re looking for headphones, the Ace Ultra are an easy recommendation, especially over the original Ace — even though those are down to $350. If you’re not in the Sonos world, though, the Sony WH-1000XM6 (or even the older XM5) with their better ANC and sound quality for less money, are a better bet.
Photography by John Higgins / The Verge

                                                                Designing Physical AI Systems Under Real-World Constraints                                                    
                        Auto, Security and AI
                        
       			
					
WHITEPAPERS
		
Where latency, power, reliability, and data movement shape system behavior.
								September 30th, 2026 - 
								By: Cadence
								
							
						
Physical AI extends artificial intelligence into systems that sense, interpret, and act in the physical world. Unlike centralized AI infrastructure, these systems operate within bounded latency, power, thermal, reliability, and environmental constraints. They must respond to changing inputs in real time, often under conditions where delayed or inconsistent behavior can affect equipment, processes, or human safety.
While Physical AI often operates at the edge, it extends beyond edge AI by combining AI inference with closed-loop interaction in the physical world, where sensing, decision-making, and actuation operate together under strict timing and operational constraints.
At the center of Physical AI is a continuous sensing, inference, and response cycle. Sensor data is captured, processed, interpreted, and translated into action. Maintaining that cycle requires predictable behavior across memory, compute, communication, and I/O resources. Delays in data arrival, variability in memory access, inefficient communication, or synchronization overhead can directly affect how the system responds.
Physical AI systems must move, process, and act on data within strict timing and operational constraints. Memory, communication, synchronization, and I/O are all part of the control path.
Edge AI plays a central role in this architecture because many Physical AI systems cannot rely on centralized infrastructure for immediate decisions. Sensor data may be too large, too frequent, too latency-sensitive, or too safety-critical to send to a remote system before action is taken. Local execution becomes necessary, but edge environments introduce additional constraints, including limited power budgets, thermal variation, vibration, motion, shock, humidity, and other physical operating conditions.
These infrastructure constraints are implemented through silicon-level decisions. Memory interfaces, interconnect, I/O subsystems, and die-to-die links carry, exchange, and synchronize data across the system.
Physical AI systems also rarely operate in isolation. Devices often participate in larger architectures spanning edge, industrial, vehicle, and cloud environments, where information must be exchanged and coordinated across multiple system boundaries. The same data movement, synchronization, and infrastructure challenges extend beyond a single device and shape behavior across the broader system.

articles.title: Nach KI-Hackerangriffen: Trump setzt auf Selbstverpflichtung statt Regulierung
articles.text:
Nach KI-Hackerangriffen: Trump setzt auf Selbstverpflichtung statt Regulierung
US-Präsident Donald Trump will trotz Warnungen vor existenziellen Risiken Künstlicher Intelligenz die Aufsicht über die Technologie ihren Entwicklern selbst überlassen. Die Unternehmen würden sich selber kontrollieren, sagte Trump nach einem Treffen mit Chefs von KI-Unternehmen in Washington. Er sieht ausreichenden Schutz durch wirtschaftliche Interessen der US-Firmen. „Ihre Unternehmen stehen auf dem Spiel, wenn etwas schiefgeht“, sagte der Präsident. „Sie werden das nicht zulassen.“ Die Unternehmen würden „sich gegenseitig kontrollieren“.
Zuletzt hatten eigenständige Hacking-Attacken durch KI-Modelle die Sorgen um Gefahren Künstlicher Intelligenz hochkochen lassen. Einige Branchenvertreter selbst warnten, man könne nicht ganz ausschließen, dass KI in der Zukunft die Menschheit auslösche.
Anthropic-Chef: „Sehr reale Risiken“
Der Chef der KI-Firma Anthropic, Dario Amodei, hatte sich dafür ausgesprochen, die Entwicklung der leistungsfähigsten KI-Modelle abzubremsen, um sicherzugehen, dass man nicht die Kontrolle über die Technologie verliert. Trump hatte bereits zuvor eine verstärkte staatliche Regulierung der Technologie abgelehnt. Es sei wichtig, dass die USA den Vorsprung zu China nicht einbüßten, betont er.
Amodei sagte nach dem Treffen mit Trump, KI habe großes Potenzial – „aber auch sehr reale Risiken“. Maßnahmen, um diesen Risiken entgegenzuwirken, seien „noch in der Diskussion“.
Freiwillige Selbstverpflichtung für KI-Firmen
Jetzt wurde bei dem Treffen in einer Selbstverpflichtung eine Reihe von Grundsätzen vereinbart, zu denen „robuste interne Kontrollen“ gehören, wie aus dem von Trump veröffentlichten Dokument hervorgeht. Dies solle unter anderem Biowaffen- und Chemiewaffen-Risiken ausräumen – und auch dafür sorgen, dass es keine Hacking-Attacken gebe.
Darüber hinaus erklärten sich die Unternehmen bereit, externe Beobachter zuzulassen. Das entspricht einer Idee, die Amodei vor einigen Wochen vorstellte, und die unter anderem von seinem Konkurrenten Sam Altman beim ChatGPT-Entwickler OpenAI sowie Tech-Milliardär Elon Musk unterstützt wurde. Die Verwaltungsräte der KI-Firmen – die in etwa den deutschen Aufsichtsräten entsprechen – sollen zudem gesonderte unabhängige Gremien einrichten, die interne und externe Berichte prüfen.
„Mit der Zeit könnte es Sinn ergeben, diese Schritte in Gesetzen oder Regeln festzuhalten“, hieß es in dem Dokument auch. Das Papier wurde unter anderem von Amodei, Musk, Facebook-Gründer Mark Zuckerberg, Google-Chef Sundar Pichai sowie dem Chef des KI-Chip-Spezialisten Nvidia, Jensen Huang, unterzeichnet.
OpenAI setzt auf KI-Agenten
Für OpenAI unterzeichnete das Papier Altmans rechte Hand, der Top-Manager Greg Brockman. Der Firmenchef konnte nicht zu dem recht kurzfristig angesetzten Treffen nach Washington kommen, weil er auf der jährlichen Entwicklerkonferenz von OpenAI in San Francisco auftrat. Er stellte dort unter dem Namen Dots (Punkte) sogenannte KI-Agenten vor, die eigenständig Aufgaben im Auftrag der Nutzer erfüllen können. Ein Dot könne am Computer praktisch alles machen, „was man sich einfallen lassen kann“. Nach dem Start in den USA sollen Dots „bald“ auch in Europa verfügbar sein, hieß es.
Zunächst bekommt man nur einen Dot pro Nutzer – aber mit der Zeit solle eine Vielzahl solcher Agenten für die Nutzer im Einsatz sein. Kommuniziert mit der Software wird über einen Chat. Für einzelne Wissensbereiche in Unternehmen – etwa Buchhaltung, Marketing oder Rechtsfragen – soll es spezialisierte Dots geben. Zunächst sind Dot-Assistenten nur hinter Abo-Schranken nutzbar, was ihre Verbreitung zunächst vor allem auf den Berufsalltag beschränken dürfte. „Aber sie sollten davon ausgehen, dass wir eines Tages etwas im Massenmarkt für Milliarden Menschen machen.“
Meta will mit KI für Verbraucher punkten
Meta hatte erst vor wenigen Wochen einen ähnlich funktionierenden KI-Assistenten mit dem Namen Muse zunächst in den USA gestartet, der auf Verbraucher ausgerichtet ist. Die Muse-App erklomm danach die Spitzenposition im US-App-Store von Apple, und Meta wurde an der Wall Street nach Milliarden-Investitionen in KI-Infrastruktur wieder als ein aussichtsreicher Anwärter im Wettbewerb um eine führende Rolle bei Künstlicher Intelligenz gesehen. ChatGPT hatte den Hype um Künstliche Intelligenz erst ausgelöst, bei dem neuesten KI-Assistenten für Verbraucher kam Meta dem Vorreiter aber zuvor. Altman sagte indes, Dots sei „allem, was heute auf dem Markt verfügbar ist, weit voraus“.
Im Prinzip könnten auch Verbraucher Dots schon jetzt für Alltagsdinge benutzen, sagte OpenAI-Manager Alexander Embiricos der Deutschen Presse-Agentur. Aber damit würden sie nicht die wirklichen Vorteile der Software nutzen, schränkte er ein. Dots sei eher für ambitionierte Aufgaben optimiert, um mehr zu machen, als man sich selbst zugetraut hat.

articles.title: SA’s Platybooks launches to help small businesses get paid in one step - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African startup Platybooks has launched an invoicing, quoting and light CRM platform that turns an accepted quote into an invoice with a built-in card payment link, settling funds directly into a small business’s own bank account.
Founded by Ché Overmeyer, Platybooks began life in 2023 as Invoiceer, before being shelved for around two years. Overmeyer revived the project in 2026, finished it and rebranded it as Platybooks.
A former photographer and tour operator, Overmeyer said the business admin was always the hardest part.
“In both of those the part I found hardest was keeping track of all my invoices and payments, spread across Excel spreadsheets, InvoiceTemplate.docx and the statements from the banking app,” he told Disrupt Africa. “I’m in my seventh professional year as a senior developer now, so I built the thing I kept wishing existed.”
With Platybooks, once a client accepts a quote, the invoice is created automatically. It is sent as a PDF carrying the fields required on a South African tax invoice, along with a card payment link. Payments go through Paystack into the business’s account, the invoice marks itself as paid, and automated reminders go out if it isn’t.
The platform also offers client management, a product catalogue, credit notes, recurring invoices, deposits, team roles and custom branding.
Overmeyer said the gap in the market is not a lack of invoicing software, but the fact that invoicing and payment remain separate.
“Xero, Zoho and QuickBooks all make you attach a gateway afterwards. Platybooks issues the invoice and the card payment link as one thing,” he said. “Xero and QuickBooks are good products. They’re just built for accountants, and priced and localised for somewhere else.”
Though Platybooks makes money through subscriptions, its four tiers are more locally-priced. The startup is bootstrapped, with the product currently being used by testers. Overmeyer said the company is now ready for a first funding round, aimed at distribution rather than product development.
“I have a complete product and no audience, and that’s the gap capital actually closes,” he said.
Platybooks is focused on South Africa for now, but Overmeyer sees a cheap route to expansion, as Paystack already operates in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and Uganda.
“South Africa proves the model; the second move is a repeat, not a pivot,” he said.

articles.title: Hackers exploit Citrix NetScaler zero-day to deploy web shells
articles.text:
Cybersecurity firms say attackers exploited the Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88772 zero-day to deploy custom web shells and tunneling malware, gain root access, steal credentials, and spread into internal networks.
Mandiant says the attacks began in at least early September and are believed to have impacted organizations in North America and Europe across the government, financial services, education, legal, and professional services sectors.
The campaign first came to light over the weekend, when Citrix administrators began reporting that IT suppliers, security teams, CERTs, and national cybersecurity agencies privately warned organizations about two unpatched NetScaler zero-days and, in some cases, advised them to shut down affected appliances.
Cybersecurity firm watchTowr later said it had verified reports that two NetScaler remote code execution zero-days were being exploited in the wild and that Citrix was preparing patches.
Citrix ultimately disclosed the flaws on Sunday as CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, with some researchers dubbing the vulnerabilities "PitScaler."
Citrix confirmed that both had been exploited on unmitigated NetScaler deployments and releasing security updates to address them.
CVE-2026-88771 is an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw affecting all NetScaler ADC and Gateway deployments, while CVE-2026-88772 is a memory overflow vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution or denial of service when DTLS is enabled.
Exploited in zero-day attacks
GreyNoise observed a threat actor attempting to exploit a Citrix NetScaler Gateway on September 24, three days before Citrix publicly disclosed CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772.
According to GreyNoise, the attack originated from 149.104.78.141, and its platform detected it before CVE detections were available.
GreyNoise says the attacker attempted to modify /bin/sh to give a root shell and install a password-protected PHP web shell at /var/netscaler/logon/LogonPoint/custom/.ctxs.receiver.
The attacker also attempted to modify /etc/httpd.conf so requests for what appeared to be CSS files, including receiver.min.css, would instead open the hidden PHP web shell.
The company is not publishing the full exploit for now, but recommends defenders hunt for the .ctxs.receiver file, related Alias or AliasMatch entries in httpd.conf, changes to the permissions of /bin/sh, and connections from the observed source IP.
A new Mandiant report provides more details about how CVE-2026-88772 is being exploited, confirming some of the same attack patterns seen by GreyNoise.
Mandiant says the exploits bypass authentication and cause the NetScaler Packet Processing Engine (NSPPE) to terminate unexpectedly, giving attackers root-level access.
"While Google Threat Intelligence Group does not possess exploit code, analysis of frontline telemetry suggests that transmitting specially malformed or fragmented record headers induces heap memory boundary corruption within the packet engine, diverting control flow to execute arbitrary shellcode with root-level operating system privileges on the underlying FreeBSD platform," explains Mandiant.
Google observed similar post-exploitation activity in intrusions, including attackers installing PHP web shells and modified the NetScaler web server configuration so non-executable file extensions would process them as PHP.
In one intrusion, Mandiant says the attackers modified /etc/httpd.conf so that .deb files would execute as PHP, allowing web shells to be used from directories normally holding NetScaler client software.
In other attacks, the threat actor used .sig files and modified the web server configuration so requests for .ico images under /vpn/media/ were instead mapped to malicious PHP files.
Google says this allowed malicious web shell requests to appear as requests for image files or CSS while executing attacker commands via the shell_exec() or eval() PHP functions.
Some of the web shells returned fake HTTP 404 responses when executing commands, further disguising the malicious activity.
Mandiant says the threat actors deployed two previously undocumented malware families, tracked as WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT.
WHIPSHOT is a PHP web shell disguised as a Debian package and stored in the NetScaler VPN scripts directory.
The malware acts as an HTTP proxy for SLAPSHOT, extracting Base64-encoded data from HTTP request headers and forwarding it to the tunneling malware running on a compromised device.
WHIPSHOT also checks whether SLAPSHOT is running and can extract and launch the embedded Python payloads in the background.
SLAPSHOT is a Python-based TCP tunneling tool that bridges the compromised NetScaler appliance and internal devices, allowing attackers to spread further into the network.
The malware accepts commands from WHIPSHOT and can open connections to internal hosts, send and receive data over those connections, and close sessions when finished.
Google says attackers used the proxy in at least one observed intrusion to manually conduct reconnaissance and steal credentials.
Mandiant says the malware can also terminate itself after periods of inactivity, making it harder to detect.
Although exploitation initially grants root privileges, commands executed by the web shells would normally run under a lower-privileged account that the NetScaler web servers run under.
To maintain root access, Google says the attackers modified permissions on /bin/sh so commands would run with elevated privileges.
"To establish persistent root-level execution for its web shells, the threat actor leveraged its lightweight installer web shells to assert the setuid (Set User ID) bit on the /bin/sh executable," Mandiant says.
The threat actor also rebooted NetScaler appliances or restarted the web server to apply configuration changes.
NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances are attractive targets because they are exposed to the Internet and often sit at the edge of internal networks, without having the same benefit of EDR software.
Mandiant says defenders should prioritize installing the latest Citrix security updates and inspect NetScaler appliances for signs of compromise.
Potential indicators include unauthorized PHP handlers or aliases in httpd.conf, suspicious .deb or .sig files containing PHP code, unusual HTTP 404 responses, unexpected NSPPE crashes, and the presence of /tmp/.uxdport or /tmp/.uxdlock files associated with SLAPSHOT.
Organizations should also check whether /bin/sh has been modified to run with setuid root permissions and look for suspicious Python processes launched with nohup or containing Base64-encoded payloads.
While Mandiant links this activity to CVE-2026-88772, Citrix says CVE-2026-88771 has also been exploited in attacks.
For organizations that cannot immediately patch, Mandiant recommends disabling DTLS where operationally feasible and blocking inbound UDP/443 upstream when DTLS is not required.
However, Google warns that these mitigations apply only to CVE-2026-88772 and do not protect against the separately exploited CVE-2026-88771 vulnerability.
Mandiant says installing the latest NetScaler security updates is the only way to address both flaws.

articles.title: Restrictions on social media for under-18? SC asks Centre to examine statutory safeguards for minors
articles.text:
Restrictions on social media for under-18? SC asks Centre to examine statutory safeguards for minors
The Supreme Court has asked the Centre to examine statutory safeguards for minors on social media, with the government indicating that intermediary rules may be amended.
India is moving towards a possible statutory restriction on minors opening social media accounts, after the Supreme Court questioned how children under 18 can independently enter into agreements with digital platforms. The Centre has indicated that it will act, but no new rule imposing such a restriction has been formally notified yet.
According to The Times of India, the Centre told the Supreme Court on September 28 that it would soon insert a provision in the Information Technology intermediary rules to prevent social media intermediaries from allowing under-18s to open accounts.
PTI, however, reported the government’s position more cautiously as an undertaking to examine the issue and take appropriate steps.
The case concerns a petition by the Just Rights for Children Alliance seeking stronger safeguards for minors on social media and other digital platforms. According to PTI, the Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked the Centre to examine whether such safeguards could be given statutory backing. The petition argues that children below 18 lack contractual capacity under Indian law.
Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 says a person is competent to contract only if they have reached the age of majority and satisfy the other legal requirements. According to the PTI report, the petitioner argued that platforms allowing minors to independently accept their terms of service were therefore entering into agreements with people who lack contractual capacity.
Justice Bagchi also pressed the government on whether platforms' technology should be brought into line with Indian law. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta signalled that the Centre would consider the matter.
The Economic Times and TOI also reported that Mehta indicated educational websites could potentially allow minors to participate with parental consent.
The petition is seeking more than a simple age threshold. According to PTI, it asks the Centre to amend the IT Intermediary Rules, 2021, or issue specific directions so that digital platforms do not enter into contracts with children under 18 without parental or lawful-guardian consent, subject to identity verification or e-KYC. It also refers to Section 79 of the IT Act, which provides conditional safe-harbour protection to intermediaries that meet specified requirements.
The issue also overlaps with India’s data protection regime. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 provides special protections for children, including verifiable parental consent for specified processing of children's personal data. Under the government's November 13, 2025 commencement notification, Sections 3 to 10 of the Act are scheduled to take effect 18 months after that date, in May 2027.
The technology industry has meanwhile been introducing its own safeguards. Meta launched Instagram Teen Accounts in India in February 2025, with private-by-default settings, stricter messaging controls and parental supervision tools. YouTube has also been expanding machine-learning age estimation in some markets to identify likely under-18 users and apply additional protections.

articles.title: Après neuf ans d'attente, la Tesla Roadster reportée à cause de... la pluie
articles.text:
Le grand retour du Tesla Roadster ne sera pas pour tout de suite. Le constructeur automobile a repoussé au 15 octobre la présentation de son bolide, initialement calée au 1er octobre. En cause, un orage attendu au Texas, sur le site d’essais de SpaceX à McGregor, où doit se tenir l’événement. Après un prototype dévoilé en 2017 et une production alors promise pour 2020, ce contretemps météo s’ajoute à une très longue liste de retards.
Une démonstration qui ne peut pas se tenir en intérieur
« Nous avons suivi de près la météo avec des météorologues locaux, mais compte tenu des conditions sévères prévues et parce que cet événement ne peut se tenir qu’en extérieur, nous avons pris la difficile décision de le reporter », a annoncé Tesla sur X le 28 septembre. Un rapide coup d’œil sur les prévisions confirme qu’elles ne sont guère encourageantes, avec un grand risque de précipitations le 1er octobre et même de possibles orages violents.
Le lieu explique la contrainte. Contrairement à un lancement automobile classique, qu’on peut rapatrier sous un hangar en cas de pluie, Tesla compte faire évoluer la Roadster équipée de propulseurs à gaz froid développés par SpaceX, un dispositif optionnel appelé « SpaceX Package » qui promet un 0 à 100 km/h en moins d’une seconde et une brève démonstration de sustentation à quelques centimètres du sol. L’engin serait piloté à distance, sans personne à bord, et le public maintenu à plusieurs centaines de mètres pour des raisons de sécurité. Le site de McGregor, habituellement utilisé pour tester des moteurs-fusées, se prête à cet usage, un hangar non.
Neuf ans de promesses non tenues
Le prototype a été présenté en novembre 2017, avec une production alors annoncée pour 2020. Le calendrier a depuis glissé à de nombreuses reprises : une démonstration promise fin 2025, puis reportée au 1er avril 2026, ensuite à un vague « d’ici un mois » au printemps, avant de glisser à août puis à octobre. La production en série n’est désormais plus évoquée qu’à l’horizon 2027, voire 2028.
Les premiers clients ont versé des acomptes de 50 000 dollars, ou jusqu’à 250 000 dollars pour l’édition Founders Series, dès l’annonce en 2017. Sam Altman, le patron d’OpenAI, avait fini par réclamer son remboursement, jugeant que sept ans et demi d’attente commençaient à faire long. En France, les réservations ont rouvert il y a quelques jours, avec un acompte remboursable de 43 000 euros. Le prix définitif reste inconnu.
Une variante réservée à la piste
La version équipée du « SpaceX Package » ne sera pas homologuée pour la route et restera réservée à un usage sur circuit. Le Roadster de série, lui, est annoncé avec 1 000 km d’autonomie, plus de 400 km/h en pointe et un 0 à 100 km/h en 2,1 secondes, pour un tarif encore inconnu. Rendez-vous le 15 octobre pour savoir si le rendez-vous a bien lieu cette fois.
